places.name: 아바나 (다메섹의 강)
places.desc: 나아만 장군이 자랑한 다메섹의 맑고 푸른 생명수 강
places.eastonKo: "돌이 많은"(마르그. "아마나," 늘 흐르는), 다메섹의 주요 강(왕하 5:12). 현대 이름은 바라다이며, 헬라인들은 크리소로아스("황금 시내")라 불렀다. 다메섹 북서쪽 약 …
places.smithKo: '끊임없이 흐르는, 돌이 많은'이라는 뜻으로 다마스쿠스의 '강들' 중 하나이다(열왕기하 5:12). 오늘날의 바라다강이 아바나에 해당하는 것으로 추정된다.
places.eastonEn: stony (Hebrews marg. “Amanah,” perennial), the chief river of Damascus (2 Kings 5:12). Its modern name is Barada, the Chrysorrhoas, or “golden stream,” of the Greeks. It rises in a cleft of the Anti-Lebanon  range, about 23 miles north-west of Damascus, and after flowing southward for a little way parts into three smaller streams, the central one flowing through Damascus, and the other two on each side of the city, diffusing beauty and fertility where otherwise there would be barrenness.
places.smithEn: (perennial, stony), one of the “rivers of Damascus.” (2 Kings 5:12) The Barada and the Awaj are now the chief streams of Damascus, the former representing the Abana and the latter the Pharpar of the text. The Barada (Abana) rises in the Antilibanus, at about 23 miles from the city, after flowing through which it runs across the plain, of whose fertility it is the chief source, till it loses itself in the lake or marsh Bahret-elKibliyeh.

places.name: 아바림
places.eastonKo: "저편의 지역들," 곧 요단 동편, 여리고 맞은편, 사해의 동남쪽에 있는 산 혹은 산맥. "비스가 산 정상"(곧 느보산, 그 봉우리 중 하나)에서 모세는 약속의 땅을 바라보았고(신…
places.smithKo: '저편의 땅들'이라는 뜻으로 요단강 동쪽, 모압 땅의 산악 지대로 여리고 맞은편에 위치한다. 모세가 약속의 땅을 바라본 느보산, 곧 비스가산 정상이 이곳에서 가장 높은 지점이다(민…
places.eastonEn: regions beyond; i.e., on the east of Jordan, a mountain, or rather a mountain-chain, over against Jericho, to the east and south-east of the Dead Sea, in the land of Moab. From “the top of Pisgah”, i.e., Mount Nebo (q.v.), one of its summits, Moses surveyed the Promised Land (Deuteronomy 3:27; 32:49), and there he died (34:1,5). The Israelites had one of their encampments in the mountains of Abarim (Numbers 33:47,48) after crossing the Arnon.
places.smithEn: (regions beyond), a mountain or range of highlands on the east of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, facing Jericho, and forming the eastern wall of the Jordan valley at that part. Its most elevated spot was “the Mount Nebo, head of the Pisgah,” from which Moses viewed the Promised Land before his death. These mountains are mentioned in (Numbers 27:12; 33:47,48) and Deuteronomy 32:49

places.name: 압돈 (아셀 지파 레위 성읍)
places.desc: 아셀 지파에 속한 게르손 자손의 레위 성읍
places.eastonKo: "종된 자"라는 뜻. (1) 비라돈 사람 힐렐의 아들로 이스라엘의 열째 사사다(삿 12:13-15). 아마 삼상 12:11의 베단일 것이다. (2) 베냐민 지파 기브온의 맏아들(대상 8:30; 9:36).
places.smithKo: '종의'라는 뜻. (1) 이스라엘의 사사로 사무엘상 12:11의 브단과 동일 인물로 추정된다(사사기 12:13). (2) 사삭의 아들(역대상 8:23). (3) 기브온의 아들 여히…
places.eastonEn: servile. (1.) The son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, the tenth judge of Israel (Judges 12:13-15). He is probably the Bedan of 1 Samuel 12:11. (2.) The first-born of Gibeon of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:30; 9:36). (3.) The son of Micah, one of those whom Josiah sent to the prophetess Huldah to ascertain from her the meaning of the recently discovered book of the law (2 Chronicles 34:20). He is called Achbor in 2 Kings 22:12. (4.) One of the “sons” of Shashak (1 Chronicles 8:23).  This is the name also of a Levitical town of the Gershonites, in the tribe of Asher (Joshua 21:30; 1 Chronicles 6:74). The ruins of Abdeh, some 8 miles north-east of Accho, probably mark its site.
places.smithEn: (servile). • A judge of Israel, (Judges 12:13,(15) perhaps the same person as Bedan, in (1 Samuel 12:11) (B.C. 1233-1225). • Son of Shashak. (1 Chronicles 8:23) • First-born son of Jehiel, son of Gideon. (1 Chronicles 8:30; 9:35,36). • Son of Micah, a contemporary of Josiah, (2 Chronicles 34:20) called Achbor in (2 Kings 22:12) (B.C. 628.) • A city in the tribe if Asher, given to the Gershonites, (Joshua 21:30; 1 Chronicles 6:74) the modern Abdeh, 10 miles northeast of Accho.

places.name: 벧아벨마아가 (지혜로운 여인)
places.modern: 텔 아벨 엘-캄흐 (Tel Abel Beth Maacah) (이스라엘 북부)
places.desc: 세바의 반역 때 지혜로운 여인이 성을 구한 곳, 앗수르 디글랏 빌레셀 3세에게 정복당한 북단 요충지
places.eastonKo: "마아가 집의 초장," 팔레스타인 북부, 단과 이욘 근처, 납달리 지파에 있는 성읍. 상당한 견고함과 중요성을 지닌 곳이었다. "이스라엘의 어미"라 불렸는데(삼하 20:19), 이는 곧 수도라는 뜻이다. 요압(삼하 20:14), 벤하닷(왕상 15:20), 디글랏빌레셀(왕하 15:29, 주전 734년경)에게 포위 공격을 받았다. 다른 곳에서는 "물들의 초장"이라는 뜻의 아벨마임이라 불린다(대하 16:4).
places.smithKo: '억압의 집의 초원'이라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 최북단의 중요한 성읍이며(사무엘하 20:15) 일찍부터 시리아와 아시리아 침략군의 표적이 되었다.
places.eastonEn: meadow of the house of Maachah, a city in the north of Palestine, in the neighbourhood of Dan and Ijon, in the tribe of Naphtali. It was a place of considerable strength and importance. It is called a “mother in Israel”, i.e., a metropolis (2 Samuel 20:19). It was besieged by Joab (2 Samuel 20:14), by Benhadad (1 Kings 15:20), and by Tiglath-pileser (2 Kings 15:29) about B.C. 734. It is elsewhere called Abel-maim, meadow of the waters, (2 Chronicles 16:4). Its site is occupied by the modern Abil or Abil-el-kamh, on a rising ground to the east of the brook Derdarah, which flows through the plain of Huleh into the Jordan, about 6 miles to the west-north-west of Daniel
places.smithEn: (meadow of the house of oppression), a town of some importance, (2 Samuel 20:15) in the extreme north of Palestine, which fell an early prey to the invading kings of Syria, (1 Kings 15:20) and Assyria. (2 Kings 15:29)

places.name: 아벨그라밈 (포도원의 아벨)
places.desc: 입다가 암몬 20성읍을 격파하며 진격한 포도원 골짜기 성읍
places.eastonKo: (삿 11:33, R.V.; A.V.에는 "포도원의 평지"), 암몬 사람들의 마을로 입다가 그들의 군대를 그곳까지 추격했다.
places.eastonEn: (Judges 11:33, R.V.; A. V., “plain of the vineyards”), a village of the Ammonites, whither Jephthah pursued their forces.

places.name: 아벨므홀라 (엘리사의 고향)
places.modern: 텔 아부 수스 (Tell Abu Sifri / Suse) (팔레스타인 서안)
places.desc: 미디안 군대가 도망한 곳, 훗날 엘리야가 소 12겨리로 밭 갈던 엘리사를 후계자로 부른 고향
places.eastonKo: "춤추는 초장"이라는 뜻으로 선지자 엘리사가 태어나 살던 곳이며 벧산에서 멀지 않은 잇사갈 지파 땅에 있다(왕상 4:12). 와디 엘 말레가 요단 계곡으로 흘러드는 부근, 벧산 남쪽 약 4마일에 걸친 기름진 초원 지대다.
places.smithKo: "춤추는 초장"이라는 뜻으로 요단 계곡 북부에 있다(왕상 4:12). 기드온에게 쫓긴 베두인 무리가 이곳으로 도망했다(삿 7:22). 엘리야가 호렙에서 계곡을 거슬러 올라오다가 밭 갈던 엘리사를 만난 곳이다(왕상 19:16-19).
places.eastonEn: meadow of dancing, or the dancing-meadow, the birth-place and residence of the prophet Elisha, not far from Beth-shean (1 Kings 4:12), in the tribe of Issachar, near where the Wady el-Maleh emerges into the valley of the Jordan, “the rich meadow-land which extends about 4 miles south of Beth-shean; moist and luxuriant.” Here Elisha was found at his plough by Elijah on his return up the Jordan valley from Horeb (1 Kings 19:16). It is now called ‘Ain Helweh.
places.smithEn: (meadow of the dance), in the northern pat of the Jordan valley, (1 Kings 4:12) to which the routed Bedouin host fled from Gideon, (Judges 7:22) Here Elisha was found at his plough by Elijah returning up the valley from Horeb. (1 Kings 19:16-19)

places.name: 아벨미스라임 (아닷의 타작마당)
places.modern: near the mouth of the Jordan River
places.desc: 야곱의 장례 행렬이 7일간 크게 애곡한 곳
places.eastonKo: "애굽의 초장" 또는 "애굽의 애곡"이라는 뜻으로 요단 "건너편" 곧 서편, "아닷의 타작마당"에 있던 곳이다. 애굽 사람들이 이곳에서 야곱을 위해 칠십 일을 애곡했다(창 50:4-11). 그 자리는 알려져 있지 않다.
places.smithKo: "애굽의 초장"이라는 뜻으로, 요셉과 그 형제들과 애굽 사람들이 야곱을 위해 애곡한 아닷의 타작마당에 가나안 사람들이 붙인 이름이다(창 50:11). 요단 건너편(동편)에 있었다.
places.eastonEn: meadow of Egypt, or mourning of Egypt, a place “beyond,” i.e., on the west of Jordan, at the “threshing-floor of Atad.” Here the Egyptians mourned seventy days for Jacob (Genesis 50:4-11). Its site is unknown.
places.smithEn: (meadow of Egypt), the name given by the Canaanites to the floor of Atad, at which Joseph, his brothers and the Egyptians made their mourning for Jacob. (Genesis 50:11) It was beyond (on the east of) Jordan. See Atad. (Schaff and others say it was on the west bank, for the writer was on the east of Jordan. It was near Jericho, or perhaps Hebron.)

places.name: 아벨싯딤 (모압 평지 싯딤)
places.desc: 이스라엘이 가나안 입경 전 마지막으로 진을 친 아카시아 들판
places.eastonKo: "아카시아 나무의 초장"이라는 뜻으로 흔히 그냥 "싯딤"이라 불린다(민 25:1; 수 2:1; 미 6:5). 요단 동편 모압 평지, 여리고 거의 맞은편에 있다. 이스라엘의 마흔두 번째 진영이며 요단을 건너기 전 마지막 쉼터였다(민 33:49; 22:1).
places.smithKo: "아카시아 나무의 초장"이라는 뜻으로 요단 계곡 낮은 지대, 여리고 맞은편 모압 "평지"에 있다. 이스라엘이 요단을 건너기 전 마지막으로 머문 곳이다(민 33:49). 대개 줄여서 싯딤이라는 이름으로 언급된다.
places.eastonEn: meadow of the acacias, frequently called simply “Shittim” (Numbers 25:1; Joshua 2:1; Micah 6:5), a place on the east of Jordan, in the plain of Moab, nearly opposite Jericho. It was the forty-second encampment of the Israelites, their last resting-place before they crossed the Jordan (Numbers 33:49; 22:1; 26:3; 31:12; comp. 25:1; 31:16).
places.smithEn: (the meadow of the acacias), in the “plains” of Moab, on the low level of the Jordan valley, opposite Jericho. The last resting-place of Israel before crossing the Jordan. (Numbers 33:49) The place is most frequently mentioned by its shorter name of Shittim. See Shittah Tree, Shittim, Shittim.

places.name: 아비에셀
places.desc: 부족/민족. 삿8:2
places.eastonKo: "도움의 아버지," 곧 "돕는 자." (1.) 길르앗의 누이 함몰레겟의 세 아들 중 둘째.
places.smithKo: '도움의 아버지, 곧 도움이 되는'이라는 뜻. (1) 길르앗의 맏아들로 므낫세의 후손이며 사사 기드온의 조상(여호수아 17:2). (2) 다윗의 용사 중 하나(사무엘하 23:27)…
places.eastonEn: father of help; i.e., “helpful.” (1.) The second of the three sons of Hammoleketh, the sister of Gilead. He was the grandson of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 7:18). From his family Gideon sprang (Joshua 17:2; comp. Judges 6:34; 8:2). He was also called Jeezer (Numbers 26:30). (2.) One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Samuel 23:27; comp. 1 Chronicles 27:12). (3.) The prince of the tribe of Dan at the Exodus (Numbers 1:12).
places.smithEn: (father of help, helpful). • Eldest son of Gilead, and descendant of Manasseh. (Joshua 17:2; 1 Chronicles 7:18) (B.C. 1450.) He was the ancestor of the great judge Gideon. [Gideon] • One of David’s mighty men. (2 Samuel 23:27; 1 Chronicles 11:28; 27:12) (B.C. 1014.)

places.name: 아빌라
places.desc: 성읍. 아빌라에 언급된 지명
places.smithKo: 아빌레네(ABILENE) 항목 참조.
places.smithEn: [Abilene]

places.name: 아빌라 루사니우
places.desc: 성읍. 아빌라 루사니우에 언급된 지명

places.name: 아빌레네
places.desc: 루사니아가 통치한 분봉왕국. 세례 요한 사역 당시 배경 지명. 헤르몬 서쪽 다메섹 서북방
places.eastonKo: "평지"라는 뜻으로 안티레바논 산맥 동쪽 비탈에 있던 지역이며, 그 으뜸 성읍 아빌라에서 이름을 얻었다(눅 3:1). 아빌라는 헬리오폴리스(바알벡)와 다메섹 사이 수크 와디 바라다에 있었고 앞의 성읍에서 38마일, 뒤에서 18마일 거리였다. 루사니아가 이 지방의 분봉왕이었다.
places.smithKo: "초장의 땅"이라는 뜻이다(눅 3:1). 안티레바논 동쪽 비탈, 바라다(아바나)강이 적셔 주는 지역에 자리한 성읍이다. 다메섹에서 18마일 거리이며 수크 와디 바라다라는 인상적인 협곡에 서 있었다.
places.eastonEn: a plain, a district lying on the east slope of the Anti-Lebanon range; so called from its chief town, Abila (Luke 3:1), which stood in the Suk Wady Barada, between Heliopolis (Baalbec) and Damascus, 38 miles from the former and 18 from the latter. Lysanias was governor or tetrarch of this province.
places.smithEn: (land of meadows), (Luke 3:1) a city situated on the eastern slope of Antilibanus, in a district fertilized by the river Barada (Abana). The city was 18 miles from Damascus, and stood in a remarkable gorge called Suk Wady Barada .

places.name: 아브로나
places.desc: 에시온게벨 직전에 진을 쳤던 홍해 아카바만 북쪽 광야 진영
places.eastonKo: 개정역 표기이며 이스라엘이 광야에서 머문 곳 중 하나로 에시온게벨 바로 앞이다(민 33:34, 35). 흠정역에는 에브로나로 나온다.

places.name: 악갓 (아카드 제국)
places.desc: 사르곤 대왕의 아카드 제국 발원지이자 시날 땅의 중심 성읍
places.eastonKo: "높은 땅 또는 산지"라는 뜻으로 시날 땅의 성읍이다. 바벨론 북쪽 약 50마일의 아케르 쿠프 언덕으로 비정되나 확실치 않다. 니므롯 왕국의 성읍 중 하나였다(창 10:10). 유브라데 가까이, 십바라 맞은편에 있었다.
places.smithKo: 시날 땅의 성읍 중 하나다(창 10:10). 그 위치는 매우 불확실하다.
places.eastonEn: the high land or mountains, a city in the land of Shinar. It has been identified with the mounds of Akker Kuf, some 50 miles to the north of Babylon; but this is doubtful. It was one of the cities of Nimrod’s kingdom (Ge 10:10). It stood close to the Euphrates, opposite Sippara. (See SEPHARVAIM.) It is also the name of the country of which this city was the capital, namely, northern or upper Babylonia. The Accadians who came from the “mountains of the east,” where the ark rested, attained to a high degree of civilization. In the Babylonian inscriptions they are called “the black heads” and “the black faces,” in contrast to “the white race” of Semitic descent. They invented the form of writing in pictorial hieroglyphics, and also the cuneiform system, in which they wrote many books partly on papyrus and partly on clay. The Semitic Babylonians (“the white race”), or, as some scholars think, first the Cushites, and afterwards, as a second immigration, the Semites, invaded and conquered this country; and then the Accadian language ceased to be a spoken language, although for the sake of its literary treasures it continued to be studied by the educated classes of Babylonia. A large portion of the Ninevite tablets brought to light by Oriental research consists of interlinear or parallel translations from Accadian into Assyrian; and thus that long-forgotten language has been recovered by scholars. It belongs to the class of languages called agglutinative, common to the Tauranian race; i.e., it consists of words “glued together,” without declension of conjugation. These tablets in a remarkable manner illustrate ancient history. Among other notable records,  they contain an account of the Creation which closely resembles that given in the book of Genesis, of the Sabbath as a day of rest, and of the Deluge and its cause. (See BABYLON; CHALDEA.)
places.smithEn: one of the cities in the land of Shinar. (Genesis 10:10) Its position is quite uncertain.

places.name: 악고 (돌레마이 항구)
places.desc: 아셀 지파가 쫓아내지 못한 천연 항구, 신약 돌레마이
places.eastonKo: "무더운 또는 모래의," 아셀 지파에 속했으나 결코 그들에게 정복되지 않은 페니키아의 항구 도시(삿 1:31).
places.smithKo: 마카베오서와 신약의 '돌레마이'로, 오늘날 아카 또는 유럽인들이 부르는 생장다크르라 불리며 두로 남쪽 약 30마일의 시리아 해안 최대 항구 도시였다. 신약에는 사도행전 21:7에서 돌레마이로 한 번 언급된다.
places.eastonEn: sultry or sandy, a town and harbour of Phoenicia, in the tribe of Asher, but never acquired by them (Judges 1:31). It was known to the ancient Greeks and Romans by the name of Ptolemais, from Ptolemy the king of Egypt, who rebuilt it about B.C. 100. Here Paul landed on his last journey to Jerusalem (Acts 21:7). During the crusades of the Middle Ages it was called Acra; and subsequently, on account of its being occupied by the Knights Hospitallers of Jerusalem, it was called St. Jean d’Acre, or simply Acre.
places.smithEn: (the Ptolemaisof the Maccabees and New Testament), Now called Acca, or more usually by Europeans St. Jean d’Acre, the most important seaport town on the Syrian coast, about 30 miles south of Tyre. It was situated on a slightly projecting headland, at the northern extremity of that spacious bay which is formed by the bold promontory of Carmel on the opposite side. Later it was named Ptolemais, after one of the Ptolemies, probably Soter. The only notice of it in the New Testament is in (Acts 21:7) where it is called Ptolemais .

places.name: 아가야
places.eastonKo: 본래 펠로폰네소스 북서쪽 그리스의 좁고 긴 지역 이름이었다. 후에 로마인들이 지금 모레아라 불리는 펠로폰네소스 전체와 그리스 남부에 이 이름을 붙였다.
places.smithKo: 신약에서는 펠로폰네소스 전역과 헬라 본토 대부분, 그리고 인근 섬들을 포함한 로마 속주를 가리킨다. 이 속주와 마게도냐 속주가 그리스 전체를 이루었다.
places.eastonEn: the name originally of a narrow strip of territory in Greece, on the north-west of the Peloponnesus. Subsequently it was applied by the Romans to the whole Peloponnesus, now called the Morea, and the south of Greece. It was then one of the two provinces (Macedonia being the other) into which they divided the country when it fell under their dominion. It is in this latter enlarged meaning that the name is always used in the New Testament (Acts 18:12, 27; 19:21; Romans 15: 26; 16:5, etc.). It was at the time when Luke wrote the Acts of the Apostles under the  proconsular form of government; hence the appropriate title given to Gallio as the “deputy,” i.e., proconsul, of Achaia (Acts 18:12).
places.smithEn: (trouble) signifies in the New Testament a Roman province which included the whole of the Peloponnesus and the greater part of Hellas proper, with the adjacent islands. This province, with that of Macedonia, comprehended the while of Greece; hence Achaia and Macedonia are frequently mentioned together in the New Testament to indicate all Greece. (Acts 18:12; 19:21; Romans 15:26; 16:5; 1 Corinthians 16:15; 2 Corinthians 7:5; 9:2; 11:10; 1 Thessalonians 1:7,8) In the time of the emperor Claudius it was governed by a proconsul, translated in the Authorized Version “deputy,” of Achaia. (Acts 18:12)

places.name: 악삽 (가나안 왕 성읍)
places.desc: 메롬 물가 연합군 왕의 성읍, 악고 평야의 중심 거점
places.eastonKo: "매혹"이라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 북부의 가나안 왕도다(수 11:1; 12:20; 19:25). 아셀 지파의 동쪽 경계에 있었으며 악고 북동쪽의 폐허 마을 케사프 또는 야시프로 비정된다.
places.smithKo: "매혹"이라는 뜻으로 아셀 지경 안의 성읍이며 베덴과 알람멜렉 사이에 이름이 나온다(수 19:25). 본래 가나안 왕이 거하던 곳이다(수 11:1; 12:20).
places.eastonEn: fascination, a royal city of the Canaanites, in the north of Palestine (Joshua 11:1; 12:20; 19:25). It was in the eastern boundary of the tribe of Asher, and is identified with the modern ruined village of Kesaf or Yasif, N.E. of Accho.
places.smithEn: (fascination), a city within the territory of Asher, named between Beten and Alammelech, (Joshua 19:25) originally the seat of a Canaanite king. (Joshua 11:1; 12:20)

places.name: 악십 (미가의 심판 예언) (Tel el Beida) 1
places.desc: "악십의 집들이 이스라엘 왕들을 속이리로다" 미가가 탄식한 성읍
places.eastonKo: "거짓"이라는 뜻. (1) 유다 평지 셰펠라의 성읍(수 15:44)으로 아마 창 38:5의 거십 곧 아인 케즈베와 같은 곳일 것이다. (2) 페니키아 성읍(그리스어 엑딥파)으로 아셀 지파에 배정되었으나 늘 페니키아의 소유로 남아 있었다(수 19:29; 삿 1:31).
places.smithKo: '거짓의'라는 뜻. (1) 유다 저지대의 성읍으로 그일라, 마레사와 함께 언급됨(여호수아 15:44); 그십, 고세바와 동일시된다. (2) 아셀 지파에 속한 성읍으로 가나안 사람들…
places.eastonEn: falsehood. (1.) A town in the Shephelah, or plain country of Judah (Joshua 15:44); probably the same as Chezib of Genesis 38:5 = Ain Kezbeh. (2.) A Phoenician city (the Gr. Ecdippa), always retained in their possession though assigned to the tribe of Asher (Joshua 19:29; Judges 1:31). It is identified with the modern es-Zib, on the Mediterranean, about 8 miles north of Accho.
places.smithEn: (lying, false). • A city in the lowlands of Judah, named with Keilah and Mareshah. (Joshua 15:44; Micah 1:14) It is probably the same with Cheziband Chozeba, which see. • A town belonging to Asher, (Joshua 19:29) from which the Canaanites were not expelled, (Judges 1:31) afterwards Ecdippa. It is now es-Zib, on the seashore, 2h. 20m. north of Acre.

places.name: 아다다
places.desc: 유다 지파 남단의 목축 거점 성읍
places.smithKo: "절기" 또는 "경계"라는 뜻으로 유다 최남단의 성읍 중 하나이며 디모나·게데스와 함께 언급된다(수 15:22).
places.smithEn: (festival or boundary), one of the cities in the extreme south of Judah, named with Dimonah and Kedesh. (Joshua 15:22)

places.name: 요단강 도하 지점 (아담 성읍)
places.desc: 제사장들의 발이 요단에 닿았을 때 강물이 멈추어 벽처럼 일어선 상류 성읍
places.eastonKo: "붉다"는 뜻의 바벨론 말로 사람을 가리키는 일반 명사이며 히브리어와 앗수르어에서 같은 뜻이다. 첫 사람에게 주어진 이름으로, 그 창조와 타락과 이후의 역사, 그리고 그 후손의 역사가 모세의 첫 책에 자세히 기록되어 있다(창 1:27~5장).
places.smithKo: 여호수아 때 "사르단 곁" 요단 가에 있던 성읍이다(수 3:16). 아담이라는 이름은 인류의 조상에게만 국한되지 않고 라틴어 호모처럼 남자와 여자 모두에게 쓰였다(창 5:2). "붉은 흙"이라는 뜻으로 성경이 첫 사람에게 준 이름이다.
places.eastonEn: red, a Babylonian word, the generic name for man, having the same meaning in the Hebrew and the Assyrian languages. It was the name given to the first man, whose creation, fall, and subsequent history and that of his descendants are detailed in the first book of Moses (Genesis 1:27-ch. 5). “God created man [Hebrews , Adam] in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.” Adam was absolutely the first man whom God created. He was formed out of the dust of the earth (and hence his name), and God breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and gave him dominion over all the lower creatures (Genesis 1:26; 2:7). He was placed after his creation in the Garden of Eden, to cultivate it, and to enjoy its fruits under this one prohibition: “Of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil thou shalt not eat of it; for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.” The first recorded act of Adam was his giving names to the beasts of the field and the fowls of the air, which God brought to him for this end. Thereafter the Lord caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, and while in an unconscious state took one of his ribs, and closed up his flesh again; and of this rib he made a woman, whom he presented to him when he awoke. Adam received her as his wife, and said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” He called her Eve, because she was the mother of all living. Being induced by the tempter in the form of a serpent to eat the forbidden fruit, Eve persuaded Adam, and he also did eat. Thus man fell, and brought  upon himself and his posterity all the sad consequences of his transgression. The narrative of the Fall comprehends in it the great promise of a Deliverer (Genesis 3:15), the “first gospel” message to man. They were expelled from Eden, and at the east of the garden God placed a flame, which turned every way, to prevent access to the tree of life (Genesis 3). How long they were in Paradise is matter of mere conjecture. Shortly after their expulsion Eve brought forth her first-born, and called him Cain. Although we have the names of only three of Adam’s sons, viz., Cain, Abel, and Seth, yet it is obvious that he had several sons and daughters (Genesis 5:4). He died aged 930 years. Adam and Eve were the progenitors of the whole human race. Evidences of varied kinds are abundant in proving the unity of the human race. The investigations of science, altogether independent of historical evidence, lead to the conclusion that God “hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth” (Acts 17:26. Comp. Romans 5:12-12; 1 Corinthians 15:22-49).
places.smithEn: a city on the Jordan, “beside Zaretan,” in the time of Joshua. (Joshua 3:16) Man, generically, for the name Adam was not confined to the father of the human race, but like homo was applicable to woman as well as to man . (Genesis 5:2) (red earth), the name given in Scripture to the first man. It apparently has reference to the ground from which he was formed, which is called in Hebrew Adamah . The idea of redness of color seems to be inherent in either word. The creation of man was the work of the sixth day—the last and crowning act of creation. Adam was created (not born) a perfect man in body and spirit, but as innocent and completely inexperienced as a child. The man Adam was placed in a garden which the Lord God had planted “eastward in Eden,” for the purpose of dressing it and keeping it. [Eden] Adam was permitted to eat of the fruit of every tree in the garden but one, which was called (“the tree of the knowledge of good and evil,” because it was the test of Adam’s obedience. By it Adam could know good and evil int he divine way, through obedience; thus knowing good by experience in resisting temptation and forming a strong and holy character, while he knew evil only by observation and inference. Or he could “know good and evil,” in Satan’s way, be experiencing the evil and knowing good only by contrast. -ED.) The prohibition to taste the fruit of this tree was enforced by the menace of death. There was also another tree which was called “the tree of life.” While Adam was in the garden of Eden, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the air were brought to him to be named. After this the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, and took one of his ribs from him, which he fashioned into a woman and brought her to the man. At this time they were both described as being naked without the consciousness of shame. By the subtlety of the serpent the woman who was given to be with Adam was beguiled into a violation of the one command which had been imposed upon them. She took of the fruit of the forbidden tree and gave it to her husband. The propriety of its name was immediately shown in the results which followed; selfconsciousness was the first-fruits of sin their eyes were opened and they knew that they were naked. Though the curse of Adam’s rebellion of necessity fell upon him, yet the very prohibition to eat of the tree of life after his transgression was probably a manifestation of divine mercy, because the greatest malediction of all would have been to have the gift of indestructible life super-added to a state of wretchedness and sin. The divine mercy was also shown in the promise of a deliverer given at the very promise of a deliverer given at the very time the curse was imposed, (Genesis 3:15) and opening a door of hope to Paradise, regained for him and his descendants. Adam is stated to have lived 930 years. His sons mentioned in Scripture are Cain, Abel and Seth; it is implied, however, that he had others.

places.name: 아다마
places.desc: 갈릴리 하부 비옥한 고원의 농경 성읍
places.eastonKo: "붉은 흙"이라는 뜻으로 납달리의 요새 성읍이며 아마 디베랴 바다 서편의 오늘날 다미예일 것이다(수 19:33, 36).
places.smithKo: "붉은 흙"이라는 뜻으로 납달리의 "견고한 성읍" 중 하나이며 긴네렛과 라마 사이에 이름이 나온다(수 19:36).
places.eastonEn: red earth, a fortified city of Naphtali, probably the modern Damieh, on the west side of the sea of Tiberias (Joshua 19:33, 36).
places.smithEn: (red earth), one of the “fenced cities” of Naphtali, named between Chinnereth and Ramah. (Joshua 19:36)

places.name: 아다미넥게브
places.desc: 납달리 지파 남쪽 경계 고갯길 성읍

places.name: 아다사
places.desc: 성읍. 아다사에 언급된 지명
places.eastonKo: '새로운'이라는 뜻으로, 유다 골짜기의 성읍(여호수아 15:37).
places.smithKo: '새로운'이라는 뜻으로 벧호론에서 약 4마일 떨어진 유대의 한 장소이며 하다사(HADASHAH)와 관련된다.
places.eastonEn: new, a city in the valley of Judah (Joshua 15:37).
places.smithEn: (new), a place in Judea, about four miles from Beth-horon. 1Ma 7:40,45[Hadashah]

places.name: 아달 (유다 남쪽 경계)
places.desc: 가데스 바네아 서쪽 유다의 남부 국경점
places.eastonKo: "넉넉하다, 빛나다"는 뜻으로 벨라의 아들이며(대상 8:3) 아릇이라고도 한다(창 46:21).
places.smithKo: "강한 자"라는 뜻으로 벨라의 아들이며(대상 8:3) 민 26:40에는 아릇으로 나온다.
places.eastonEn: ample, splendid, son of Bela (1 Chronicles 8:3); called also “Ard” (Genesis 46:21)
places.smithEn: (mighty one), son of Bela, (1 Chronicles 8:3) called Ardin (Numbers 26:40)

places.name: 앗돈
places.eastonKo: "낮은," 느헤미야 7:61에 언급된 사람 중 하나로, 포로에서 돌아왔을 때 "자기 조상의 집"을 증명하지 못한 자.
places.smithKo: '주인'이라는 뜻. 앗단(ADDAN) 항목 참조.
places.eastonEn: low, one of the persons named in Nehemiah 7:61 who could not “shew their father’s house” on the return from captivity. This, with similar instances (ver. 63), indicates the importance the Jews attached to their genealogies.
places.smithEn: (lord). [Addan]

places.name: 아두스 (두마)
places.desc: 유다 셰펠라 저지대의 고대 마을
places.smithKo: "두 겹 장식"이라는 뜻으로 저지대에 있던 유다의 성읍이며 사아라임과 그데라 사이에 이름이 나온다. 수 15:36에만 언급된다.
places.smithEn: (double ornament), a town belonging to Judah, lying in the low country, and named, between Sharaim and hag-Gederah, in (Joshua 15:36) only.

places.name: 아드마
places.desc: 소돔, 고모라와 함께 유황 불 심판으로 멸망한 평지 성읍
places.eastonKo: "흙"이라는 뜻으로 싯딤 골짜기의 다섯 성읍 중 하나다(창 10:19). 소돔·고모라와 함께 멸망했다(창 19:24; 신 29:23). 수 3:16의 아담과 같은 곳으로 보는 이들도 있는데, 그 이름이 요단 나루 다미예에 아직 남아 있다.
places.smithKo: "흙, 요새"라는 뜻으로 "평지 성읍" 중 하나이며 늘 스보임과 짝지어 나온다(창 10:19; 14:2, 8; 신 29:23; 호 11:8).
places.eastonEn: earth, one of the five cities of the vale of Siddim (Genesis 10:19). It was destroyed along with Sodom and Gomorrah (19:24; Deuteronomy 29:23). It is supposed by some to be the same as the Adam of Joshua 3:16, the name of which still lingers in Damieh, the ford of Jordan. (See ZEBOIM.)
places.smithEn: (earthy, fortress), one of the “cities of the plain,” always coupled with Zeboim. (Genesis 10:19; 14:2,8; 29:23; Hosea 11:8)

places.name: 아도라임 (르호보암 요새)
places.desc: 헤브론 남서쪽 유다 산지를 방어하던 르호보암의 국경 요새
places.smithKo: "두 겹 둔덕"이라는 뜻으로 르호보암이 유다에 세운 요새 성읍이다(대하 11:9). 아도라임은 아마 마카베오상 13:20의 아도라와 같은 곳일 것이다. 로빈슨은 헤브론 서쪽 높은 지대의 "큰 마을" 두라로 비정한다.
places.smithEn: (double mound), a fortified city built by Rehoboam, (2 Chronicles 11:9) in Judah. Adoraim is probably the same place with Adora, 1Ma 13:20Unless that be Dor, on the seacoast below Carmel. Robinson identifies it with Dura, a “large village” on a rising ground west of Hebron.

places.name: 아드라뭇데노
places.desc: 바울 로마행 마지막 항해 출발 선박 소속 소아시아 에게해 항구도시. 가이사랴 출항 배
places.eastonKo: 무시아 해안에 있던 소아시아의 성읍으로 이른 시기에는 아이올리스라 불렸다. 바울이 가이사랴에서 탄 배가 이 성읍의 배였다(행 27:2). 바울은 그 배로 루기아의 무라까지만 갔고, 거기서 알렉산드리아 배로 갈아타 이탈리아로 갔다.
places.smithKo: 루디아 왕 크로이소스의 형제 아드라미스에게서 이름을 얻었으며, 에게해 만에 자리한 아시아 속주의 항구다. 서머나 북쪽 약 70마일, 옛적에 아이올리스라 불리고 무시아라고도 하던 지역에 있다(행 27:2). 오늘날의 아드라미티는 초라한 마을이다.
places.eastonEn: a city of Asia Minor on the coast of Mysia, which in early times was called AEolis. The ship in which Paul embarked at Caesarea belonged to this city (Acts 27:2). He was conveyed in it only to Myra, in Lycia, whence he sailed in an Alexandrian ship to Italy. It was a rare thing for a ship to sail from any port of Palestine direct for Italy. It still bears the name Adramyti, and is a place of some traffic.
places.smithEn: named form Adramys, brother of Croesus king of Lydia, a seaport in the province of Asia [Asia], situated on a bay of the Aegean Sea, about 70 miles north of Smyrna, in the district anciently called Aeolis, and also Mysia. See (Acts 16:7) [Mitylene] (Acts 27:2) The modern Adramyti is a poor village.

places.name: 아드리아해
places.desc: 바다/호수. 행27:27

places.name: 아둘리스
places.desc: 성읍. 아둘리스에 언급된 지명

places.name: 아둘람 (다윗의 피신 요새)
places.desc: 르호보암이 유다 서남부를 방어하기 위해 요새화한 성읍
places.eastonKo: 가나안 사람들의 왕도 중 하나로, 오늘날의 '아이드 엘마'다(여호수아 12:15; 15:35). 옛 로마 도로 위, 엘라 골짜기에 위치했으며 이곳은 다윗이 골리앗을 이긴 기념할 만…
places.smithKo: '백성의 정의'라는 뜻으로 유다 저지대(세벨라)의 도시이며(여호수아 15:35) 본래 가나안 왕의 거처였다. 르호보암이 요새화했고(역대하 11:7) 포로 후 유대인들이 재정착한 곳…
places.eastonEn: one of the royal cities of the Canaanites, now ‘Aid-el-ma (Joshua 12:15; 15:35). It stood on the old Roman road in the valley of Elah (q.v.), which was the scene of David’s memorable victory over Goliath (1 Samuel 17:2), and not far from Gath. It was one of the towns which Rehoboam fortified against Egypt (2 Chronicles 11:7). It was called “the glory of Israel” (Micah 1:15). The Cave of Adullam has been discovered about 2 miles south of the scene of David’s triumph, and about 13 miles west from Bethlehem. At this place is a hill some 500 feet high pierced with numerous caverns, in one of which David gathered together “every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented” (1 Samuel 22:2). Some of these caverns are large enough to hold 200 or 300 men. According to tradition this cave was at Wady Khureitun, between Bethlehem and the Dead Sea, but this view cannot be well maintained.
places.smithEn: (justice of the people), Apocr. Odollam, a city of Judah int he lowland of the Shefelah, (Joshua 15:35) the seat of a Canaanite king, (Joshua 12:15) and evidently a place of great antiquity. (Genesis 38:1,12,20) Fortified by Rehoboam, (2 Chronicles 11:7) it was one of the towns reoccupied by the Jews after their return from Babylon, (Nehemiah 11:30) and still a city in the time of the Macabees. 2Ma 12:38Adullam was probably near Deir Dubban, five or six miles north of Eleutheropolis. The limestone cliffs of the whole of that locality are pierced with extensive excavations, some one of which is doubtless the “cave of Adullam,” the refuge of David. (1 Samuel 22:1; 2 Samuel 23:13; 1 Chronicles 11:15)

places.name: 아둠밈 비탈 (피의 언덕)
places.desc: 선한 사마리아인 비유의 배경이 된 예루살렘에서 여리고로 내려가는 붉은 비탈길
places.eastonKo: '붉은 것들'이라는 뜻으로, 여리고와 예루살렘 사이 길 위, 와디 켈트 급류의 남쪽, 길갈을 바라보는 곳에 위치한 장소로 보인다(여호수아 15:7; 18:17). 예루살렘과 여리고…
places.smithKo: '오르막'이라는 뜻으로 길갈 맞은편, 시내 남쪽의 고갯길이며(여호수아 15:7) 오늘날에도 여리고에서 예루살렘으로 오르는 길이 지나는 와디 켈트 협곡 남쪽 사면에 해당한다.
places.eastonEn: the red ones, a place apparently on the road between Jericho and Jerusalem, “on the south side of the torrent” Wady Kelt, looking  toward Gilgal, mentioned Joshua 15:7; 18:17. It was nearly half-way between Jerusalem and Jericho, and now bears the name of Tal-at-ed-Dumm. It is supposed to have been the place referred to in the parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30-37). Recently a new carriage-road has been completed, and carriages for the first time have come along this road from Jerusalem.
places.smithEn: (the going up to), a rising ground or pass over against Gilgal,” and “on the south side of the ’torrent’” (Joshua 15:7; 18:17) which is the position still occupied by the road leading up from Jericho and the Jordan valley to Jerusalem, on the south face of the gorge of the Wady Kelt. (Luke 10:30-36)

places.name: 에논 & 살림 (세례 요한 사역지)
places.desc: 물이 많아 세례 요한이 와서 세례를 베풀던 요단 골짜기 샘터
places.eastonKo: "샘들"이라는 뜻으로 요한이 세례를 베푼 살렘 근처의 한 곳이다(요 3:23). 아마 에발산에서 요단까지 뻗은 트인 골짜기 와디 파라의 상류 발원지 부근일 것이다. 샘이 많은 곳이다. 그 샘들 북쪽 4마일에서 아이눈이라는 곳이 발견되었다.
places.smithKo: "샘들"이라는 뜻으로 요한이 세례를 베푼 "살렘 가까운" 곳이다(요 3:23). 요단 서편이었음이 분명하며 물이 많았다. 오노마스티콘에는 스키토폴리스 남쪽 8마일, "살렘과 요단 근처"로 나온다.
places.eastonEn: springs, a place near Salim where John baptized (John 3:23). It was probably near the upper source of the Wady Far’ah, an open valley extending from Mount Ebal to the Jordan. It is full of springs. A place has been found called ‘Ainun, four miles north of the springs.
places.smithEn: (springs) a place “near to Salim,” at which John baptized. (John 3:23) It was evidently west of the Jordan, comp. (John 3:22) with John 3:26and with John 1:28And abounded in water. It is given in the Omomasticon as eight miles south of Scythopolis “near Salem and the Jordan.”

places.name: 아하와 강가 (에스라 금식기도)
places.desc: 포로 귀환자들을 모아 왕의 군대 없이 오직 하나님의 도우심을 구하며 금식 기도한 강가
places.eastonKo: '물'이라는 뜻으로, 에스라 아래 모인 유대인 포로들이 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 돌아가려 할 때 그 강둑에 진을 쳤던 강이다(에스라 8:21). 아마도 바벨론 서북쪽 어딘가에서 유프…
places.smithKo: '물'이라는 뜻으로 에스라가 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 돌아올 두 번째 무리를 모은 장소 또는 강이다(에스라 8:15).
places.eastonEn: water, the river (Ezra 8:21) by the banks of which the Jewish exiles assembled under Ezra when about to return to Jerusalem from Babylon. In all probability this was one of the streams of Mesopotamia which flowed into the Euphrates somewhere in the north-west of  Babylonia. It has, however, been supposed to be the name of a place (Ezra 8:15) now called Hit, on the Euphrates, east of Damascus.
places.smithEn: (water), a place, (Ezra 8:15) or a river, Ezra 8:21On the banks of which Ezra collected the second expedition which returned with him from Babylon to Jerusalem. Perhaps it is the modern Hit, on the Euphrates due east of Damascus.

places.name: 아흘랍 (아셀 지파 성읍)
places.desc: 아셀 지파가 가나안 사람을 쫓아내지 못한 두로 북쪽 해안 성읍
places.eastonKo: "기름지다"는 뜻으로 정복되지 않은 페니키아 경계 안, 갈릴리 바다 북서쪽에 있던 아셀의 성읍이다(삿 1:31). 흔히 기스칼라 곧 오늘날의 엘 지시로 비정된다.
places.smithKo: "비옥하다"는 뜻으로 가나안 사람이 쫓겨나지 않은 아셀의 성읍이다(삿 1:31).
places.eastonEn: fatness, a town of Asher lying within the unconquered Phoenician border (Judges 1:31), north-west of the Sea of Galilee; commonly identified with Giscala, now el-Jish.
places.smithEn: (fertile), a city of Asher from which the Canaanites were not driven out. (Judges 1:31)

places.name: 아이 (아브라함과 여호수아) (Et Tell) 1

places.desc: 아브라함이 장막을 치고 여호수아가 매복 작전으로 정복한 성읍
places.eastonKo: "폐허"라는 뜻. (1) 가나안 왕도 중 하나(수 10:1; 창 12:8; 13:3). 여호수아가 패배했다가 후에 승리한 곳으로, 이스라엘이 점령한 두 번째 가나안 성읍이다(수 7:2-5; 8:1-29). 후에 다시 세워져 베냐민 자손이 거했다(스 2:28; 느 7:32).
places.smithKo: '폐허 더미'라는 뜻. (1) 벧엘 동쪽, 벧아웬 곁에 위치한 성읍으로 이스라엘이 요단강을 건넌 후 두 번째로 점령해 완전히 멸한 곳이다(여호수아 7:2). (2) 암몬 사람의 성…
places.eastonEn: ruins. (1.) One of the royal cities of the Canaanites (Joshua 10:1; Genesis 12:8; 13:3). It was the scene of Joshua’s defeat, and afterwards of his victory. It was the second Canaanite city taken by Israel (Joshua 7:2-5; 8:1-29). It lay rebuilt and inhibited by the Benjamites (Ezra 2:28; Nehemiah 7:32; 11:31). It lay to the east of Bethel, “beside Beth-aven.” The spot which is most probably the site of this ancient city is Haiyan, 2 miles east from Bethel. It lay up the Wady Suweinit, a steep, rugged valley, extending from the Jordan valley to Bethel. (2.) A city in the Ammonite territory (Jeremiah 49:3). Some have thought that the proper reading of the word is Ar (Isaiah 15:1).
places.smithEn: (heap of ruins). • A city lying east of Bethel and “beside Bethaven.” (Joshua 7:2; 8:9) It was the second city taken by Israel after the passage of the Jordan, and was “utterly destroyed.” (Joshua 7:3-5; 8:1; Joshua 9:3; 10:1,2; 12:9) • A city of the Ammonites, apparently attached to Heshbon. (Jeremiah 49:3)

places.name: 아이 (아브라함과 여호수아) (in Moab 1) 2
places.desc: 아브라함이 장막을 치고 여호수아가 매복 작전으로 정복한 성읍

places.name: 아야 (아이얏)
places.desc: 앗수르 군대가 침공하며 처음 지난 아이성 부근 성읍
places.smithKo: 아이의 여성형이며 이사야가 미그론·믹마스와 함께 언급한 곳이다(사 10:28). 아마 아이와 같은 곳일 것이다.
places.smithEn: (feminine of Ai), a place named by Isaiah, (Isaiah 10:28) in connection with Migron and Michmash probably the same as Ai.

places.name: 아이야
places.eastonKo: '여호와의 형제'(곧 '벗')라는 뜻. (1.) 벨라의 아들 중 하나(역대상 8:7, 개정역). 흠정역에서는 '아히아'로 불린다. (2.) 유다의 증손자인 여라므엘의 다섯 아들 중 하나(역대상 2:25). (3.) 아히둡의 아들(사무엘상 14:3,18)이며 이가봇의 형제. 사울 시대에 놉에서 대제사장이었던 아히멜렉과 아마도 동일 인물일 것이다(사무엘상 22:11). 다만 일부는 아히멜렉이 아히야의 형제였고, 둘 다 대제사장으로 봉사했는데 아히야는 기브아 또는 기럇여아림에서, 아히멜렉은 놉에서 봉사했다고 본다. (4.) 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람인 블론 사람(역대상 11:36); 엘리암이라고도 불린다(사무엘하 23:34). (5.) 성전 성물 창고를 관리하던 레위인(역대상 26:20). (6.) 솔로몬의 서기관 중 한 사람(열왕기상 4:3). (7.) 르호보암 시대에 '실로 사람'이라 불린 실로의 선지자(열왕기상 11:29; 14:2). 그가 남긴 주목할 만한 두 예언이 기록되어 있다. 열왕기상 11:31-39는 솔로몬으로부터 열 지파가 찢겨 나갈 것을 선포하고, 열왕기상 14:6-16은 여로보암의 아내에게 전한 것으로 왕의 아들 아비야의 죽음과 여로보암 집의 멸망, 그리고 이스라엘이 '강 너머로' 사로잡혀 갈 것을 예언한다. 여로보암 자신도 그가 하나님의 선지자로서 얼마나 높이 존경받았는지를 증언한다(열왕기상 14:2,3).
places.smithKo: 아얏처럼 '아이'의 변형으로 추정되며 믹마스, 벧엘과 함께 언급된다(느헤미야 11:31).
places.eastonEn: brother (i.e., “friend”) of Jehovah. (1.) One of the sons of Bela (1 Chronicles 8:7, R.V.). In A.V. called “Ahiah.” (2.) One of the five sons of Jerahmeel, who was great-grandson of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:25). (3.) Son of Ahitub (1 Samuel 14:3, 18), Ichabod’s brother; the same probably as Ahimelech, who was high priest at Nob in the reign of Saul (1 Samuel 22:11). Some, however, suppose that Ahimelech was the brother of Ahijah, and that they both officiated as high priests, Ahijah at Gibeah or Kirjath-jearim, and Ahimelech at Nob. (4.) A Pelonite, one of David’s heroes (1 Chronicles 11:36); called also Eliam (2 Samuel 23:34). (5.) A Levite having charge of the sacred treasury in the temple (1 Chronicles 26:20). (6.) One of Solomon’s secretaries (1 Kings 4:3). (7.) A prophet of Shiloh (1 Kings 11:29; 14:2), called the “Shilonite,” in the days of Rehoboam. We have on record two of his remarkable prophecies, 1 Kings 11:31-39, announcing the rending of the ten tribes from Solomon; and 1 Kings 14:6-16, delivered to Jeroboam’s wife, foretelling the death of Abijah the king’s son, the destruction of Jeroboam’s house, and the captivity of Israel “beyond the river.” Jeroboam bears testimony to the high esteem in which he was held as a prophet of God (1 Kings 14:2,3).
places.smithEn: like Aiath probably a variation of the name Ai, mentioned with Michmash and Bethel. (Nehemiah 11:31)

places.name: 아얄론 (태양이 머문 골짜기) (Yalo) 1
places.desc: "달아 아얄론 골짜기에 머물라" 기도가 이루어진 골짜기
places.smithKo: '노루의 처소'라는 뜻. (1) 고핫 자손의 레위 성읍이자 도피성(여호수아 21:24); 본래 단 지파에 배분되었으나 아모리 족속을 쫓아내지 못했다(사사기 1:35). 르호보암이 …
places.smithEn: (place of gazelles). • A city of the Kohathites. (Joshua 21:24; 1 Chronicles 6:69) It was a Levitical city and a city of refuge. It was originally allotted to the tribe of Dan, (Joshua 19:42) Authorized Version, AJALON, which tribe, however, was unable to dispossess the Amorites of the place. (Judges 1:35) Aijalon was one of the towns fortified by Reheboam, (2 Chronicles 11:10) and the last we hear of it is being in the hands of the Philistines. (2 Chronicles 28:18) Being on the very frontier of the two kingdoms, we can understand how Aijalon should be spoken of sometimes, (1 Chronicles 6:69) comp. with 1Chr 6:66As in Ephraim and sometimes, (2 Chronicles 11:10; 1 Samuel 14:31) as in Judah and Benjamin. It is represented by the modern Yalo, a little to the north of the Jaffa road, about 14 miles out of Jerusalem. • A broad and beautiful valley near the city of Aijalon over which Joshua commanded the moon to stand still during the pursuit after the battle of Gibeon. (Joshua 10:12) • A place in Zebulon, mentioned as the burial-place of Elon, one of the Judges. (Judges 12:12)

places.name: 아얄론 (태양이 머문 골짜기) (Rumana) 2
places.desc: "달아 아얄론 골짜기에 머물라" 기도가 이루어진 골짜기
places.smithKo: '노루의 처소'라는 뜻. (1) 고핫 자손의 레위 성읍이자 도피성(여호수아 21:24); 본래 단 지파에 배분되었으나 아모리 족속을 쫓아내지 못했다(사사기 1:35). 르호보암이 …
places.smithEn: (place of gazelles). • A city of the Kohathites. (Joshua 21:24; 1 Chronicles 6:69) It was a Levitical city and a city of refuge. It was originally allotted to the tribe of Dan, (Joshua 19:42) Authorized Version, AJALON, which tribe, however, was unable to dispossess the Amorites of the place. (Judges 1:35) Aijalon was one of the towns fortified by Reheboam, (2 Chronicles 11:10) and the last we hear of it is being in the hands of the Philistines. (2 Chronicles 28:18) Being on the very frontier of the two kingdoms, we can understand how Aijalon should be spoken of sometimes, (1 Chronicles 6:69) comp. with 1Chr 6:66As in Ephraim and sometimes, (2 Chronicles 11:10; 1 Samuel 14:31) as in Judah and Benjamin. It is represented by the modern Yalo, a little to the north of the Jaffa road, about 14 miles out of Jerusalem. • A broad and beautiful valley near the city of Aijalon over which Joshua commanded the moon to stand still during the pursuit after the battle of Gibeon. (Joshua 10:12) • A place in Zebulon, mentioned as the burial-place of Elon, one of the Judges. (Judges 12:12)

places.name: 아인 (시므온 성읍) (Tel Dan) 1
places.desc: 시므온 지파에 속했던 샘 성읍, 레위 제사장 성읍
places.smithKo: '샘, 우물'이라는 뜻. (1) 팔레스타인 동쪽 경계의 지표 중 하나(민수기 34:11). (2) 유다 최남단 성읍으로(여호수아 15:32) 이후 시므온 지파에 배분되고(여호수아 …
places.smithEn: (spring, well). • One of the landmarks on the eastern boundary of Palestine. (Numbers 34:11) It is probably ’Ain el-’Azy, the main source of the Orontes. • One of the southernmost cities of Judah, (Joshua 15:32) afterwards allotted to Simeon, (Joshua 19:7; 1 Chronicles 4:32) and given to the priests. (Joshua 21:16)

places.name: 아켈다마 (피밭 / 토기장이의 밭)
places.modern: 힌놈 골짜기 하크 엘-담 성 오누프리오스 수도원 (예루살렘)
places.desc: 가룟 유다가 은 30을 돌려준 후 나그네의 묘지로 산 피밭 (아켈다마)
places.eastonKo: 우리 주를 배반한 자에게 주었던 돈으로 산 밭에 유대인들이 자기 나라 말, 곧 아람어로 붙인 이름. 이 말은 "피밭"을 뜻한다.
places.smithKo: 개정역이 행 1:19의 아겔다마를 이렇게 적는다.
places.eastonEn: the name which the Jews gave in their proper tongue, i.e., in Aramaic, to the field which was purchased with the money which had been given to the betrayer of our Lord. The word means “field of blood.” It was previously called “the potter’s field” (Matthew 27:7, 8; Acts 1:19), and was appropriated as the burial-place for strangers. It lies on a narrow level terrace on the south face of the valley of Hinnom. Its modern name is Hak ed-damm.
places.smithEn: Revised Version of (Acts 1:19) for Aceldama.

places.name: 아그랍빔 고개 (전갈 언덕)
places.desc: 약속의 땅 남방 경계 험준한 고개. 전갈 많은 언덕길. 아모리 족속 거주 남부 국경 표지
places.eastonKo: "전갈"이라는 뜻. 사해 남쪽과 신 사이의 고갯길을 품은 능선 에스 수파에 붙은 총칭으로 보이며, 이 길로 팔레스타인 땅 높이까지 올라간다. 이 일대에 전갈이 많다고 하여 붙은 이름이다(민 34:4).
places.smithKo: "오르막" 또는 "올라가는 길"이라는 뜻이며 마알레 아그랍빔 곧 "전갈 고개"라고도 한다. 사해 남쪽 끝과 신 사이의 고갯길로 유다(수 15:3)와 거룩한 땅(민 34:4)의 남쪽 경계 표지를 이룬다. 아모리의 경계이기도 했다.
places.eastonEn: scorpions, probably the general name given to the ridge containing the pass between the south of the Dead Sea and Zin, es-Sufah, by which there is an ascent to the level of the land of Palestine. Scorpions are said to abound in this whole district, and hence the name (Numbers 34:4). It is called “Maaleh-acrabbim” in Joshua 15:3, and “the ascent of Akrabbim” in Numbers 34:4.
places.smithEn: (the ascent of, or the going up to); also MAALEH-ACRABBIM (the scorpion pass), A pass between the south end of the Dead Sea and Zin, forming one of the landmarks on the south boundary at once of Judah, (Joshua 15:3) and of the Holy Land. (Numbers 34:4) Also the boundary of the Amorites. (Judges 1:36) As to the name, scorpions abound in the whole of this district.

places.name: 알레멧 (알몬)
places.desc: 베냐민 지파 레위 고핫 자손 배당 성읍. 예루살렘 북동방 근교. 아나돗과 인접
places.eastonKo: "덮음"이라는 뜻. (1) 베냐민의 아들 베겔의 아홉 아들 중 하나(대상 7:8). (2) 아하스의 아들 여호앗다 또는 야라의 아들 중 하나(대상 8:36). (3) 베냐민의 제사장 성읍(대상 6:60)으로 알몬이라고도 하며(수 21:18) 지금은 옛 아나돗 북동쪽 1마일의 알밋이다.
places.smithKo: "덮음"이라는 뜻으로 여호앗다 또는 야라의 아들인 베냐민 사람이며(대상 8:36; 9:42) 사울의 아들 요나단의 후손이다.
places.eastonEn: covering. (1.) One of the nine sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:8). (2.) One of the sons of Jehoadah, or Jarah, son of Ahaz (1 Chronicles 8:36).  (3.) A sacerdotal city of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 6:60), called also Almon (Joshua 21:18), now Almit, a mile north-east of the ancient Anathoth.
places.smithEn: (covering), a Benjamite, son of Jehoadah or Jarah, (1 Chronicles 8:36; 9:42) and descended from Jonathan the son of Saul. (B.C after 1077.)

places.name: 알렉산드리아 (아볼로의 고향)
places.desc: 성읍. 이집트 알렉산드리아. 행6:9; 행18:24; 행27:6; 행28:11
places.eastonKo: 하애굽의 옛 중심 도시로, 창건자 알렉산더 대왕(기원전 333년경)의 이름에서 왔다. 오랫동안 당대 최대 도시였는데, 니느웨와 바벨론은 이미 무너졌고 로마는 아직 융성하기 전이었기 때문이다.
places.smithKo: 알렉산더의 이름을 딴 이집트의 헬라·로마·그리스도교 수도로, 주전 332년 알렉산더 대왕이 건설했다. 유대인 인구가 많아 두 구역이 '유대인 구역'으로 불렸으며, 방대한 고대 도서…
places.eastonEn: the ancient metropolis of Lower Egypt, so called from its founder, Alexander the Great (about B.C. 333). It was for a long period the greatest of existing cities, for both Nineveh and Babylon had been destroyed, and Rome had not yet risen to greatness. It was the residence of the kings of Egypt for 200 years. It is not mentioned in the Old Testament, and only incidentally in the New. Apollos, eloquent and mighty in the Scriptures, was a native of this city (Acts 18:24). Many Jews from Alexandria were in Jerusalem, where they had a synagogue (Acts 6:9), at the time of Stephen’s martyrdom. At one time it is said that as many as 10,000 Jews resided in this city. It possessed a famous library of 700,000 volumes, which was burned by the Saracens (A.D. 642). It was here that the Hebrew Bible was translated into Greek. This is called the Septuagint version, from the tradition that seventy learned men were  engaged in executing it. It was, however, not all translated at one time. It was begun B.C. 280, and finished about B.C. 200 or 150. (See VERSION.)
places.smithEn: (from Alexander), 3 Ma 3:1; (Acts 18:24; 6:9) the Hellenic, Roman and Christian capital of Egypt. Situation .— (Alexandria was situated on the Mediterranean Sea directly opposite the island of Pharos, 12 miles west of the Canopic branch of the Nile and 120 miles from the present city of Cairo.) It was founded by Alexander the Great, B.C. 332, who himself traced the ground plan of the city. The work thus begun was continued after the death of Alexander by the Ptolemies. Description .— Under the despotism of the later Ptolemies the trade of Alexandria declined, but its population and wealth were enormous. Its importance as one of the chief corn-ports of Rome secured for it the general favor of the first emperors. Its population was mixed from the first. According to Josephus Alexander himself assigned to the Jews a place in his new city. Philo estimated the number of the Alexandrine Jews in his time at a little less than 1,000,000 and adds that two of the five districts of Alexandria were called “Jewish districts,” and that many Jews lived scattered in the remaining three. “For a long period Alexandria was the greatest of known cities.” After Rome became the chief city of the world, Alexandria ranked second to Rome in wealth and importance, and second to Athens only in literature and science. Its collection of books grew to be the greatest library of ancient times, and contained at one time 700,000 rolls or volumes. Here was made the Septuagint translation of the Old Testament into Greek, begun about B.C. 285, especially in grain, was very great. According to the common legend, St. Mark first “preached the gospel in Egypt, and founded the first church in Alexandria.” At the beginning of the second century the number of Christians at Alexandria must have been very large, and the great leaders of Gnosticism who arose there (Basilides, Valentinus) exhibit an exaggeration of the tendency of the Church. PRESENT CONDITION. The city still bears the same name and is a thriving metropolis, with inhabitants from nearly every European and Oriental nation. Cleopatra’s needle, set up by Thotmes in 1500 B.C., was found in Alexandria.

places.name: 알람멜렉
places.desc: 갈멜산 북쪽 기손강으로 흘러드는 시내와 성읍
places.smithKo: '왕의 상수리나무'라는 뜻으로 아셀 지파 경계, 악삽과 아맛 사이의 한 장소이다(여호수아 19:26).
places.smithEn: (king’s oak), a place within the limits of Asher, named between Achshaph and Amad. (Joshua 19:26) only.

places.name: 알론
places.eastonKo: '참나무'라는 뜻. (1.) 흠정역 여호수아 19:33의 '알론에서 사아난님까지'라는 표현은 개정역에서 '사아난님에 있는 참나무에서'로 더 정확히 번역된다. 이 단어는 사아난님 근…
places.smithKo: '큰 나무, 아마도 상수리나무'라는 뜻. (1) 납달리 성읍 중 하나로 더 정확히는 엘론이며(여호수아 19:33) '사아난님 곁 상수리나무'로 읽는 것이 옳다. (2) 알론바굿, …
places.eastonEn: oak. (1.) The expression in the Authorized Version of Joshua 19:33, “from Allon to Zaanannim,” is more correctly rendered in the Revised Version, “from the oak in Zaanannim.” The word denotes some remarkable tree which stood near Zaanannim, and which served as a landmark. (2.) The son of Jedaiah, of the family of the Simeonites, who expelled the Hamites from the valley of Gedor (1 Chronicles 4:37).
places.smithEn: a large strong tree of some description probably an oak. •Allonmore accurately Elon, a place named among the cities of Naphtali. (Joshua 19:33) Probably the more correct construction is to take it with the following word, i.e., “the oak by Zaanannim. [Elon] •AllonBACHUTH (oak of weeping) the tree under which Rebekah’s nurse, Deborah, was buried. (Genesis 35:8) (an oak) a Simeonite, ancestor of Ziza, a prince of his tribe in the reign of Hezekiah (1 Chronicles 4:37) (B.C. 727.)

places.name: 알론 바굿 (드보라 무덤 상수리)
places.desc: 리브가 유모 드보라 장사지. '통곡의 상수리나무' 의미. 야곱 가나안 귀환 시 벧엘 근방
places.eastonKo: '통곡의 참나무'라는 뜻으로, 벧엘 근처, 리브가의 유모 드보라가 묻힌 자리에 있던 나무다(창세기 35:8). 팔레스타인 평지에서는 큰 나무가 드물었기 때문에 흔히 이정표로 지정되었다. 이 특정한 나무는 아마도 '드보라의 종려나무'(사사기 4:5)와 같은 것이었을 것이다.
places.eastonEn: oak of weeping, a tree near Bethel, at the spot where Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, was buried (Genesis 35:8). Large trees, from their rarity in the plains of Palestine, were frequently designated as landmarks. This particular tree was probably the same as the “palm tree of Deborah” (Judges 4:5).

places.name: 알몬 (베냐민 제사장 성읍)
places.desc: 아나돗 곁에 위치한 아론 자손의 레위 제사장 성읍
places.eastonKo: "감추어졌다"는 뜻으로 베냐민의 제사장 성읍 중 하나이며(수 21:18) 알레멧이라고도 한다(대상 6:60).
places.smithKo: "감추어졌다"는 뜻으로 베냐민 지파 안의 성읍이며 딸린 들과 함께 제사장에게 주어졌다(수 21:18).
places.eastonEn: hidden, one of the sacerdotal cities of Benjamin (Joshua 21:18), called also Alemeth (1 Chronicles 6:60).
places.smithEn: (concealed) a city within the tribe of Benjamin, with “suburbs” given to the priests. (Joshua 21:18) [Alemeth]

places.name: 알몬디블라다임
places.desc: 모압 평지에 이르기 전 디본 갓을 떠나 진을 친 성읍
places.smithKo: "두 덩이를 감춤"이라는 뜻으로 디본갓과 아바림 산지 사이, 이스라엘의 후기 진영 중 하나다(민 33:46, 47). 아마 벧디블라다임과 같은 곳일 것이다.
places.smithEn: (concealing the two cakes), one of the latest stations of the Israelites between Dibon-gad and the mountains of Abarim (Numbers 33:46,47) It is probably identical with Beth-diblathaim.

places.name: 알루스
places.desc: 돕가를 떠나 르비딤에 이르기 전 머물렀던 시나이 광야 숙영지
places.eastonKo: 히브리인이 시내로 가는 길에 쉰 곳 중 하나로 르비딤 바로 앞이다(민 33:13, 14). 아마 홍해 기슭에 있었을 것이다.
places.smithKo: "사람의 무리"라는 뜻으로 이스라엘이 시내로 가는 여정에서 머문 진영 중 하나이며 르비딤 바로 앞이다(민 33:13, 14).
places.eastonEn: one of the places, the last before Rephidim, at which the Hebrews rested on their way to Sinai (Numbers 33:13, 14). It was probably situated on the shore of the Red Sea.
places.smithEn: (a crowd of men) one of the stations of the Israelites on their journey to Sinai, the last before Rephidim. (Numbers 33:13,14)

places.name: 아마
places.desc: 성읍. 아마에 언급된 지명
places.eastonKo: '규빗'이라는 뜻으로, 요압과 아비새가 아브넬을 추격하던 중 해질 무렵 이른 언덕의 이름이다(사무엘하 2:24). 기브온 동쪽에 위치했다.
places.smithKo: '머리'라는 뜻으로 기브온 광야로 가는 길목의 기아 맞은편 언덕이며, 요압이 아브넬을 쫓은 지점으로 언급된다(사무엘하 2:24).
places.eastonEn: a cubit, the name of a hill which Joab and Abishai reached as the sun went down, when they were in pursuit of Abner (2 Samuel 2:24). It lay to the east of Gibeon.
places.smithEn: (head), The hill of, A hill facing Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon, named as the point to which Joab pursued Abner (2 Samuel 2:24)

places.name: 아맛 (아셀)
places.desc: 악고 평야 남동쪽 아셀 성읍
places.smithKo: "오래 견디다"는 뜻으로 아셀에 있던 알려지지 않은 곳이며 알람멜렉과 미살 사이에 있다. 수 19:26에만 나온다.
places.smithEn: (enduring), an unknown place in Asher, between Alammelech and Misheal. (Joshua 19:26) only.

places.name: 아말렉
places.desc: 이스마엘의 후손으로 시나이 반도와 네게브에 거주한 유목 민족. 출애굽 직후 이스라엘을 공격(출17). 사울·다윗이 크게 격파
places.eastonKo: '골짜기의 거주자'라는 뜻으로, 엘리바스의 아들이며 에서의 손자(창세기 36:12; 역대상 1:36); 에돔 부족의 우두머리였다(창세기 36:16). 그의 어머니는 호리 족속으로,…
places.smithKo: '골짜기에 거하는 자'라는 뜻으로 엘리바스가 첩 딤나를 통해 낳은 아들이며 에서의 손자이자 에돔의 족장이다(창세기 36:12).
places.eastonEn: dweller in a valley, the son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau (Genesis 36:12; 1 Chronicles 1:36); the chief of an Idumean tribe (Genesis 36:16). His mother was a Horite, a tribe whose territory the descendants of Esau had seized.
places.smithEn: (dweller in a valley), a son of Eliphaz by his concubine Timnah grandson of Esau, and chieftain (“duke,” Authorized Version) of Edom. (Genesis 36:12,16; 1 Chronicles 1:36) (B.C. about 1700.)

places.name: 아맘
places.desc: 유다 지파 남부 네게브 평야 성읍
places.smithKo: "모이는 곳"이라는 뜻으로 유다 남부의 성읍이며 세마·몰라다와 함께 수 15:26에만 언급된다.
places.smithEn: (gathering place), a city in the south of Judah named with Shema and Moladah in (Joshua 15:26) only.

places.name: 아마나 (안티레바논 산맥)
places.desc: 다메섹의 바라다 강이 발원하는 사자 굴이 있는 산
places.eastonKo: "마르지 않는다"는 뜻. (1) 히브리어 난외주 왕하 5:12는 이를 다메섹 근처의 시내 아바나의 다른 읽기로 제시한다. (2) 산 이름(아 4:8)으로 아마 안티레바논 남쪽 봉우리일 것이며 그 기슭에 아바나의 발원지가 있다.
places.smithKo: "언약"이라는 뜻으로 레바논 안이나 그 근처의 산으로 보인다(아 4:8). 흔히 아바나강(왕하 5:12)이 발원하는 산으로 여겨진다.
places.eastonEn: perennial. (1.) The Hebrew margin of 2 Kings 5:12 gives this as another reading of Abana (q.v.), a stream near Damascus. (2.) A mountain (Cant. 4:8), probably the southern summit of Anti-Libanus, at the base of which are the sources of the Abana.
places.smithEn: (a covenant), apparently a mountain in or near Lebanon. (Song of Solomon 4:8) It is commonly assumed that this is the mountain in which the river Abana, (2 Kings 5:12) has its source.

places.name: 아마데
places.desc: 성읍. 아마데에 언급된 지명

places.name: 암마
places.desc: 언덕. 삼하2:24
places.eastonKo: '규빗'이라는 뜻으로, 요압과 아비새가 아브넬을 추격하던 중 해질 무렵 이른 언덕의 이름이다(사무엘하 2:24). 기브온 동쪽에 위치했다.
places.smithKo: '머리'라는 뜻으로 기브온 광야로 가는 길목의 기아 맞은편 언덕이며, 요압이 아브넬을 쫓은 지점으로 언급된다(사무엘하 2:24).
places.eastonEn: a cubit, the name of a hill which Joab and Abishai reached as the sun went down, when they were in pursuit of Abner (2 Samuel 2:24). It lay to the east of Gibeon.
places.smithEn: (head), The hill of, A hill facing Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon, named as the point to which Joab pursued Abner (2 Samuel 2:24)

places.name: 암몬
places.desc: 롯의 후손으로 요단 동편에 정착한 민족. 이스라엘의 이웃 적대 민족으로 삿기와 왕정기에 자주 충돌. 현재 요르단 암만
places.eastonKo: 롯의 아들 벤암미(창세기 19:38)의 또 다른 형태의 이름. 이 이름은 그의 후손을 가리키는 데도 쓰인다(시편 83:7).
places.smithKo: '명성의 아들들, 산사람들'이라는 뜻으로 롯이 작은딸에게서 낳은 벤암미의 후손이다(창세기 19:38). 모압 족속과 자주 함께 언급되며 얍복강을 경계로 삼았고 수도는 랍바(랍바암몬…
places.eastonEn: another form of the name Ben-ammi, the son of Lot (Genesis 19:38). This name is also used for his posterity (Psalm 83:7).
places.smithEn: (sons of renown, mountaineers), Am’monites, Children of Ammon, A people descended from Ben-ammi, the son of Lot by his younger daughter. (Genesis 19:38) comp Psal 83:7,8The Ammonites are frequently mentioned with the Moabites (descendants of Ben-ammi’s half-brother), and sometimes under the same name. Comp. (Judges 10:6; 2 Chronicles 20:1; Zephaniah 2:8) etc. The precise position of the territory of the Ammonites is not ascertainable. In the earliest mention of them, (2:20) they are said to have dwelt in their place, Jabbok being their border. (Numbers 21:24; 2:37; 3:16) (i.e. Land or country is, however, but rarely ascribed to them. Their capital city was Rabbath, called also Rabbath Ammon on the Jabbok. We find everywhere traces of the fierce habits of maranders in their incursions.) (1 Samuel 11:2; Amos 1:13) and a very high degree of crafty cruelty to their toes. (Jeremiah 41:6,7; Judges 17:11,12) Moab was the settled and civilized half of the nation of Lot, and Ammon formed its predatory and Bedouin section. On the west of Jordan they never obtained a footing. The hatred in which the Ammonites were held by Israel is stated to have arisen partly from their denial of assistance, (23:4) to the Israelites on their approach to Canaan. But whatever its origin the animosity continued in force to the latest date. The tribe was governed by a king, (Judges 11:12) etc.; (1 Samuel 12:12; 2 Samuel 10:1; Jeremiah 40:14) and by “princes.” (2 Samuel 10:3; 1 Chronicles 19:3) The divinity of the tribe was Molech [Molech], and they were gross idolaters.

places.name: 암비볼리
places.desc: 로마 에그나티아 가도를 따라 빌립보에서 데살로니가로 향하던 중 지나간 마게도냐 주요 도시
places.eastonKo: "양편의 성읍"이라는 뜻으로 마게도냐의 성읍이자 로마의 큰 군사 요충지다. 바울과 실라가 빌립보에서 데살로니가로 가는 길에 이곳을 지났으며 빌립보에서 로마 33마일 거리다(행 17:1).
places.smithKo: "바다에 둘러싸인 성읍"이라는 뜻으로 마게도냐의 성읍이며 바울과 실라가 빌립보에서 데살로니가로 가는 길에 지났다(행 17:1). 빌립보 남서쪽 로마 33마일, 바다에서 약 3마일 거리였다. 그 자리에는 지금 네오코리오라는 마을이 들어서 있다.
places.eastonEn: city on both sides, a Macedonian city, a great Roman military station, through which Paul and Silas passed on their way from Philippi to Thessalonica, a distance of 33 Roman miles from Philippi (Acts 17:1).
places.smithEn: (a city surrounded by the sea), a city of Macedonia, through which Paul and Silas passed on their way from Philippi to Thessalonica (Acts 17:1) It was distant 33 Roman miles from Philippi, to the southwest, and about three miles from the sea. Its site is now occupied by a village called Neokhorio ; in Turkish Jeni-Keni, or “New Town.”

places.name: 아납 (아낙 자손 멸절 성읍)
places.desc: 여호수아가 아낙 족속의 거인들을 진멸하고 취한 산지 성읍
places.eastonKo: "포도의 성읍"이라는 뜻으로 유다 산지의 성읍 중 하나이며 여호수아가 이곳에서 아낙 자손을 쫓아냈다(수 11:21; 15:50). 지금도 옛 이름을 그대로 지니고 있으며 헤브론 남남서쪽 10마일 산지에 있다.
places.smithKo: "포도의 성읍"이라는 뜻으로 유다 산지의 성읍이며(수 15:50) 드빌·헤브론과 함께 한때 아낙 자손에게 속했던 곳으로 언급된다(수 11:21).
places.eastonEn: grape-town, one of the cities in the mountains of Judah, from which Joshua expelled the Anakim (Joshua 11:21; 15:50). It still retains its ancient name. It lies among the hills, 10 miles south-south-west of Hebron.
places.smithEn: (grape-town), a town in the mountains of Judah, (Joshua 15:50) named with Debir and Hebron as once belonging to the Anakim. (Joshua 11:21)

places.name: 아나하라트
places.desc: 투트모세 3세 승전비에 기록된 잇사갈 평야 성읍
places.smithKo: "협곡 또는 고갯길"이라는 뜻으로 잇사갈 경계 안의 한 곳이며 시온·랍빗과 함께 언급된다(수 19:19).
places.smithEn: (gorge or pass), a place within the border of Issachar, named with Shihon and Rabbith. (Joshua 19:19)

places.name: 아나냐 (베냐민 귀환지)
places.desc: 예루살렘 북쪽 5km에 위치한 베냐민 포로 귀환자 성읍

places.eastonEn: protected by Jehovah, the name of a town in the tribe of Benjamin between Nob and Hazor (Nehemiah 11:32). It is probably the modern Beit Hanina, a small village 3 miles north of Jerusalem.
places.smithEn: a place, named between Nob and Hazor, in which the Benjamites lived after their return from captivity. (Nehemiah 11:32) (protected by Jehovah) probably a priest, and ancestor of Azariah, who assisted in rebuilding the city wall in the days of Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 3:23) (B.C. before 446.)

places.name: 아나돗 (예레미야 선지자 고향)
places.desc: 눈물의 선지자 예레미야의 제사장 가문 고향 성읍, 밭을 산 구속사적 상징지
places.eastonKo: 베냐민 지파에 속한 도피성 중 하나의 이름이다(수 21:18). 유대인들은 대체로 팔레스타인에서 발견한 성읍의 이름을 바꾸지 않았으므로, 이 성읍 이름은 여신 아낫에서 온 것으로 볼 수 있다.
places.smithKo: 베냐민 지파에 속한 제사장의 성읍으로 "들"이 딸려 있었다(수 21:18; 대상 6:60). 아나돗은 예루살렘에서 약 3마일 거리에 있었다(사 10:30). 제사장들이 일구던 자취가 지금도 곡식밭과 무화과·감람나무로 남아 있다.
places.eastonEn: the name of one of the cities of refuge, in the tribe of Benjamin (Joshua 21:18). The Jews, as a rule, did not change the names of the towns they found in Palestine; hence this town may be regarded as deriving its name from the goddess Anat. It was the native place of Abiezer, one of David’s “thirty” (2 Samuel 23:27), and of Jehu, another of his mighty men (1 Chronicles 12:3). It is chiefly notable, however, as the birth-place and usual residence of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 1:1; 11:21-23; 29:27; 32:7-9). It suffered greatly from the army of Sennacherib, and only 128 men returned to it from the Exile (Nehemiah 7:27; Ezra 2:23). It lay about 3 miles north of Jerusalem. It has been identified with the small and poor village of ‘Anata, containing about 100 inhabitants.
places.smithEn: a priests’ city belonging to the tribe of Benjamin, with “suburbs.” (Joshua 21:18; 1 Chronicles 6:60) Anathoth lay about three miles from Jerusalem. (Isaiah 10:30) The cultivation of the priests survives in tilled fields of grain, with figs and olives. There are the remains of walls and strong foundations, and the quarries still supply Jerusalem with building stones. (answers to prayer). • Son of Becher, a son of Benjamin. (1 Chronicles 7:8) • One of the “heads of the people” who signed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 10:19) (B.C. 410.)

places.smithKo: "두 샘"이라는 뜻으로 딸린 들과 함께 게르손 자손에게 속한 잇사갈의 성읍이다(대상 6:73).
places.eastonEn: two fountains, a Levitical city in the tribe of Issachar (1 Chronicles 6:73). It is also called En-gannim (q.v.) in Joshua 19:21; the modern Jenin.
places.smithEn: (two springs), a city of Issachar, with “suburbs,” belonging to the (Gershonites). (1 Chronicles 6:70)

places.eastonEn: a boy. (1.) A Canaanitish chief who joined his forces with those of Abraham in pursuit of Chedorlaomer (Genesis 14:13,24). (2.) A city of Manasseh given to the Levites of Kohath’s family (1 Chronicles 6:70).
places.smithEn: one of the three Amorite chiefs of Hebron who aided Abraham in the pursuit after the four invading kings. (Genesis 14:13,24) (boy), a city of Manasseh, west of Jordan, with “suburbs,” given to the Kohathites. (1 Chronicles 6:70)

places.name: 아님 (레위 성읍)
places.desc: 에스드모 동쪽에 위치한 유다 산지 성읍
places.eastonKo: "샘들"이라는 뜻으로 유다 산지의 성읍이며(수 15:50) 지금은 에스드모 근처, 헤브론 남서쪽 약 10마일의 엘 구웨인이다.

places.eastonEn: fountains, a city in the mountains of Judah (Joshua 15:50), now el-Ghuwein, near Eshtemoh, about 10 miles south-west of Hebron.
places.smithEn: (fountains), a city in the mountains of Judah, named with Eshtemoh and Goshen. (Joshua 15:50)

places.name: 수리아 안디옥 (베드로 동굴교회) (Antioch on the Orontes) 1

places.eastonEn: In Syria, on the river Orontes, about 16 miles from the Mediterranean, and some 300 miles north of Jerusalem. It was the metropolis of Syria, and afterwards became the capital of the Roman province in Asia. It ranked third, after Rome and Alexandria, in point of importance, of the cities of the Roman empire. It was called the “first city of the East.” Christianity was early introduced into it (Acts 11:19, 21, 24), and the name “Christian” was first applied here to its professors (Acts 11:26). It is intimately connected with the early history of the gospel (Acts 6:5; 11:19, 27, 28, 30; 12:25; 15:22-35; Galatians 2:11, 12). It was the great central point whence missionaries to the Gentiles were sent forth. It was the birth-place of the famous Christian father Chrysostom, who died A.D. 407. It bears the modern name of Antakia, and is now a miserable, decaying Turkish town. Like Philippi, it was raised to the rank of a Roman colony. Such colonies were ruled by “praetors” (R.V. marg., Acts 16:20, 21). (2.) In the extreme north of Pisidia; was visited by Paul and Barnabas on the first missionary journey (Acts 13:14). Here they found a synagogue and many proselytes. They met with great success in preaching the gospel, but the Jews stirred up a violent opposition against them, and they were obliged to leave the place. On his return, Paul again visited Antioch for the purpose of confirming the disciples (Acts 14:21). It has been identified with the modern Yalobatch, lying to the east of Ephesus.
places.smithEn: (from Antiochus)- • IN Syria. The capital of the Greek kings of Syria, and afterwards the residence of the Roman governors of the province which bore the same name. Situation .—This metropolis was situated where the chain of Lebanon, running northward, and the chain of Taurus, running eastward. are brought to an abrupt meeting. Here the Orontes breaks through the mountains; and Antioch was placed at a bend of the river, 16 1/2 miles from the Mediterranean, partly on an island, partly on the levee which forms the left bank, and partly on the steep and craggy ascent of Mount Silpius, which, rose abruptly on the south. It is about 300 miles north of Jerusalem. In the immediate neighborhood was Daphne the celebrated sanctuary of Apollo 2 Macc. 4:33; whence the city was sometimes called Antioch by Daphne, to distinguish it from other cities of the same name. Destruction .—The city was founded in the year 300 B.C., by Seleucus Nicator. It grew under the successive Seleucid kings till it became a city of great extent and of remarkable beauty. One feature, which seems to have been characteristic of the great Syrian cities,—a vast street with colonnades, intersecting the whole from end to end,—was added by Antiochus Epiphanes. By Pompey it was made a free city, and such it continued till the time of Antoninus Pius. The early emperors raised there some large and important structures, such as aqueducts, amphitheatres and baths. (Antioch, in Paul’s time, was the third city of the Roman empire, and contained over 200,000 inhabitants. Now it is a small, mean place of about 6000.—ED.) Bible History .—No city, after Jerusalem, is so intimately connected with the history of the apostolic church. Jews were settled there from the first in large numbers, were governed by their own ethnarch, and allowed to have the same political privileges with the Greeks. The chief interest of Antioch, however, is connected with the progress of Christianity among the heathen, Here the first Gentile church was founded, (Acts 11:20,21) here the disciples of Jesus Christ were first called Christians (Acts 11:26) It was from Antioch that St. Paul started on his three missionary journeys. • IN Pisidia, (Acts 13:14; 14:19,21; 2 Timothy 3:11) on the borders of Phrygia, corresponds to Yalobatch, which is distant from Aksher six hours over the mountains. This city, like the Syrian Antioch, was founded by Seleucus Nicator. Under the Romans it became a colonia, and was also called Caesarea.

places.smithEn: (from Antiochus)- • IN Syria. The capital of the Greek kings of Syria, and afterwards the residence of the Roman governors of the province which bore the same name. Situation .—This metropolis was situated where the chain of Lebanon, running northward, and the chain of Taurus, running eastward. are brought to an abrupt meeting. Here the Orontes breaks through the mountains; and Antioch was placed at a bend of the river, 16 1/2 miles from the Mediterranean, partly on an island, partly on the levee which forms the left bank, and partly on the steep and craggy ascent of Mount Silpius, which, rose abruptly on the south. It is about 300 miles north of Jerusalem. In the immediate neighborhood was Daphne the celebrated sanctuary of Apollo 2 Macc. 4:33; whence the city was sometimes called Antioch by Daphne, to distinguish it from other cities of the same name. Destruction .—The city was founded in the year 300 B.C., by Seleucus Nicator. It grew under the successive Seleucid kings till it became a city of great extent and of remarkable beauty. One feature, which seems to have been characteristic of the great Syrian cities,—a vast street with colonnades, intersecting the whole from end to end,—was added by Antiochus Epiphanes. By Pompey it was made a free city, and such it continued till the time of Antoninus Pius. The early emperors raised there some large and important structures, such as aqueducts, amphitheatres and baths. (Antioch, in Paul’s time, was the third city of the Roman empire, and contained over 200,000 inhabitants. Now it is a small, mean place of about 6000.—ED.) Bible History .—No city, after Jerusalem, is so intimately connected with the history of the apostolic church. Jews were settled there from the first in large numbers, were governed by their own ethnarch, and allowed to have the same political privileges with the Greeks. The chief interest of Antioch, however, is connected with the progress of Christianity among the heathen, Here the first Gentile church was founded, (Acts 11:20,21) here the disciples of Jesus Christ were first called Christians (Acts 11:26) It was from Antioch that St. Paul started on his three missionary journeys. • IN Pisidia, (Acts 13:14; 14:19,21; 2 Timothy 3:11) on the borders of Phrygia, corresponds to Yalobatch, which is distant from Aksher six hours over the mountains. This city, like the Syrian Antioch, was founded by Seleucus Nicator. Under the Romans it became a colonia, and was also called Caesarea.

places.name: 아벡 (북부 아셀 지파 / 레바논 국경) (Tel Afek) 1
places.desc: 아셀 지파가 쫓아내지 못하고 가나안 족속과 함께 거주했던 북부 평야 성읍
places.smithKo: "힘"이라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 여러 곳의 이름이다.
places.smithEn: (strength), the name of several places in Palestine. • A royal city of the Canaanites, the king of which was killed by Joshua, (Joshua 12:18) probably the same as Aphekahin (Joshua 15:53) • A city, apparently in the extreme north of Asher, (Joshua 19:30) from which the Canaanites were not ejected, (Judges 1:31) though here it is Aphik. This is probably the same place as APHEK, (Joshua 13:4) on the extreme north “border of the Amorites,”; identified with the Aphaca of classical times, the modern Afka . • A place at which the Philistines encamped while the Israelites pitched in Eben-ezer, before the fatal battle in which the sons of Eli were killed and the ark was taken. (1 Samuel 4:1) This would be somewhere to the northwest of and at no great distance from Jerusalem. • The scene of another encampment of the Philistines, before an encounter not less disastrous than that just named,—the defeat and death of Saul. (1 Samuel 29:1) It is possible that it may be the same place as the preceding. • A city on the military road from Syria to Israel. (1 Kings 20:26) It is now found in Fik, at the head of the Wady Fik, six miles east of the Sea of Galilee.
