places.name: 하로셋 하고임
places.desc: 갈릴리 서부의 성읍. 가나안 군대 장관 시스라의 본거지로, 드보라와 바락이 시스라를 패퇴시킨 전투와 관련된 곳이다.

places.name: 하스모나 (광야 숙영지)
places.desc: 밋가를 떠나 머물렀던 네게브 광야 남단 숙영지
places.eastonKo: "기름짐"이라는 뜻으로 이스라엘이 광야에서 유랑하는 동안 머문 서른 번째 진영이며 호르산에서 멀지 않다(민 33:29, 30).
places.smithKo: "기름짐"이라는 뜻으로 이스라엘의 진영 중 하나이며 모세롯 바로 앞으로 언급된다(민 33:29).
places.eastonEn: fatness, the thirtieth halting-place of the Israelites during their wanderings in the wilderness, not far from Mount Hor (Numbers 33:29, 30).
places.smithEn: (fatness), a station of the Israelites, mentioned (Numbers 33:29) as next before Moseroth.

places.name: 핫디
places.desc: 지역. 핫디에 언급된 지명

places.name: 하우란
places.desc: 요단 동편의 넓은 평원 지역. 에스겔의 성전 환상에서 이스라엘의 미래 경계로 언급된다.
places.eastonKo: "동굴의 땅"이라는 뜻으로 겔 47:16, 18에만 언급된다. 바산의 옛 구분 중 하나였으며 가울라니티스 곧 자울란 남동쪽, 레자 남쪽에 있어 아르논에서 히에로막스까지 뻗어 있었다.
places.smithKo: "동굴들"이라는 뜻으로 에스겔이 두 번 언급한 팔레스타인의 한 지방이다(겔 47:16, 17). 잘 알려진 그리스 지방 아우라니티스, 곧 갈릴리 바다 동쪽 사막 접경 빌립의 분봉 안에 있던 오늘날의 하우란과 같은 곳임이 거의 틀림없다.
places.eastonEn: cave-land, mentioned only in Ezekiel 47:16, 18. It was one of the ancient divisions of Bashan (q.v.), and lay on the south-east of Gaulanitis or the Jaulan, and on the south of Lejah, extending from the Arnon to the Hieromax. It was the most fertile region in Syria, and to this day abounds in the ruins of towns, many of which have stone doors and  massive walls. It retains its ancient name. It was known by the Greeks and Romans as “Auranitis.”
places.smithEn: (caverns), a province of Palestine twice mentioned by Ezekiel. (Ezekiel 47:16,17) There can be little doubt that it is identical with the well-known Greek province of Auranitis and the modern Hauran east of the Sea of Galilee, on the borders of the desert, in the tetrarchy of Philip.

places.name: 하윌라 (in Babylonia) 1
places.desc: 이스마엘 자손들이 정착한 애굽 앞 술까지 이르는 광대한 아라비아 지역
places.eastonKo: "모래 지역"이라는 뜻. (1) 창 2:11에 언급된 땅으로 금과 베델리엄과 호마노가 많았다. 이 지역의 위치를 두고는 매우 다양한 견해가 있다.
places.smithKo: (1) 에덴을 흐르는 비손강(아락세스)이 지나는 지역으로(창세기 2:11) 소아시아 북동쪽 모서리, 카스피해 근처 그리스 콜키스로 추정된다. (2) 아라비아 펠릭스의 한 지역으로(…
places.eastonEn: the sand region. (1.) A land mentioned in Genesis 2:11 rich in gold and bdellium and onyx stone. The question as to the locality of this region has given rise to a great diversity of opinion. It may perhaps be identified with the sandy tract which skirts Babylonia along the whole of its western border, stretching from the lower Euphrates to the mountains of Edom. (2.) A district in Arabia-Felix. It is uncertain whether the tribe gave its name to this region or derived its name from it, and whether it was originally a Cushite (Genesis 10:7) or a Joktanite tribe (10:29; comp. 25:18), or whether there were both a Cushite and a Joktanite Havilah. It is the opinion of Kalisch, however, that Havilah “in both instances designates the same country, extending at least from the Persian to the Arabian Gulf, and on account of its vast extent easily divided into two distinct parts.” This opinion may be well vindicated. (3.) One of the sons of Cush (Genesis 10:7). (4.) A son of Joktan (Genesis 10:29; 1 Chronicles 1:23).
places.smithEn: (Genesis 2:11) • A part of Eden through which flowed the river Pison (Araxes). It was probably the Grecian Colchis, in the northeast corner of Asia Minor, near the Caspian Sea. • A district in Arabia Felix, (Genesis 10:7) named from the second son of Cush; probably the district of Kualan, in the northwestern part of Yemen. (circle). • A son of Cush. (Genesis 10:7) • A son of Joktan. (Genesis 10:29)

places.name: 하윌라 (Arabian Peninsula) 2
places.desc: 이스마엘 자손들이 정착한 애굽 앞 술까지 이르는 광대한 아라비아 지역

places.name: 하봇야일 (야일의 60성읍)
places.desc: 므낫세의 아들 야일이 점령하여 자기 이름을 붙인 요단 동편 60개 요새 촌락
places.eastonKo: '빛을 비추는 자의 마을들'이라는 뜻으로, 요단강 동편 지역. (1.) 므낫세의 아들 야일이 길르앗의 몇몇 마을을 차지하여 이 이름을 붙였다(민수기 32:41). (2.) 야일이 '아르곱 지역 전체'를 차지했다고도 한다.
places.smithKo: '야일의 마을들'이라는 뜻으로 요단강 동쪽, 길르앗 또는 바산 지역의 마을들이며 므낫세의 아들 야일이 정복해 자신의 이름을 붙였다(민수기 32:41). 므낫세 기록에는 다른 지역들과 함께 60개 '성읍'을 이룬 것으로 계산되나 정확한 성읍 수에 대한 기록은 다소 혼란스러워 역대상 2:22에서는 23개, 사사기 10:4에서는 30개로 명시된다.
places.eastonEn: hamlets of the enlightener a district in the east of Jordan. (1.) Jair, the son of Manasseh, took some villages of Gilead and called them by this name (Numbers 32:41). (2.) Again, it is said that Jair “took all the tract of Argob,” and called it Bashanhavoth-jair (Deuteronomy 3:14). (See also Joshua 13:30; 1 Kings 4:13; 1 Chronicles 2:22, 23.)
places.smithEn: (villages of Jair), certain villages on the east of Jordan, in Gilead or Bashan, which were taken by Jair the son of Manasseh, and called after his name. (Numbers 32:41; 3:14) In the records of Manasseh in (Joshua 13:30) and 1Chr 2:23The Havoth-jair are reckoned with other districts as making up sixty “cities.” Comp. (1 Kings 4:13) There is apparently some confusion in these different statements as to what the sixty cities really consisted of. No less doubtful is the number of the Havoth-Jair. In (1 Chronicles 2:22) they are specified as twenty-three, but in (Judges 10:4) as thirty.

places.name: 하살앗달
places.eastonKo: '앗달의 마을'이라는 뜻으로, 팔레스타인 남쪽 경계, 가데스바네아 서쪽 광야의 한 장소(민수기 34:4). 여호수아 15:3에서는 아달이라 불린다.
places.smithKo: 하살(HAZER) 항목 참조.
places.eastonEn: village of Addar, a place in the southern boundary of Palestine (Numbers 34:4), in the desert to the west of Kadesh-barnea. It is called Adar in Joshua 15:3.
places.smithEn: etc. [Hazer]

places.name: 하살 에난
places.desc: 약속의 땅 북동쪽 경계점. 에스겔 이상 새 땅 경계. '샘들의 마을' 의미
places.eastonKo: "샘들의 마을"이라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 북동쪽 변경의 한 곳이다(민 34:9, 10). 안티레바논 중앙 산맥 한복판의 아얀 에드 다라로 비정하는 이들도 있으나, 다메섹 동북동쪽 약 60마일의 쿠리에테인으로 보는 편이 더 그럴듯하다.
places.eastonEn: village of fountains, a place on the north-east frontier of Palestine (Numbers 34:9, 10). Some have identified it with Ayan ed-Dara in the heart of the central chain of Anti-Libanus. More probably, however, it has been identified with Kuryetein, about 60 miles east-north-east of Damascus. (Comp. Ezekiel 47:17; 48:1.)

places.name: 하살갓다
places.desc: 유다 남부 네게브의 목축 정착지
places.eastonKo: "복의 마을"이라는 뜻으로 유다 남쪽 경계의 성읍이며(수 15:27) 지중해와 사해의 중간쯤에 있다.
places.eastonEn: village of fortune, a city on the south border of Judah (Joshua 15:27), midway between the Mediterranean and the Dead Sea.

places.name: 하살수알
places.desc: 여우의 뜰'이라 불린 시므온 지파 영지 성읍
places.eastonKo: "승냥이의 마을 또는 우리"라는 뜻으로 유다 남쪽 경계의 성읍이다(수 15:28; 느 11:27). 브엘세바와 몰라다의 중간쯤에 있는 사웨 폐허로 비정된다.
places.eastonEn: village or enclosure of the jackal, a city on the south border of Judah (Joshua 15:28; Nehemiah 11:27). It has been identified with the ruins of Saweh, half-way between Beersheba and Moladah.

places.name: 하살수사
places.desc: 현재 Khirbet esh Shamsaniyat. Sbalat Abu Susein. 수·대상에 언급
places.eastonKo: '말의 마을'이라는 뜻으로, 산산나와 같은 곳이며 솔로몬의 '병거성' 중 하나(여호수아 15:31; 역대하 1:14), 유다 남쪽 경계의 병참기지였다.
places.eastonEn: village of the horse, the same as Sansannah, one of Solomon’s “chariot cities” (Joshua 15:31; 2 Chronicles 1:14), a depot in the south border of Judah.

places.name: 하사손다말 (엔게디) (En Hazeva) 1
places.desc: 종려나무 성읍이라 불린 아모리 족속의 성읍 (엔게디 남부)

places.name: 하사손다말 (엔게디) (Ein Gedi) 2
places.desc: 종려나무 성읍이라 불린 아모리 족속의 성읍 (엔게디 남부)

places.name: 하세롯
places.desc: 미리암과 아론이 모세를 비방하다 미리암이 나병에 걸려 진영 밖에 갇혔던 곳
places.eastonKo: 울타리를 두른 곳으로, "낮은 돌담에 가시 돋친 아카시아 다발을 촘촘히 꽂아 얽힌 가지와 바늘 같은 가시가 진영 둘레에 도무지 뚫을 수 없는 울타리를 이룬" 형태다. 장막과 가축을 그 안에 두었다.
places.smithKo: "마을들"이라는 뜻(민 11:35; 12:16; 33:17; 신 1:1). 이스라엘이 광야에서 머문 진영으로, 시내산 북동쪽 40마일의 아랍어 지명 아인 후드헤라가 이곳일 수 있다.
places.eastonEn: fenced enclosures consisting of “a low wall of stones in which thick bundles of thorny acacia are inserted, the tangled branches and long needle-like spikes forming a perfectly impenetrable hedge around the encampment” of tents and cattle which they sheltered. Such like enclosures abound in the wilderness of Paran, which the Israelites entered after leaving Sinai (Numbers 11:35; 12:16; 33:17, 18). This third encampment of the Israelites has been identified with the modern ‘Ain el-Hudhera, some 40 miles north-east of Sinai. Here Miriam (q.v.), being displeased that Moses had married a Cushite wife (Numbers 12:1), induced Aaron to join with her in rebelling against Moses. God vindicated the authority of his “servant Moses,” and Miriam was smitten with leprosy. Moses interceded for her, and she was healed (Numbers 12:4-16). From this encampment the Israelites marched northward across the plateau of et-Tih, and at length reached KADESH.
places.smithEn: (villages), (Numbers 11:35; 12:16; 33:17; 1:1) a station of the Israelites in the desert, and perhaps recognizable in the Arabic Ain Hudhera, forty miles northeast of Sinai.

places.name: 하솔 (북부 가나안 맹주) (Tel Hazor) 1
places.desc: 야빈 왕이 이끄는 북부 가나안 연합군의 중심 수도, 여호수아가 불태운 성읍
places.eastonKo: "둘러싸인 곳, 요새"라는 뜻. (1) 메롬 호수 북쪽 산지에 있던 가나안의 요새(수 11:1-5). 야빈 왕이 동맹 부족들과 함께 이곳에서 여호수아와 큰 전투를 벌였다. 여호수아가 결정적 승리를 거두어 사실상 가나안 정복을 마무리했다(수 11:10-13).
places.smithKo: '성채'라는 뜻. (1) 정복 당시 납달리에 배정된 요새 성읍으로(여호수아 19:36) 메롬 호수를 내려다보는 고지대, 라마와 게데스 사이에 위치했던 것으로 보이며 야빈 왕의 성읍…
places.eastonEn: enclosed; fortified. (1.) A stronghold of the Canaanites in the mountains north of Lake Merom (Joshua 11:1-5). Jabin the king with his allied tribes here encountered Joshua in a great battle. Joshua gained a signal victory, which virtually completed his conquest of Canaan (11:10-13). This city was, however, afterwards rebuilt by the Canaanites, and was ruled by a king with the same hereditary name of Jabin. His army, under a noted leader of the name of Sisera, swept down upon the south, aiming at the complete subjugation of the country. This powerful army was met by the Israelites under Barak, who went forth by the advice of the prophetess Deborah. The result was one of the most remarkable victories for Israel recorded in the Old Testament (Joshua 19:36; Judges 4:2; 1 Samuel 12:9). The city of Hazor was taken and occupied by the Israelites. It was fortified by Solomon to defend the entrance into the kingdom from Syria and Assyria. When Tiglath-pileser, the Assyrian king, invaded the land, this was one of the first cities he captured, carrying its inhabitants captive into Assyria (2 Kings 15:29). It has been identified with Khurbet Harrah, 2 1/2 miles south-east of Kedesh. (2.) A city in the south of Judah (Joshua 15:23). The name here should probably be connected with the word following, Ithnan, HAZOR-ITHNAN instead of “Hazor and Ithnan.” (3.) A district in Arabia (Jeremiah 49:28-33), supposed by some to be Jetor, i.e., Ituraea. (4.) “Kerioth and Hezron” (Joshua 15: 25) should be “Kerioth-hezron” (as in the R.V.), the two names being joined together as the name of one place (e.g., like Kirjath-jearim), “the same is Hazor” (R.V.). This place has been identified with el-Kuryetein, and has been supposed to be the home of Judas Iscariot. (See KERIOTH.)
places.smithEn: (castle). • A fortified city, which on the occupation of the country was allotted to Naphtali. (Joshua 19:36) Its position was apparently between Ramah and Kedesh, ibid. (Joshua 12:19) on the high ground overlooking the Lake of Merom. There is no reason for supposing it a different place from that of which Jabin was king. (Joshua 11:1; Judges 4:2,17; 1 Samuel 12:9) It was the principal city of the whole of north Palestine. (Joshua 11:10) It was fortified by Solomon, (1 Kings 9:15) and its inhabitants were carried captive by Tiglath-pileser. (2 Kings 15:29) The most probable site of Hazor is Tell Khuraibeh . • One of the “cities” of Judah in the extreme south, named next in order to Kedesh. (Joshua 15:23) • Hazor-Hadattah = “new Hazor” another of the southern towns of Judah. (Joshua 15:25) • A place in which the Benjamites resided after their return from the captivity. (Nehemiah 11:33)

places.eastonEn: New Hazor, a city in the south of Judah (Joshua 15:25). It is probably identified with the ruins of el-Hazzarah, near Beit Jebrin.

places.name: 헤브론 (마므레 상수리 / 막벨라 굴)
places.modern: 알칼릴 막벨라 굴 (Cave of Patriarchs) (팔레스타인 서안)
places.desc: 아브라함이 단을 쌓은 곳, 사라·아브라함·이삭·리브가·야곱·레아가 묻힌 족장의 묘실
places.eastonKo: "공동체" 또는 "동맹"이라는 뜻. (1) 에스골 골짜기 남쪽 끝의 성읍으로 예루살렘과 브엘세바의 중간쯤, 직선거리로 약 20마일 떨어져 있다. "애굽 소안보다 칠 년 전에" 세워졌다(창 13:18; 민 13:22).
places.smithKo: (1) 고핫의 셋째 아들로(출애굽기 6:18) 헤브론 자손(또는 브네헤브론)의 조상이 되었다. (2) 유다의 성읍으로(여호수아 15:54) 산악 지대에 위치하며(여호수아 20:7)…
places.eastonEn: a community; alliance. (1.) A city in the south end of the valley of Eshcol, about midway between Jerusalem and Beersheba, from which it is distant about 20 miles in a straight line. It was built “seven years before Zoan in Egypt” (Genesis 13:18; Numbers 13:22). It still exists under the same name, and is one of the most ancient cities in the world. Its earlier name was Kirjath-arba (Genesis 23:2; Joshua 14:15; 15:3). But “Hebron would appear to have been the original name of the city, and it was not till after Abraham’s stay there that it received the name Kirjath-arba, who [i.e., Arba] was not the founder but the conqueror of the city, having led thither the tribe of the Anakim, to which he belonged. It retained this name till it came into the possession of Caleb, when the Israelites restored the original name Hebron” (Keil, Com.). The name of this city does not occur in any of the prophets or in the New Testament. It is found about forty times in the Old. It was the favorite home of Abraham. Here he pitched his tent under the oaks of Mamre, by which name it came afterwards to be known; and here Sarah died, and was buried in the cave of Machpelah (Genesis 23:17-20), which he bought from Ephron the Hittite. From this place the patriarch departed for Egypt by way of Beersheba (37:14; 46:1). It was taken by Joshua and given to Caleb (Joshua 10:36, 37; 12:10; 14:13). It became a Levitical city and a city of refuge (20:7; 21:11). When David became king of Judah this was his royal residence, and he resided here for seven and a half years (2 Samuel 5:5); and here he was anointed as king over all Israel (2 Samuel 2:1-4, 11; 1 Kings 2:11). It became the residence also of the rebellious Absalom (2 Samuel 15:10), who probably expected to find his chief support in the tribe of Judah, now called el-Khulil. In one part of the modern city is a great mosque, which is built over the grave of Machpelah. The first European who was permitted to enter this mosque was the Prince of Wales in 1862. It was also visited by the  Marquis of Bute in 1866, and by the late Emperor Frederick of Germany (then Crown-Prince of Prussia) in 1869. One of the largest oaks in Palestine is found in the valley of Eshcol, about 3 miles north of the town. It is supposed by some to be the tree under which Abraham pitched his tent, and is called “Abraham’s oak.” (See OAK.) (2.) The third son of Kohath the Levite (Exodus 6:18; 1 Chronicles 6:2, 18). (3.) 1 Chronicles 2:42, 43. (4.) A town in the north border of Asher (Joshua 19:28).
places.smithEn: (alliance). • The third son of Kohath, who was the second son of Levi. (Exodus 6:18; Numbers 3:19; 1 Chronicles 6:2,18; 23:12) He was the founder of a family of Hebronites, (Numbers 3:27; 26:58; 1 Chronicles 26:23,30,31), or Bene-Hebron. (1 Chronicles 15:9; 23:19) • A city of Judah, (Joshua 15:54) situated among the mountains, (Joshua 20:7) 20 Roman miles south of Jerusalem, and the same distance north of Beersheba. Hebron is one of the most ancient cities in the world still existing; and in this respect it is the rival of Damascus. It was a well-known town when Abraham entered Canaan, 3800 years ago. (Genesis 13:18) Its original name was Kirjath-arba, (Judges 1:10) “the city of Arba;” so called from Arba the father of Anak. (Joshua 15:13,14; 21:13) Sarah died at Hebron; and Abraham then bought from Ephron the Hittite the field and cave of Machpelah, to serve as a family tomb (Genesis 23:2-20) The cave is still there, and the massive walls of the Haram or mosque, within which it lies, form the most remarkable object in the whole city. Abraham is called by Mohammedans elKhulil, “the Friend,” i.e. of God, and this is the modern name of Hebron. Hebron now contains about 5000 inhabitants, of whom some fifty families are Jews. It is picturesquely situated in a narrow valley, surrounded by rocky hills. The valley runs from north to south; and the main quarter of the town, surmounted by the lofty walls of the venerable Haram, lies partly on the eastern slope. (Genesis 37:14) comp. Genesis23:19 About a mile from the town, up the valley, is one of the largest oak trees in Palestine. This, say some, is the very tree beneath which Abraham pitched his tent, and it still bears the name of the patriarch. • One of the towns in the territory of Asher, (Joshua 19:28) probably Ebdon or Abdom.

places.name: 헬람
places.desc: 요단 동편의 장소. 다윗이 아람 연합군을 격파한 전투 현장이다 (삼하 10:16-18).
places.eastonKo: "풍성한 곳"이라는 뜻으로 요단 동편, 유브라데 서편의 한 곳이다. 다윗이 소박이 거느린 수리아 군대를 크게 이긴 곳이다(삼하 10:16). 니케포리움 근처의 알라마타로 보는 이들도 있다.
places.smithKo: "요새"라는 뜻으로 요단 동편, 유브라데 서편의 한 곳이다. 하닷에셀이 수리아 사람들을 이곳에 모았고 다윗이 맞서 무찔렀다(삼하 10:16, 17).
places.eastonEn: place of abundance, a place on the east of Jordan and west of the Euphrates where David gained a great victory over the Syrian army (2 Samuel 10:16), which was under the command of Shobach. Some would identify it with Alamatta, near Nicephorium.
places.smithEn: (stronghold), a place east of the Jordan but west of the Euphrates at which the Syrians were collected by Hadarezer, and where David met and defeated them. (2 Samuel 10:16,17)

places.name: 헬바
places.eastonKo: '기름짐'이라는 뜻으로, 페니키아 평지에 있던 아셀 지파의 성읍(사사기 1:31).
places.smithKo: '비옥한'이라는 뜻으로 아셀 지파의 성읍이며 시돈에서 멀지 않은 페니키아 평지에 위치했던 것으로 보인다(사사기 1:31).
places.eastonEn: fatness, a town of the tribe of Asher (Judges 1:31), in the plain of Phoenicia.
places.smithEn: (fertile), a town of Asher, probably on the plain of Phoenicia not far from Sidon. (Judges 1:31)

places.name: 헬본 (다메섹 북서쪽 포도주 산지)
places.desc: 고대 왕실에 진상되던 최상급 포도주 산지이자 다메섹과 두로 무역의 중심 계곡
places.eastonKo: "기름지다" 곧 "비옥하다"는 뜻으로 겔 27:18에만 나온다. 두로의 큰 시장으로 포도주가 들어오던 곳이다.
places.smithKo: "비옥하다"는 뜻으로 겔 27:18에만 언급된다. 지리학자들은 지금까지 헬본을 아랍인이 할렙이라 부르는 알레포 성읍과 같은 곳으로 보아 왔다.
places.eastonEn: fat; i.e., “fertile”, (Ezekiel 27: 18 only), a place whence wine was brought to the great market of Tyre. It has been usually identified with the modern Aleppo, called Haleb by the native Arabs, but is more probably to be found in one of the villages in the Wady Helbon, which is celebrated for its grapes, on the east slope of Anti-Lebanon, north of the river Barada (Abana).
places.smithEn: (fertile), a place mentioned only in (Ezekiel 27:18) Geographers have hitherto represented Helbon as identical with the city of Aleppo, called Haleb by the Arabs; but there are strong reasons against this, and the ancient city must be identified with a village within a few miles of Damascus still bearing the ancient name Helbon, and still celebrated as producing the finest grapes in the country.

places.name: 헬렙
places.desc: 납달리 지파 영토의 경계 성읍. 여호수아 19장의 지파 분배에서 언급된다.
places.eastonKo: "바꿈"이라는 뜻으로 납달리 북쪽 경계의 성읍이다(수 19:33).
places.smithKo: "바꿈"이라는 뜻으로 납달리 지파의 경계가 시작되던 곳이다(수 19:33).
places.eastonEn: exchange, a city on the north border of Naphtali (Joshua 19:33).
places.smithEn: (exchange), the place from which the boundary of the tribe of Naphtali started. (Joshua 19:33)

places.name: 온 (헬리오폴리스 / 아스낫)
places.desc: 요셉의 아내 아스낫의 부친 제사장 보디베라가 섬기던 태양신 도시
places.eastonKo: "빛, 태양"이라는 뜻(창 41:45, 50)으로 태양 숭배의 큰 중심지였다. 벧세메스(렘 43:13), 아웬(겔 30:17)이라고도 불렸다. 나일 동안, 멤피스 북쪽 몇 마일 지점 카이로 북동쪽 부근에 있었다.
places.smithKo: "태양의 거처 또는 성읍"이라는 뜻으로 하애굽의 성읍이며 렘 43:13에서는 벧세메스라 불린다. 그리스어 이름 헬리오폴리스로 더 잘 알려져 있다. 나일강 펠루시아 갈래 동편, 삼각주 어귀 바로 아래, 멤피스 북동쪽 약 20마일에 있었다.
places.smithEn: [See On]

places.name: 헬갓 (레위 성읍)
places.desc: 기손 강변 아셀 지파 동남쪽 경계의 레위 성읍
places.eastonKo: "매끄러움"이라는 뜻으로 동쪽 경계에 있던 아셀의 성읍이며(수 19:25; 21:31) 훅곡이라고도 한다(대상 6:75).
places.eastonEn: smoothness, a town of Asher, on the east border (Joshua 19:25; 21:31); called also Hukok (1 Chronicles 6:75).

places.name: 헬갓핫수림 (기브온 24인 결투장)
places.desc: 요압의 부하 12명과 아브넬의 부하 12명이 서로 머리를 잡고 칼로 찔러 죽은 '날카로운 칼의 밭'
places.eastonKo: "날선 칼날의 밭" 또는 "용사의 밭"이라는 뜻이다(삼하 2:16). 사울과 그 집안에 참혹했던 길보아 전투 후, 다윗은 하나님의 지시대로 헤브론에 거처를 정하고 그곳에서 유다의 왕으로 기름 부음을 받았다.
places.smithKo: "바위의 밭"이라는 뜻으로 기브온 못 바로 곁으로 보이는 평평한 땅이다. 요압의 무리와 아브넬의 무리가 이곳에서 맞붙어 싸운 자들이 모두 죽었고 그 일로 큰 싸움이 벌어졌다(삼하 2:16).
places.eastonEn: plot of the sharp blades, or the field of heroes, (2 Samuel 2:16). After the battle of Gilboa, so fatal to Saul and his house, David, as divinely directed, took up his residence in Hebron, and was there anointed king over Judah. Among the fugitives from Gilboa was Ish-bosheth, the only surviving son of Saul, whom Abner, Saul’s uncle, took across the Jordan to Mahanaim, and there had him proclaimed king. Abner gathered all the forces at his command and marched to Gibeon, with the object of wresting Judah from David. Joab had the command of David’s army of trained men, who encamped on the south of the pool, which was on the east of the hill on which the town of Gibeon was built, while Abner’s army lay on the north of the pool. Abner proposed that the conflict should be decided by twelve young men engaging in personal combat on either side. So fiercely did they encounter each other that “they caught every man his fellow by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow’s side; so they fell down together: wherefore that place was called Helkath-hazzurim.” The combat of the champions was thus indecisive, and there followed a severe general engagement between the two armies, ending in the total rout of the Israelites under Abner. The general result of this  battle was that “David waxed stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul waxed weaker and weaker” (2 Samuel 3:1). (See GIBEON.)
places.smithEn: (field of rock), a smooth piece of ground, apparently close to the pool of Gibeon, where the combat took place between the two parties of Joab’s men and Abner’s men which ended in the death of the whole of the combatants, and brought on a general battle. (2 Samuel 2:16)

places.name: 헤나 & 아와
places.desc: 앗수르 왕에게 멸망당한 유프라테스 강변의 고대 도시들
places.eastonKo: 산헤립이 멸망시킨 메소포타미아의 성읍 중 하나(왕하 18:34; 19:13). 유브라데 우안에 있는 오늘날의 아나로 비정되며 스발와임에서 멀지 않다.
places.smithKo: "괴롭힘"이라는 뜻. 산헤립 시대 직전에 앗수르 왕들이 굴복시킨 성읍(왕하 19:13; 사 37:13). 십바라(지금의 모사이브)에서 멀지 않은 곳에 아나라는 옛 성읍이 있는데 헤나와 같은 곳일 수 있다. 유브라데 강가로 바벨론에서 20마일 거리다.
places.eastonEn: one of the cities of Mesopotamia destroyed by sennacherib (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13). It is identified with the modern Anah, lying on the right bank of the Euphrates, not far from Sepharvaim.
places.smithEn: (troubling), a city the Assyrian kings had reduced shortly before the time of Sennacherib. (2 Kings 19:13; Isaiah 37:13) At no great distance from Sippara (now Mosaib) is an ancient town called And or Anah, which may be the same as Hena. It is 20 miles from Babylon on the Euphrates.

places.name: 헤벨 (가나안 왕)
places.desc: 솔로몬의 제3행정관구 중심지이자 가나안 헤벨 왕의 도성
places.eastonKo: "우물 또는 시내"라는 뜻. (1) 여호수아가 점령한 가나안 왕도(수 12:17). (2) 길르앗의 막내아들(민 26:32; 27:1). (3) 아셀의 둘째 아들(대상 4:6). (4) 다윗의 용사 중 하나(대상 11:36).
places.smithKo: 정복된 왕들의 목록에 나오는 고대 가나안의 한 곳이다(수 12:17). 요단 서편에 있었다(수 12:7; 왕상 4:10 참조). "우물"이라는 뜻이다.
places.eastonEn: a well or stream. (1.) A royal city of the Canaanites taken by Joshua (12:17). (2.) The youngest son of Gilead (Numbers 26:32; 27:1). (3.) The second son of Asher (1 Chronicles 4:6). (4.) One of David’s heroes (1 Chronicles 11:36).
places.smithEn: a place in ancient Canaan which occurs in the lists of conquered kings. (Joshua 12:17) It was on the west of Jordan. Comp. (Joshua 12:7) and 1Kin 4:10 (a well). • The youngest of the sons of Gilead, (Numbers 26:32) and head of the family of the Hepherites. (B.C. before 1450.) • Son of Ashur, the “father of Tekoa.” (1 Chronicles 4:6) (B.C. about 1445.) • The Mecherathite, one of the heroes of David’s guard. (1 Chronicles 11:36) (B.C. 1046.)

places.name: 헤라클레오폴리스 마그나
places.desc: 성읍. 헤라클레오폴리스 마그나에 언급된 지명

places.name: 헤라클레오폴리스 파르바
places.desc: 성읍. 헤라클레오폴리스 파르바에 언급된 지명

places.name: 헤레스
places.eastonKo: '태양'이라는 뜻. (1.) '헤레스 산'(사사기 1:35), 히브리어 '하르헤레스', 곧 '태양의 산'; 아마도 여호수아 19:41의 이르세메스와 같은 곳일 것이다. (2.) 이…
places.smithKo: '태양'이라는 뜻으로(사사기 1:35) 아얄론 근처 에브라임 산지의 단 지파 성읍이며 이르세메스(태양의 성읍)와 동일한 곳일 가능성이 있다.
places.eastonEn: sun. (1.) “Mount Heres” (Judges 1:35), Hebrews Har-heres, i.e., “sun-mountain;” probably identical with Irshemesh in Joshua 19:41. (2.) Isaiah 19:18, marg. (See ON.)
places.smithEn: (the sun), (Judges 1:35) a city of Dan, in Mount Ephraim, near Ajalon; possibly identical with Mount Jearim (Ir-shemesh, city of the gun).

places.name: 헤롯 궁전
places.desc: 건물/구조물. 현재 Herod’s palace in Jerusalem. Herod’s palace in Jerusalem

places.name: 헤스본 (아모리 시혼의 수도)
places.desc: 아모리 왕 시혼의 수도, 이스라엘이 쳐서 정복하고 르우벤·갓 지파에 분배한 성읍
places.eastonKo: "명철"이라는 뜻으로 아모리 왕 시혼이 다스리던 성읍(수 3:10; 13:17). 모세가 점령했고(민 21:23-26) 후에 르우벤 지파에 속한 레위 성읍이 되었다(수 21:39; 민 32:37). 포로기 이후에는 모압이 차지했다(사 15:4).
places.smithKo: "요새"라는 뜻으로 아모리 왕 시혼의 수도(민 21:26). 높은 평원 미솔의 서쪽 경계(수 13:17), 곧 르우벤과 갓 지파의 경계선 위에 있었다.
places.eastonEn: intelligence, a city ruled over by Sihon, king of the Amorites (Joshua 3:10; 13:17). It was taken by Moses (Numbers 21:23-26), and became afterwards a Levitical city (Joshua 21:39) in the tribe of Reuben (Numbers 32:37). After the Exile it was taken possession of by the Moabites (Isaiah 15:4; Jeremiah 48:2, 34, 45). The ruins of this town are still seen about 20 miles east of Jordan from the north end of the Dead Sea. There are reservoirs in this district, which are probably the “fishpools” referred to in Cant. 7:4.
places.smithEn: (stronghold), the capital city of Sihon king of the Amorites. (Numbers 21:26) It stood on the western border of the high plain—Mishor, (Joshua 13:17)—and on the boundary line between the tribes of Reuben and Gad. The ruins of Hesban, 20 miles east of the Jordan, on the parallel of the northern end of the Dead Sea mark the site, as they bear the name; of the ancient Heshbon. There are many cisterns among the ruins. Comp. (Song of Solomon 7:4)

places.name: 헤스몬
places.desc: 유다 지파 서남단 애굽 시내 방면 성읍
places.eastonKo: "기름짐"이라는 뜻으로 유다 남부의 성읍이다(수 15:27).
places.smithKo: "기름진 땅"이라는 뜻으로 유다 최남단에 있던 곳으로 다른 성읍들과 함께 언급된다(수 15:27).
places.eastonEn: fatness, a town in the south of Judah (Joshua 15:27).
places.smithEn: (rich soil), a place named, with others, as lying in the extreme south of Judah. (Joshua 15:27)

places.name: 헤들론
places.eastonKo: '감싸인'이라는 뜻으로, 팔레스타인 북쪽 경계의 한 장소. '헤들론 길'(에스겔 47:15; 48:1)은 아마도 지중해에서 하맛(참조)의 큰 평지로 이어지는 레바논 끝의 고갯길, …
places.smithKo: '숨는 곳'이라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 북쪽 경계의 한 장소이다(에스겔 47:15). '헤들론으로 가는 길'은 레바논 북쪽 끝 고갯길로 추정되며 민수기 34:8의 '하맛 어귀'와 동일…
places.eastonEn: wrapped up, a place on the north border of Palestine. The “way of Hethlon” (Ezekiel 47:15; 48:1) is probably the pass at the end of Lebanon from the Mediterranean to the great plain of Hamath (q.v.), or the “entrance of Hamath.”
places.smithEn: (hiding-place), the name of a place on the northern border of Palestine. (Ezekiel 47:15; 48:1) In all probability the “way of Hethlon” is the pass at the northern end of Lebanon, and is thus identical with “the entrance of Hamath” in (Numbers 34:8) etc.

places.name: 헤스론 (게스론)
places.desc: 가룟 유다의 출신지 '그리욧'으로 추정되는 유다 남부 성읍
places.eastonKo: "둘러싸인 곳"이라는 뜻. (1) 르우벤의 아들 중 하나(창 46:9; 출 6:14). (2) 베레스의 두 아들 중 형(창 46:12). (3) 가데스 바네아 서쪽, 유다 남부의 평지(수 15:3).
places.smithKo: '벽으로 둘러싸인'이라는 뜻. (1) 르우벤의 아들(창세기 46:9). (2) 베레스의 아들(창세기 46:12).
places.eastonEn: enclosed. (1.) One of the sons of Reuben (Genesis 46:9; Exodus 6:14). (2.) The older of the two sons of Pharez (Genesis 46:12). (3.) A plain in the south of Judah, west of Kadesh-barnea (Joshua 15:3).
places.smithEn: (surrounded by a wall). • A son of Reuben. (Genesis 46:9; Exodus 6:14) • A son of Pharez. (Genesis 46:12; Ruth 4:18)

places.name: 히에라볼리 (파묵칼레)
places.desc: 뜨거운 온천수가 솟아나는 도시, 빌립 집사의 순교지 유적과 기념 성당이 있는 곳
places.eastonKo: "거룩한 성읍"이라는 뜻으로 브루기아의 성읍이며 에바브라가 돌보던 기독교 교회가 있었다(골 4:12, 13). 이 교회는 골로새 교회와 같은 때에 세워졌다.
places.smithKo: "거룩한 성읍"이라는 뜻으로 브루기아의 성읍이며 리쿠스강과 마이안드로스강이 만나는 곳 위, 골로새와 라오디게아 근처에 자리한다. 아마 에바브라가 세웠을 교회의 자리로 골 4:13에만 언급된다.
places.eastonEn: sacred city, a city of Phrygia, where was a Christian church under the care of Epaphras (Colossians 4:12, 13). This church was founded at the same time as that of Colosse. It now bears the name of Pambuk-Kalek, i.e., “Cotton Castle”, from the white appearance of the cliffs at the base of which the ruins are found.
places.smithEn: (holy city), a city of Phrygia, situated above the junction of the rivers Lycus and Maeander, near Colossae and Laodicea mentioned only in (Colossians 4:13) as the seat of a church probably founded by Epaphras.

places.name: 힐라꾸
places.desc: 지역. 힐라꾸에 언급된 지명

places.name: 호바 (다메섹 북편)
places.desc: 아브라함이 318명의 가신을 거느리고 조카 롯을 구출하기 위해 적을 추격한 북방 한계선
places.eastonKo: "숨는 곳"이라는 뜻으로 다메섹 북쪽의 한 곳이다. 아브라함이 그돌라오멜과 그 동맹을 이곳까지 추격했다(창 14:15).
places.smithKo: "숨는 곳"이라는 뜻으로 아브라함이 소돔을 노략한 왕들을 추격해 이른 곳이다(창 14:15). "다메섹 북쪽에" 있었다.
places.eastonEn: hiding-place, a place to the north of Damascus, to which Abraham pursued Chedorlaomer and his confederates (Genesis 14:15).
places.smithEn: (hiding-place), the place to which Abraham pursued the kings who had pillaged Sodom. (Genesis 14:15) It was situated “to the north of Damascus.”

places.name: 홀론 (레위 제사장 성읍) (Khirbet Alin) 1
places.desc: 아론 자손에게 분배된 유다 산지 도피성/레위 성읍
places.smithKo: '모래의'라는 뜻. (1) 유다 산악 지대의 성읍으로 드빌이 가장 두드러진 첫 그룹에 속한다(여호수아 15:51). (2) 모압의 성읍(예레미야 48:21)으로 아직 확인되지 않았…
places.smithEn: (sandy). • A town in the mountains of Judah. One of the first group, of which Debir was apparently the most considerable. (Joshua 15:51; 21:15) [Hilen] • A city of Moab. (Jeremiah 48:21) only. No identification of it has yet taken place.

places.name: 홀론 (레위 제사장 성읍) (in Moab 1) 2
places.desc: 아론 자손에게 분배된 유다 산지 도피성/레위 성읍
places.smithKo: '모래의'라는 뜻. (1) 유다 산악 지대의 성읍으로 드빌이 가장 두드러진 첫 그룹에 속한다(여호수아 15:51). (2) 모압의 성읍(예레미야 48:21)으로 아직 확인되지 않았…
places.smithEn: (sandy). • A town in the mountains of Judah. One of the first group, of which Debir was apparently the most considerable. (Joshua 15:51; 21:15) [Hilen] • A city of Moab. (Jeremiah 48:21) only. No identification of it has yet taken place.

places.name: 성소 1
places.desc: 성막/성전의 첫 번째 구역. 진설병·금 촛대·분향단이 있는 거룩한 공간. 제사장만 출입 가능한 하나님 임재의 장소
places.eastonKo: 성막이 나뉜 두 부분 중 하나(출애굽기 26:31; 37:17-25; 히브리서 9:2). 길이 20규빗, 높이와 너비 10규빗이었다. 빛이 들어올 창이 없어 금 등잔대로 밝혔다.
places.eastonEn: one of the two portions into which the tabernacle was divided (Exodus 26:31; 37:17-25; Hebrews 9:2). It was 20 cubits long and 10 in height and breadth. It was illuminated by the golden candlestick, as it had no opening to admit the light. It contained the table of showbread (Exodus 25:23-29) and the golden altar of incense (30:1-11). It was divided from the holy of holies by a veil of the most costly materials and the brightest colours. The arrangement of the temple (q.v.) was the same in this respect. In it the walls of hewn stone were wainscotted with cedar and overlaid with gold, and adorned with beautiful carvings. It was entered from the porch by folding doors overlaid with gold and richly embossed. Outside the holy place stood the great tank or “sea” of molten brass, supported by twelve oxen, three turned each way, capable of containing two thousand baths of water. Besides this there were ten lavers and the brazen altar of burnt sacrifice.

places.name: 성소 (Mount Moriah) 2
places.desc: 성막/성전의 첫 번째 구역(성소). 진설병·금 촛대·분향단이 있는 거룩한 공간
places.eastonKo: 성막이 나뉜 두 부분 중 하나(출애굽기 26:31; 37:17-25; 히브리서 9:2). 길이 20규빗, 높이와 너비 10규빗이었다. 빛이 들어올 창이 없어 금 등잔대로 밝혔다.
places.eastonEn: one of the two portions into which the tabernacle was divided (Exodus 26:31; 37:17-25; Hebrews 9:2). It was 20 cubits long and 10 in height and breadth. It was illuminated by the golden candlestick, as it had no opening to admit the light. It contained the table of showbread (Exodus 25:23-29) and the golden altar of incense (30:1-11). It was divided from the holy of holies by a veil of the most costly materials and the brightest colours. The arrangement of the temple (q.v.) was the same in this respect. In it the walls of hewn stone were wainscotted with cedar and overlaid with gold, and adorned with beautiful carvings. It was entered from the porch by folding doors overlaid with gold and richly embossed. Outside the holy place stood the great tank or “sea” of molten brass, supported by twelve oxen, three turned each way, capable of containing two thousand baths of water. Besides this there were ten lavers and the brazen altar of burnt sacrifice.

places.name: 호렘
places.desc: 상부 갈릴리 산지의 성읍
places.eastonKo: "구별된 곳"이라는 뜻으로 납달리의 견고한 성읍 중 하나다(수 19:38).
places.smithKo: "거룩하다"는 뜻으로 납달리 지경의 요새 중 하나이며 이론·믹달엘과 함께 언급된다(수 19:38). 반 데 벨데는 후라를 호렘의 자리로 제안한다.
places.eastonEn: consecrated, one of the fenced cities of Naphtali (Joshua 19:38).
places.smithEn: (sacred), one of the fortified places in the territory of Naphtali; named with Iron and Migdalel. (Joshua 19:38) Van Deuteronomy Velde suggests Hurah as the site of Horem.

places.name: 홀하깃갓 (굿고다)
places.desc: 골짜기와 시내가 흐르는 광야의 휴식 진영
places.smithKo: '눈에 띄는 산'이라는 뜻으로 이스라엘이 진 친 광야 진영지의 이름이며(민수기 33:32) 굿고다(신명기 10:7)와 같은 곳으로 추정된다.
places.smithEn: (conspicous mountain), the name of the desert station where the Israelites encamped, (Numbers 33:32) probably the same as Gudgodah. (10:7)

places.name: 호르마 (스밧)
places.modern: 텔 엘-말하타 / 텔 이라 (Tel Ira) (이스라엘 네게브)
places.desc: 초기 불순종 전투에서 패했던 곳, 후에 가나안 왕 아랏을 전멸시키고 '온전한 멸망(호르마)'을 선포한 성읍
places.eastonKo: "진멸에 붙임", 곧 "헤렘"으로 바쳐 온전히 멸하기로 정한다는 뜻이다.
places.smithKo: "황폐하게 된 곳"이라는 뜻으로 스밧이라고도 한다(삿 1:17). 팔레스타인 남쪽 가나안 부족 왕의 으뜸 성읍이었으나 여호수아에게 굴복해 유다 지경의 성읍이 되었고(수 15:30; 삼상 30:30) 실제로는 시므온에 속한 듯하다(대상 4:30).
places.eastonEn: banning; i.e., placing under a “ban,” or devoting to utter destruction. After the manifestation of God’s anger against the Israelites, on account of their rebellion and their murmurings when the spies returned to the camp at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Paran, with an evil report of the land, they quickly repented of their conduct, and presumed to go up “to the head of the mountain,” seeking to enter the Promised Land, but without the presence of the Lord, without the ark of the convenant, and without Moses. The Amalekites and the Canaanites came down and “smote and discomfited them even unto Hormah” (Numbers 14:45). This place, or perhaps the watch-tower commanding it, was originally called Zephath (Judges 1:17), the modern Sebaiteh. Afterwards (Numbers 21:1-3) Arad, the king of the Canaanites, at the close of the wanderings, when the Israelites were a second time encamped at Kadesh, “fought against them, and took some of them prisoners.” But Israel vowed a vow unto the Lord utterly to destroy the cities of the Canaanites; they “banned” them, and hence the place was now called Hormah. But this “ban” was not fully executed till the time of Joshua, who finally conquered the king of this district, so that the ancient name Zephath became “Hormah” (Joshua 12:14; Judges 1:17).
places.smithEn: (a place laid waste), or Zephath, (Judges 1:17) was the chief town of a king of a Canaanitish tribe on the south of Palestine, which was reduced by Joshua, and became a city of the territory of Judah, (Joshua 15:30; 1 Samuel 30:30) but apparently belonged to Simeon. (1 Chronicles 4:30)

places.name: 하소론 (모압 비탈길) (El Iraq) 1
places.desc: "호로나임 길에서 패망의 부르짖음이 들리도다" 눈물의 피난길 성읍
places.eastonKo: "두 동굴"이라는 뜻으로 아르논 남쪽 모압의 성읍이다. 높은 곳에 세워진 듯하며 제법 중요한 곳이었다(사 15:5; 렘 48:3, 5, 34).
places.smithKo: "두 동굴"이라는 뜻의 모압 성읍이며 성소였을 수 있다. 소알, 루힛과 함께 언급된다(사 15:5; 렘 48:3, 5, 34).
places.eastonEn: two caverns, a city of Moab to the south of the Arnon, built, apparently, upon an eminence, and a place of some importance (Isaiah 15:5; Jeremiah 48:3, 5, 34).
places.smithEn: (two caverns), a town of Moab, possibly a sanctuary, named with Zoar and Luhith. (Isaiah 15:5; Jeremiah 48:3,5,34)

places.name: 하소론 (모압 비탈길) (Beit Ur al Tahta) 2
places.desc: "호로나임 길에서 패망의 부르짖음이 들리도다" 눈물의 피난길 성읍
places.eastonKo: "두 동굴"이라는 뜻으로 아르논 남쪽 모압의 성읍이다. 높은 곳에 세워진 듯하며 제법 중요한 곳이었다(사 15:5; 렘 48:3, 5, 34).
places.smithKo: "두 동굴"이라는 뜻의 모압 성읍이며 성소였을 수 있다. 소알, 루힛과 함께 언급된다(사 15:5; 렘 48:3, 5, 34).
places.eastonEn: two caverns, a city of Moab to the south of the Arnon, built, apparently, upon an eminence, and a place of some importance (Isaiah 15:5; Jeremiah 48:3, 5, 34).
places.smithEn: (two caverns), a town of Moab, possibly a sanctuary, named with Zoar and Luhith. (Isaiah 15:5; Jeremiah 48:3,5,34)

places.name: 마문 (Horse Gate / 왕궁 기마대 출입문)
places.desc: 제사장들이 각기 자기 집과 마주 대한 곳을 중수한 왕궁 기마 성문
places.eastonKo: 예루살렘 성벽의 문 중 하나로 다리 서쪽 끝, 시온에서 성전으로 통하는 곳에 있었다(느 3:28; 렘 31:40).
places.eastonEn: a gate in the wall of Jerusalem, at the west end of the bridge, leading from Zion to the temple (Nehemiah 3:28; Jeremiah 31:40).

places.name: 호사 (두로 남쪽 관문)
places.desc: 섬 도시 두로의 본토 맞은편 담수원 요새 성읍
places.eastonKo: "피난처"라는 뜻. (1) 아셀 지파 경계의 한 곳으로 시돈 조금 남쪽에 있다(수 19:29). (2) 므라리 가문의 레위인(대상 16:38).
places.smithKo: 므라리 자손 레위인으로, 법궤가 예루살렘에 이른 뒤 다윗이 첫 문지기 중 하나로 세웠다(대상 16:38). 또한 "피난처"라는 뜻의 아셀 성읍이며(수 19:29) 두로로 이어지는 경계의 다음 표지다.
places.eastonEn: refuge. (1.) A place on the border of the tribe of Asher (Joshua 19:29), a little to the south of Zidon. (2.) A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chronicles 16:38).
places.smithEn: a Merarite Levite, chosen by David to be one of the first doorkeepers to the ark after its arrival in Jerusalem. (1 Chronicles 16:38) (B.C. 1014.) (refuge), a city of Asher, (Joshua 19:29) The next landmark on the boundary to Tyre.

places.name: 레바논 나무 궁
places.orig: House of the Forest of Lebanon

places.name: 훅곡
places.eastonKo: '정해진'이라는 뜻으로, 요단강에서 멀지 않은, 스불론 근처, 납달리 경계의 성읍(여호수아 19:34; 헬갓 항목 참조).
places.smithKo: '새겨진'이라는 뜻으로 납달리 경계의 한 장소이다(여호수아 19:34). 갈릴리 호수 상류 서쪽 납달리 산지의 야쿠크 마을로 확인되었다.
places.eastonEn: decreed, a town near Zebulun, not far from Jordan, on the border of Naphtali (Joshua 19:34). (See HELKATH.)
places.smithEn: (incised), a place on the boundary of Naphtali. (Joshua 19:34) It has been recovered in Yakuk, a village in the mountains of Naphtali west of the upper end of the Sea of Galilee.

places.name: 후곡
places.desc: 성읍. 대상6:75
places.eastonKo: '정해진'이라는 뜻으로, 요단강에서 멀지 않은, 스불론 근처, 납달리 경계의 성읍(여호수아 19:34; 헬갓 항목 참조).
places.smithKo: 역대상 6:75에서 헬갓을 잘못 쓴 이름이다. 헬갓(HELKATH) 항목 참조.
places.eastonEn: decreed, a town near Zebulun, not far from Jordan, on the border of Naphtali (Joshua 19:34). (See HELKATH.)
places.smithEn: a name which in (1 Chronicles 6:75) is erroneously used for HELKATH, which see.

places.name: 훔다
places.desc: 헤브론 인근 9성읍 중 하나
places.smithKo: "도마뱀의 곳"이라는 뜻으로 유다의 성읍 중 하나이며 산지 지역에서 헤브론 바로 다음에 나온다(수 15:54).
places.smithEn: (place of lizards), a city of Judah one of those in the mountain districts the next to Hebron. (Joshua 15:54)

places.name: 후사
places.desc: 유다 지파 영토의 성읍. 역대기의 족보에 등장하며, 다윗의 용사 중 한 명인 시브개의 출신지이다.
places.smithKo: "서두름"이라는 뜻으로 유다 지파의 족보에 나오는 이름이다(대상 4:4).
places.smithEn: (haste), a name which occurs in the genealogies of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:4)

places.name: 이블르암 (므낫세 속 성읍)
places.desc: 잇사갈 땅에 있었으나 므낫세에 속한 성읍, 거대한 지하 수로 터 발굴지
places.eastonKo: "백성을 삼키는 자"라는 뜻으로 므낫세에 배정된 성읍이나(수 17:11) 이스라엘이 가나안 사람을 쫓아내지 못했다(삿 1:27). 빌르암이라고도 한다(대상 6:70). 예닌 북쪽 2.5마일의 마을 젤라마로 보인다.
places.smithKo: "백성을 삼킴"이라는 뜻으로 딸린 마을과 성읍을 거느린 므낫세의 성읍이다(삿 1:27). 잇사갈이나 아셀 지경에 있었던 것으로 보인다.
places.eastonEn: people-waster, a city assigned to Manasseh (Joshua 17:11), from which the Israelites, however, could not expel the Canaanites (Judges 1:27). It is also called Bileam (1 Chronicles 6:70). It was probably the modern Jelamah, a village 2 1/2 miles north of Jenin.
places.smithEn: (devouring the people), a city of Manasseh, with villages or towns dependent on it. (Judges 1:27) It appears to have been situated in the territory of either Issachar or Asher. (Joshua 17:11) The ascent of Gur was “at Ibleam,” (2 Kings 9:27) somewhere near the present Jenin, probably to the north of it.

places.name: 이고니온
places.desc: 많은 유대인과 헬라인이 믿었으나 시기하는 자들이 돌로 치려 하여 피신한 갈라디아 도시
places.eastonKo: 고대 루가오니아의 수도. 바울의 1차 전도여행 때 비시디아 안디옥에서 바울과 바나바가 처음 방문했다(행 13:50, 51). 이곳에서 유대인들에게 박해를 받아 성읍에서 쫓겨나 루스드라로 피했다.
places.smithKo: "작은 형상"이라는 뜻으로 지금의 코니에이며 소아시아 루가오니아의 수도였다.
places.eastonEn: the capital of ancient Lycaonia. It was first visited by Paul and Barnabas from Antioch-in-Pisidia during the apostle’s first missionary journey (Acts 13:50, 51). Here they were persecuted by the Jews, and being driven from the city, they fled to Lystra. They afterwards returned to Iconium, and encouraged the church which had been founded there (14:21,22). It was probably again visited by Paul during his third missionary journey along with Silas (18:23). It is the modern Konieh, at the foot of Mount Taurus, about 120 miles inland from the Mediterranean.
places.smithEn: (little image), the modern Konieh, was the capital of Lycaonia, in Asia Minor. It was a large and rich city, 120 miles north from the Mediterranean Sea, at the foot of the Taurus mountains, and on the great line of communication between Ephesus and the western coast of the peninsula on one side, and Tarsus, Antioch and the Euphrates on the other. Iconium was a well-chosen place for missionary operations. (Acts 14:1,3,21,22; 16:1,2; 18:23) Paul’s first visit here was on his first circuit, in company with Barnabas; and on this occasion he approached it from Antioch in Pisidia, which lay to the west. The modern Konieh is between two and three miles in circumference and contains over 30,000 inhabitants. It contains manufactories of carpets and leather.

places.name: 이들라
places.desc: 나사렛 서쪽 스불론 산지 성읍
places.eastonKo: "올무"라는 뜻으로 보이며 스불론 서쪽 경계 부근의 성읍이다(수 19:15). 기손 골짜기의 오늘날 제이다로 비정된다.
places.smithKo: "하나님의 기념"이라는 뜻으로 스불론 지파의 성읍 중 하나이며 시므론과 베들레헴 사이에 이름이 나온다(수 19:15).
places.eastonEn: snares(?), a city near the west border of Zebulun (Joshua 19:15). It has been identified with the modern Jeida, in the valley of Kishon.
places.smithEn: (memorial of God), one of the cities of the tribe of Zebulun, named between Shimron and Bethlehem. (Joshua 19:15)

places.name: 이두매 (에돔 유대화 지역)
places.desc: 헤롯 대왕 가문의 출신지이자 예수님의 소문을 듣고 무리가 몰려온 남부 지역
places.smithKo: '붉은'이라는 뜻. 에돔(EDOM, IDUMAEA) 항목 참조.
places.smithEn: (red). [Edom, Idumaea Or Idumea]

places.name: 이임
places.desc: 유다 남단 아즈몬 인근의 국경 성읍
places.eastonKo: "폐허"라는 뜻. (1) 유다 남부의 성읍(수 15:29). (2) 이스라엘이 광야에서 머문 진영 중 하나(민 33:45).
places.smithKo: '폐허들'이라는 뜻. (1) 이예아바림의 축약형(민수기 33:45). (2) 유다 최남단의 성읍(여호수아 15:29).
places.eastonEn: ruins. (1.) A city in the south of Judah (Joshua 15:29). (2.) One of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Numbers 33:45).
places.smithEn: (ruins). • The partial or contracted form of the name IJE-ABARIM. (Numbers 33:45) • A town in the extreme south of Judah. (Joshua 16:29)

places.name: 이욘 (북단 국경 성읍)
places.desc: 벤하닷과 디글랏 빌레셀 3세가 침공하여 점령한 이스라엘 북단 계곡 성읍
places.eastonKo: "폐허"라는 뜻으로 납달리의 성읍이다. 아사의 청으로 수리아의 벤하닷이 점령했고(왕상 15:20), 후에 베가 때 앗수르의 디글랏빌레셀이 점령했다(왕하 15:29). 지금의 엘 키암이다.
places.smithKo: "폐허"라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 북부의 성읍이며 납달리 지파에 속했다. 벤하닷의 장관들에게 점령되어 노략당했고(왕상 15:20; 대하 16:4) 디글랏빌레셀에게 두 번째로 점령되었다.
places.eastonEn: a ruin, a city of Naphtali, captured by Ben-hadad of Syria at the instance of Asa (1 Kings 15:20), and afterwards by Tiglath-pileser of Assyria (2 Kings 15:29) in the reign of Pekah; now el-Khiam.
places.smithEn: (a ruin), a town in the north of Palestine, belonging to the tribe of Naphtali. It was taken and plundered by the captains of Ben-hadad, (1 Kings 15:20; 2 Chronicles 16:4) and a second time by Tiglath-pileser. (2 Kings 16:29) It was situated a few miles northwest of the site of Dan, in a fertile and beautiful little plain called Merj’ Ayun .

places.name: 일루리곤 (로마서 복음 전파 한계)
places.desc: "예루살렘으로부터 두루 행하여 일루리곤까지 그리스도의 복음을 편만하게 전하였노라"
places.eastonKo: 마게도냐 북서쪽, 아드리아해 동쪽 기슭의 나라다. 지금은 거의 전부가 달마디아에 포함되는데, 달마디아는 본래 일루리곤 남부에 붙은 이름이었다(딤후 4:10). 바울이 3차 전도여행 때 이곳을 두루 다녔다(롬 15:19).
places.smithKo: 아드리아해 동쪽 해안을 따라 뻗은 넓은 지역으로, 북쪽 이탈리아 경계에서 남쪽 에피루스까지 이르며 동쪽으로 모이시아·마게도냐와 맞닿는다(롬 15:19).
places.eastonEn: a country to the north-west of Macedonia, on the eastern shores of the Adriatic, now almost wholly comprehended in Dalmatia, a name formerly given to the southern part of Illyricum (2 Timothy 4:10). It was traversed by Paul in his third missionary journey (Romans 15:19). It was the farthest district he had reached in preaching the gospel of Christ. This reference to Illyricum is in harmony with Acts 20:2, inasmuch as the apostle’s journey over the parts of Macedonia would bring him to the borders of Illyricum.
places.smithEn: an extensive district lying along the eastern coast of the Adriatic, from the boundary of Italy on the north of Epirus on the south, and contiguous to Moessia and Macedonia on the east. (Romans 6:19)

places.name: 임멜
places.eastonKo: '말이 많은'이라는 뜻. (1.) 열여섯째 제사장 반열의 우두머리(역대상 24:14). (2.) 예레미야 20:1. (3.) 에스라 2:37; 느헤미야 7:40. (4.) 에스라 …
places.smithKo: '말 많은'이라는 뜻. (1) 중요한 제사장 가문의 창시자로(역대상 9:12) 성전 봉사 열여섯째 반차의 이름이 되었다(역대상 24:14). (2) 바벨론의 한 지명으로 보임(에스…
places.eastonEn: talkative. (1.) The head of the sixteenth priestly order (1 Chronicles 24:14). (2.) Jeremiah 20:1. (3.) Ezra 2:37; Nehemiah 7:40. (4.) Ezra 2:59; Nehemiah 7:61. (5.) The father of Zadok (Nehemiah 3:29).
places.smithEn: (talkative). • The founder of an important family of priests. (1 Chronicles 9:12; Nehemiah 11:13) This family had charge of, and gave its name to, the sixteenth course of the service. (1 Chronicles 24:14) (B.C. 1014.) • Apparently the name of a place in Babylonia. (Ezra 2:59; Nehemiah 7:61)

places.name: 인도 (힌두)
places.desc: 아하수에로(크세르크세스) 왕국의 동쪽 끝. 에스더서에서 페르시아 제국의 판도를 설명할 때 "인도에서 구스까지"로 언급된다.
places.eastonKo: 에 1:1과 8:9에만 나오며 파사 왕의 통치 범위를 서술하는 대목이다. 여기서 가리키는 나라는 힌두스탄 반도가 아니라 인더스강 일대인 펀자브다.
places.smithKo: 인도라는 이름은 에스더서 이전 성경에는 나오지 않는다. 에스더서에서 아하수에로 영토의 동쪽 한계로 언급되며, 서쪽 한계는 구스였다(에 1:1).
places.eastonEn: occurs only in Esther 1:1 and 8:9, where the extent of the dominion of the Persian king is described. The country so designated here is not the peninsula of Hindustan, but the country surrounding the Indus, the Punjab. The people and the products of India were well known to the Jews, who seem to have carried on an active trade with that country (Ezekiel 27:15, 24).
places.smithEn: The name of India does not occur in the Bible before the book of Esther where it is noticed as the limit of the territories of Ahasuerus in the east, as Ethiopia was in the west. (Esther 1:1; 8:9) The India of the book of Esther is not the peninsula of Hindostan, but the country surrounding the Indus, the Punjab and perhaps Scinde . The people and productions of that country must have been tolerably well known to the Jews. An active trade was carried on between India and western Asia. The trade opened by Solomon with Ophir through the Red Sea consisted chiefly of Indian articles.

places.name: 입다 (유다 평지)
places.desc: 유다 산지로 올라가는 골짜기 입구 성읍

places.name: 일나하스
places.desc: 성읍. 대상4:12
places.smithKo: '뱀의 성읍'이라는 뜻으로 다른 여러 지명들처럼 유다 족보 목록에 나온다(역대상 4:12).
places.smithEn: (serpent city), a name which, like many other names of places, occurs in the genealogical lists of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:12)

places.name: 이르브엘
places.smithKo: '하나님이 고치신다'는 뜻으로 베냐민 지파 성읍 중 하나이다(여호수아 18:27). 위치가 아직 밝혀지지 않았다.
places.smithEn: (God heals), one of the cities of Benjamin. (Joshua 18:27) No trace has yet been discovered of its situation.

places.name: 이르세메스 (벧세메스)
places.desc: 단 지파에 처음 할당된 소렉 골짜기 어귀 '태양의 성읍'
places.smithKo: "태양의 성읍"이라는 뜻으로 단 자손의 성읍이며(수 19:41) 아마 벧세메스와 같은 곳일 것이다.
places.smithEn: (city of the sun), a city of the Danites (Joshua 19:41) probably identical with Bethshemesh.

places.name: 이달리아
places.eastonKo: (사도행전 18:2; 27:1,6; 히브리서 13:24) 대부분의 지리적 명칭처럼 역사의 시기마다 다르게 쓰였다. 로마의 세력이 커지면서 여러 민족이 차례로 정복되어 편입되었다.
places.smithKo: 신약에서 당대의 일반적 의미, 곧 알프스와 메시나 해협 사이의 이탈리아 반도 전체를 지리적으로 가리키는 데 쓰인다(사도행전 18:2).
places.eastonEn: Acts 18:2; 27:1, 6; Hebrews 13:24), like most geographical names, was differently used at different periods of history. As the power of Rome advanced, nations were successively conquered and added to it till it came to designate the whole country to the south of the Alps. There was constant intercourse between Palestine and Italy in the time of the Romans.
places.smithEn: This word is used in the New Testament, (Acts 18:2; 27:1; Hebrews 13:24) in the usual sense of the period, i.e. in its true geographical sense, as denoting the whole natural peninsula between the Alps and the Straits of Messina.

places.name: 잇난
places.smithKo: '주어진'이라는 뜻으로 유다 최남단의 성읍 중 하나이다(여호수아 15:23). 아직 확인되지 않았다.
places.smithEn: (given), one of the towns in the extreme south of Judah. (Joshua 15:23) No trace of its existence has yet been discovered.

places.name: 이두래
places.desc: 지역. 눅3:1
places.eastonKo: 팔레스타인 북동쪽 지역으로, 인접한 트라코니티스와 함께 빌립의 분봉국을 이루었다(누가복음 3:1). 오늘날의 제두르가 이두래의 주요 부분을 차지한다.
places.smithKo: '예델의 땅'이라는 뜻으로 헤르몬산 기슭을 따라 있는 팔레스타인 북서쪽 경계의 작은 지방이며 누가복음 3:1에만 언급된다. 이스마엘의 아들 여둘이 이 지역에 정착해 이름을 남겼다(…
places.eastonEn: a district in the north-east of Palestine, forming, along with the adjacent territory of Trachonitis, the tetrarchy of Philip (Luke 3:1). The present Jedur comprehends the chief part of Ituraea. It is bounded on the east by Trachonitis, on the south by Gaulanitis, on the west by Hermon, and on the north by the plain of Damascus.
places.smithEn: (land of Jether), a small province on the northwestern border of Palestine, lying along the base of Mount Hermon, only mentioned in (Luke 3:1) Jetur the son of Ishmael gave his name like the rest of his brethren, to the little province he colonized. (Genesis 25:15,16) It adjoined Trachonitis, and lay along the base of Libanus between Tiberias and Damascus. At the place indicated is situated the modern province of Jedur, which is the Arabic form of the Hebrew Jetur

places.name: 헤나 & 아와
places.desc: 앗수르 왕에게 멸망당한 유프라테스 강변의 고대 도시들
places.eastonKo: 산헤립이 멸망시킨 메소포타미아의 성읍 중 하나(왕하 18:34; 19:13). 유브라데 우안에 있는 오늘날의 아나로 비정되며 스발와임에서 멀지 않다.
places.smithKo: "괴롭힘"이라는 뜻. 산헤립 시대 직전에 앗수르 왕들이 굴복시킨 성읍(왕하 19:13; 사 37:13). 십바라(지금의 모사이브)에서 멀지 않은 곳에 아나라는 옛 성읍이 있는데 헤나와 같은 곳일 수 있다. 유브라데 강가로 바벨론에서 20마일 거리다.
places.eastonEn: overturning, a city of the Assyrians, whence colonists were brought to Samaria (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13). It lay on the Euphrates,  between Sepharvaim and Henah, and is supposed by some to have been the Ahava of Ezra (8:15).
places.smithEn: (ruined), or A’va, which is mentioned in Scripture twice, (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13) comp. Isai 37:13In connection with Hena and Sepharvaim, and once, (2 Kings 17:24) in connection with Babylon and Cuthah, must be sought in Babylonia, and is probably identical with the modern Hit, on the Euphrates.

places.name: 이예아바림 (모압 앞 사막)
places.desc: 모압 동쪽 해 돋는 편 광야에 위치한 아바림 산지 앞 진영

places.name: 야복강
places.desc: 야곱이 하나님의 사자와 씨름한 강. 암몬·길르앗·모압 경계선. 야복='비우다' 어원
places.eastonKo: '쏟아냄' 또는 '씨름'이라는 뜻으로, 요단강 동편의 시내 중 하나로 갈릴리 바다와 사해 중간쯤, 곧 갈릴리 바다에서 약 45마일 아래 지점에서 요단강에 합류한다. 길르앗 산지 동…
places.smithKo: '비움'이라는 뜻으로 길르앗 산맥을 가로질러 갈릴리 호수와 사해 사이 중간 지점에서 동쪽으로 요단강에 합류하는 시내이다. 고대에는 암몬 자손의 경계였다(민수기 21:24). 얍복강…
places.eastonEn: a pouring out, or a wrestling, one of the streams on the east of Jordan, into which it falls about midway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, or about 45 miles below the Sea of Galilee. It rises on the eastern side of the mountains of Gilead, and runs a course of about 65 miles in a wild and deep ravine. It was the boundary between the territory of the Ammonites and that of Og, king of Bashan (Joshua 12:1-5; Numbers 21:24); also between the tribe of Reuben and the half tribe of Manasseh (21:24; Deuteronomy 3:16). In its course westward across the plains it passes more than once underground. “The scenery along its banks is probably the most picturesque in Palestine; and the ruins of town and village and fortress which stud the surrounding mountain-side render the country as interesting as it is beautiful.” This river is now called the Zerka, or blue river.
places.smithEn: (emptying), a stream which intersects the mountain range of Gilead, comp. (Joshua 12:2,5) and falls into the Jordan on the east about midway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea. It was anciently the border of the children of Ammon. (Numbers 21:24; 2:37; 3:16) It was on the south bank of the Jabbok that the interview took place between Jacob and Esau, (Genesis 32:22) and this river afterward became, toward its western part, the boundary between the kingdoms of Sihon and Og. (Joshua 12:2,5) Its modern name is Wady Zurka .

places.name: 야베스 길르앗
places.desc: 밤새 달려가 벧산 성벽에서 사울의 시신을 수습하여 장사지낸 의리 있는 용사들의 성읍
places.eastonKo: 요단 동편의 성읍으로 길르앗의 푸른 언덕 하나의 꼭대기에 있다. 므낫세 반 지파의 경계 안에 있으며 벧산이 한눈에 내려다보인다.
places.eastonEn: a town on the east of Jordan, on the top of one of the green hills of Gilead, within the limits of the half tribe of Manasseh, and in full view of Beth-shan. It is first mentioned in connection with the vengeance taken on its inhabitants because they had refused to come up to Mizpeh to take part with Israel against the tribe of Benjamin (Judges 21:8-14). After the battles at Gibeah, that tribe was almost extinguished, only six hundred men remaining. An expedition went against  Jabesh-Gilead, the whole of whose inhabitants were put to the sword, except four hundred maidens, whom they brought as prisoners and sent to “proclaim peace” to the Benjamites who had fled to the crag Rimmon. These captives were given to them as wives, that the tribe might be saved from extinction (Judges 21). This city was afterwards taken by Nahash, king of the Ammonites, but was delivered by Saul, the newly-elected king of Israel. In gratitude for this deliverance, forty years after this, the men of Jabesh-Gilead took down the bodies of Saul and of his three sons from the walls of Beth-shan, and after burning them, buried the bones under a tree near the city (1 Samuel 31:11-13). David thanked them for this act of piety (2 Samuel 2:4-6), and afterwards transferred the remains to the royal sepulchre (21:14). It is identified with the ruins of ed-Deir, about 6 miles south of Pella, on the north of the Wady Yabis.

places.name: 야베스
places.desc: 성읍. 대상2:55
places.eastonKo: '고통'이라는 뜻. (1.) 유다의 후손으로 '하나님이 그가 구한 것을 허락하셨다'고 기록된다(역대상 4:9,10). (2.) 서기관 여러 가문이 거주하던 장소(역대상 2:55).
places.smithKo: '슬픔'이라는 뜻. (1) 겐 족속 서기관 가문이 거주한 곳으로 보이는 장소(역대상 2:55). (2) 유다 족보, 베들레헴과 연관된 구절에 상세히 묘사된 인물(역대상 4:9).
places.eastonEn: affiction. (1.) A descendant of Judah, of whom it is recorded that “God granted him that which he requested” (1 Chronicles 4:9, 10). (2.) A place inhabited by several families of the scribes (1 Chronicles 2:55).
places.smithEn: (sorrow). • Apparently a place at which the families of the scribes resided who belonged to the families of the Kenites. (1 Chronicles 2:55) • The name occurs again in the genealogies of Judah, (1 Chronicles 4:9,10) in a passage of remarkable detail inserted in a genealogy again connected with Bethlehem. ver. 4.

places.name: 야브넬 (Yibna) 1
places.desc: 유다 지파 북서쪽 경계의 성읍. 블레셋 평야와 인접하며, 여호수아의 지파 분배에서 유다의 경계로 언급된다.
places.eastonKo: "하나님이 세우셨다"는 뜻. (1) 유다 북쪽 경계의 성읍(수 15:11)으로 후에 그리스인이 얌니아라 불렀으며 오늘날의 예브나로 야파 남쪽 11마일에 있다. 예루살렘이 무너진 뒤(주후 70년) 유대에서 손꼽히는 인구 많은 성읍이자 이름난 학교의 자리가 되었다.
places.smithKo: '하나님의 건축'이라는 뜻. (1) 유다 북쪽 경계 지표 중 하나로 바닷가에 가깝다(여호수아 15:11). 요세푸스는 이를 단 지파 소유로 본다. 훗날 블레셋 사람 손에 들어갔으나…
places.eastonEn: built by God. (1.) A town in the north boundary of Judah (Joshua 15:11), called afterwards by the Greeks Jamnia, the modern Yebna, 11 miles south of Jaffa. After the fall of Jerusalem (A.D. 70), it became one of the most populous cities of Judea, and the seat of a celebrated school. (2.) A town on the border of Naphtali (Joshua 19:33). Its later name was Kefr Yemmah, “the village by the sea,” on the south shore of Lake Merom.
places.smithEn: (building of God). • One of the points on the northern boundary of Judah, not quite at the sea, though near it. (Joshua 15:11) There is no sign, however, of its ever having been occupied by Judah. Josephus attributes it to the Danites. There was a constant struggle going on between that tribe and the Philistines for the possession of all the places in the lowland plains, and it is not surprising that the next time we meet with Jabneel it should be in the hands of the latter. (2 Chronicles 26:6) Uzziah dispossessed them of it and demolished its fortifications. Called also Jabneh. At the time of the fall of Jerusalem, Jabneh was one of the most populous places of Judea. The modern village of Yebna, more accurately Ibna, stands about two miles from the sea, on a slight eminence just south of the Nahr Rubin . • One of the landmarks on the boundary of Naphtali, (Joshua 19:33) in upper Galilee.

places.name: 얍느엘 (Tel Yin’am) 2
places.eastonKo: '하나님이 지으신'이라는 뜻. (1.) 유다 북쪽 경계의 성읍(여호수아 15:11)으로, 훗날 그리스인들은 얌니아라 불렀고 오늘날은 야파 남쪽 11마일의 예브나다. 예루살렘 멸망(…

places.name: 야굴
places.desc: 유다 지파 최남단 네게브 성읍
places.eastonKo: "머무는 곳"이라는 뜻으로 유다 남쪽 경계의 성읍이다(수 15:21).
places.smithKo: "묵는 곳"이라는 뜻으로 에돔 접경, 유다 최남단에 있던 성읍 중 하나다(수 15:21).
places.eastonEn: place of sojourn, a city on the southern border of Judah (Joshua 15:21).
places.smithEn: (lodging), a town of Judah, one of those farthest to the south, on the frontier of Edom. (Joshua 15:21)

places.name: 야하스 (아모리 시혼 격파지)
places.desc: 아모리 왕 시혼이 군대를 이끌고 나와 이스라엘과 대결하다 전멸당한 결전지
places.eastonKo: "짓밟힌 곳"이라는 뜻으로 야하사(수 13:18), 야사(수 21:36), 야사(대상 6:78)라고도 한다. 시혼이 패한 성읍으로 모압 경계, 요단 건너 암몬 땅, 아르논 북쪽에 있다(민 21:23; 신 2:32).
places.smithKo: '짓밟힌'이라는 뜻으로 흠정역에서 네 가지 형태로 표기된다. 이스라엘 자손과 아모리 왕 시혼 사이 결정적 전투가 벌어진 곳이며(민수기 21:23) 르우벤 지파 몫에 속했다(여호수아…
places.eastonEn: trodden down (called also Jahaza, Joshua 13:18; Jahazah, 21:36; Jahzah, 1 Chronicles 6:78), a town where Sihon was defeated, in the borders of Moab and in the land of the Ammonites beyond Jordan, and north of the river Arnon (Numbers 21:23; Deuteronomy 2:32). It was situated in the tribe of Reuben, and was assigned to the Merarite Levites (Joshua 13:18; 21:36). Here was fought the decisive battle in which Sihon (q.v.) was completely routed, and his territory (the modern Belka) came into the possession of Israel. This town is mentioned in the denunciations of the prophets against Moab (Isaiah 15:4; Jeremiah 48:34).
places.smithEn: (trodden down). Under these four forms is given in the Authorized Version the name of a place which in the Hebrew appears as Yahats and Yahtsah . At Jahaz the decisive battle was fought between the children of Israel and Sihon king of the Amorites. (Numbers 21:23; 2:32; Judges 11:20) It was in the allotment of Reuben. (Joshua 13:18) Like many others relating to the places east of the Dead Sea, the question of its site must await further research.

places.name: 야노아 (에브라임 동쪽 경계) (Khirbet Yanun) 1
places.desc: 세겜 동남쪽 요단 계곡으로 내려가는 에브라임 경계 성읍
places.eastonKo: 야노하라고도 하며 "안식"이라는 뜻. (1) 요단 계곡, 에브라임 북동쪽 경계의 성읍(수 16:6, 7). 나블루스 남동쪽 8마일의 오늘날 야눈으로 비정된다. (2) 납달리 경계 안 북부 팔레스타인의 성읍으로 앗수르 왕에게 점령되었다(왕하 15:29).
places.smithKo: "안식"이라는 뜻으로 갈릴리 북부 곧 "납달리 땅"에 있던 것으로 보인다. 디글랏빌레셀이 팔레스타인에 처음 침입했을 때 점령한 곳 중 하나다(왕하 15:29). 다른 곳에는 자취가 없다.
places.eastonEn: or Jano’hah, rest. (1.) A town on the north-eastern border of Ephraim, in the Jordan valley (Joshua 16:6, 7). Identified with the modern Yanun, 8 miles south-east of Nablus. (2.) A town of Northern Palestine, within the boundaries of Naphtali. It was taken by the king of Assyria (2 Kings 15:29).
places.smithEn: (rest), a place apparently in the north of Galilee, or the “land of Naphtali,”—one of those taken by Tiglath-pileser in his first incursion into Palestine. (2 Kings 15:29) No trace of it appears elsewhere.

places.name: 야노아 (에브라임 동쪽 경계) (Yanouh) 2
places.desc: 세겜 동남쪽 요단 계곡으로 내려가는 에브라임 경계 성읍
places.eastonKo: 야노하라고도 하며 "안식"이라는 뜻. (1) 요단 계곡, 에브라임 북동쪽 경계의 성읍(수 16:6, 7). 나블루스 남동쪽 8마일의 오늘날 야눈으로 비정된다. (2) 납달리 경계 안 북부 팔레스타인의 성읍으로 앗수르 왕에게 점령되었다(왕하 15:29).

places.name: 야누아
places.desc: 성읍. 야누아에 언급된 지명

places.name: 야비아 (나사렛 남서부)
places.desc: 나사렛 남서쪽 3km에 위치한 요새화된 갈릴리 성읍
places.eastonKo: "빛나다"는 뜻. (1) 여호수아를 대적하는 연합에 가담한 라기스 왕으로(수 10:3) 패해 죽임을 당했다. 아마르나 서판 하나에서는 자신을 게셀 왕이라 말한다. 호람이라고도 한다(수 10:33). (2) 예루살렘에서 태어난 다윗의 아들 중 하나(삼하 5:15).
places.smithKo: "빛나다"는 뜻. 스불론의 경계가 다브랏에서 야비아로 올라가고 거기서 가드헤벨로 지나갔다(수 19:12). 나사렛 남쪽 2마일의 야파가 야비아와 같은 곳일 가능성이 있다.
places.eastonEn: splendid. (1.) The king of Lachish, who joined in the confederacy against Joshua (Joshua 10:3), and was defeated and slain. In one of the Amarna tablets he speaks of himself as king of Gezer. Called also Horam (Joshua 10:33). (2.) One of the sons of David (2 Samuel 5:15), born in Jerusalem. (3.) A town in the southern boundary of Zebulum (Joshua 19:12); now Yafa, 2 miles south-west of Nazareth.
places.smithEn: (splendid). • King of Lachish at the time of the conquest of Canaan by the Israelites. (Joshua 10:3) (B.C. 1450.) • One of the sons of David born to him in Jerusalem. (2 Samuel 5:15; 1 Chronicles 3:7; 14:6) (B.C. 1046.) (splended) The boundary of Zebulun ascended from Daberath to Japhia, and thence passed to Gath-hepher. (Joshua 19:12) Yafa, two miles south of Nazareth, is not unlikely to be identical with Japhin.

places.name: 야르뭇 (가나안 남부 연합군 왕) (Tel Yarmuth) 1
places.desc: 아도니세덱과 함께 기브온을 치러 올라왔다가 막게다 굴에서 사형당한 왕의 성읍
places.eastonKo: "높음"이라는 뜻. (1) 유다 평지의 성읍으로(수 15:35) 본래 가나안 왕 하나가 거하던 곳이었다(수 10:3, 5, 23). 벧 지브린 북동쪽 약 7마일의 마을 야르무크로 비정된다. (2) 잇사갈 지파의 레위 성읍(수 21:29).
places.smithKo: '높은'이라는 뜻. (1) 유다 저지대의 성읍(여호수아 15:35). 그 왕 비람은 기브온을 벌하기 위해 동맹한 다섯 왕 중 하나로 벧호론에서 패해 막게다에서 여호수아에게 처형당했…
places.eastonEn: height. (1.) A town in the plain of Judah (Joshua 15:35), originally the residence of one of the Canaanitish kings (10:3, 5, 23). It has been identified with the modern Yarmuk, a village about 7 miles north-east of Beit-Jibrin. (2.) A Levitical city of the tribe of Issachar (Joshua 21:29), supposed by some to be the Ramah of Samuel (1 Samuel 19:22).
places.smithEn: (high). • A town in the low country of Judah. (Joshua 16:35) Its king, Piram, was one of the five who conspired. to punish Gibeon for having made alliance with Israel, (Joshua 10:3,5) and who were routed at Beth-horon and put to death by Joshua at Makkedah. ver. 33. Its site is probably the modern Yarmuk . • A city of Issachar allotted with its suburbs to the Gershonite Levites. (Joshua 21:29)

places.name: 야르뭇 (가나안 남부 연합군 왕) (Kokab el Hawa) 2
places.desc: 아도니세덱과 함께 기브온을 치러 올라왔다가 막게다 굴에서 사형당한 왕의 성읍

places.name: 얏딜 (다윗의 친구 성읍)
places.desc: 레위 제사장 성읍, 다윗이 망명 시절 은혜를 입고 전리품을 보낸 성읍
places.eastonKo: "뛰어나다"는 뜻으로 유다 산지의 성읍(수 15:48; 21:14).
places.smithKo: "뛰어나다"는 뜻으로 유다 산지 지역의 성읍이며(수 15:48) 소고·에스드모아 등과 같은 무리에 속한다(수 21:14; 삼상 30:27; 대상 6:57). 로빈슨은 몰라다 북쪽 6마일, 헤브론 남쪽 10마일의 아티르로 비정한다.
places.eastonEn: pre-eminent, a city in the mountains of Judah (Joshua 15:48; 21:14).
places.smithEn: (pre-eminent), a town of Judah in the mountain districts, (Joshua 15:48) one of the group containing Socho, Eshtemoa, etc. See also (Joshua 21:14; 1 Samuel 30:27; 1 Chronicles 6:57) By Robinson it is identified with ’Attir, six miles north of Molada and ten miles south of Hebron.

places.name: 야완 (그리스)
places.desc: 고대 이오니아(그리스)를 가리키는 히브리어 명칭. 야벳의 아들 야완의 후손이 거주한 곳으로, 다니엘서와 에스겔서에서 서방 세력의 상징으로 등장한다.
places.eastonKo: (1) 야벳의 넷째 "아들"(창 10:2)로 그 후손이 그리스 곧 이오니아에 정착했으며, 이오니아는 히브리어로 야완이라는 이름을 지닌다. 알렉산더 대왕은 "야완 왕"이라 불린다(단 8:21; 10:20; 슥 9:13 참조).
places.smithKo: '진흙'이라는 뜻. (1) 야벳의 아들(창세기 10:2)로 그리스 민족을 대표하는 인물로 여겨진다. 이 이름은 상업 활동이 활발했던 이오니아인들을 통해 페니키아인들이 아시아에 소개…
places.eastonEn: The fourth “son” of Japheth (Genesis 10:2), whose descendants settled in Greece, i.e., Ionia, which bears the name of Javan in Hebrew. Alexander the Great is called the “king of Javan” (rendered “Grecia,” Daniel 8:21; 10:20; comp. 11:2; Zechariah 9:13). This word was universally used by the nations of the East as the generic name of the Greek race. (2.) A town or district of Arabia Felix, from which the Syrians obtained iron, cassia, and calamus (Ezekiel 27:19).
places.smithEn: (clay). • A son of Japheth. (Genesis 10:2,4) Javan was regarded as the representative of the Greek race. The name was probably introduced into Asia by the Phoenicians, to whom the Ionians were naturally better known than any other of the Hellenic races, on account of their commercial activity and the high prosperity of their towns on the western coast of Asia Minor. • A town in the souther part of Arabia (Yemen), whither the Phoenicians traded. (Ezekiel 27:19)

places.name: 야셀 (길르앗 요새)
places.desc: 암몬 국경 지대의 울창한 삼림과 포도원 요새 성읍
places.eastonKo: '그(하나님)가 도우신다'는 뜻으로, 요단강 동편 아모리 사람의 성읍으로 길르앗의 이웃 지역들과 함께 갓 지파에 배정되었다(민수기 32:1,35). 므라리 계통 레위인에게 주어졌다(21:39).
places.smithKo: '여호와께서 도우신다'는 뜻. 야셀(JAAZER, OR JAZER) 항목 참조.
places.eastonEn: he (God) helps, a city of the Amorites on the east of Jordan, and assigned, with neighbouring places in Gilead, to Gad (Numbers 32:1, 35; Joshua 13:25). It was allotted to the Merarite Levites (21:39). In David’s time it was occupied by the Hebronites, i.e., the descendants of  Kohath (1 Chronicles 26:31). It is mentioned in the “burdens” proclaimed over Moab (Isaiah 16:8, 9; Jeremiah 48:32). Its site is marked by the modern ruin called Sar or Seir, about 10 miles west of Amman, and 12 from Heshbon. “The vineyards that once covered the hill-sides are gone; and the wild Bedawin from the eastern desert make cultivation of any kind impossible.”
places.smithEn: (Jehovah helps). [Jaazer, Or Jazer]

places.name: 여부스 (예루살렘)
places.desc: 다윗이 정복하기 전 여부스 족속의 요새 성읍 명칭
places.eastonKo: "단단히 밟힌 곳", "요새", 또는 "물 없는 언덕"이라는 뜻으로 시온산 위에 있던 가나안 성읍의 이름이다(수 15:8; 18:16, 28). 삿 19:10에서는 예루살렘과, 대상 11:4, 5에서는 다윗성과 같은 곳으로 밝혀진다.
places.smithKo: "타작마당"이라는 뜻으로 예루살렘의 이름 중 하나이며 여부스 사람의 성읍이다. 여부스 사람은 여부시라 불린다(수 15:8; 18:16, 28; 삿 19:10, 11; 대상 11:4, 5).
places.eastonEn: trodden hard, or fastness, or “the waterless hill”, the name of the Canaanitish city which stood on Mount Zion (Joshua 15:8; 18:16, 28). It is identified with Jerusalem (q.v.) in Judges 19:10, and with the castle or city of David (1 Chronicles 11:4,5). It was a place of great natural strength, and its capture was one of David’s most brilliant achievements (2 Samuel 5:8).
places.smithEn: (threshing-floor), one of the names of Jerusalem, the city of the Jebusites, are called Jebusi. (Joshua 15:8; 18:16,28; Judges 19:10,11; 1 Chronicles 11:4,5) [Jerusalem]

places.eastonEn: place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites (Joshua 3:16). Its site was near the ‘Ain es-Sultan, Elisha’s Fountain (2 Kings 2:19-22), about 5 miles west of Jordan. It was the most important city in the Jordan valley (Numbers 22:1; 34:15), and the strongest fortress in all the land of Canaan. It was the key to Western Palestine. This city was taken in a very remarkable manner by the Israelites (Joshua 6). God gave it into their hands. The city was “accursed” (Hebrews herem, “devoted” to Jehovah), and accordingly (Joshua 6:17; comp. Leviticus 27:28, 29; Deuteronomy 13:16) all the inhabitants and all the spoil of the city were to be destroyed, “only the silver, and the gold, and the vessels of brass and of iron” were reserved and “put into the treasury of the house of Jehovah” (Joshua 6:24; comp. Numbers 31:22, 23, 50-54). Only Rahab “and her father’s household, and all that she had,” were preserved from destruction, according to the promise of the spies (Joshua 2:14). In one of the Amarna tablets Adoni-zedec (q.v.) writes to the king of Egypt informing him that the ‘Abiri (Hebrews) had prevailed, and had taken the fortress of Jericho, and were plundering “all the king’s lands.” It would seem that the Egyptian troops had before this been withdrawn from Palestine. This city was given to the tribe of Benjamin (Joshua 18:21), and it was inhabited in the time of the Judges (Judges 3:13; 2 Samuel 10:5). It is not again mentioned till the time of David (2 Samuel 10:5). “Children of Jericho” were among the captives who returned under Zerubbabel Ezra 2:34; Nehemiah 7:36). Hiel (q.v.) the Bethelite attempted to make it once  more a fortified city (1 Kings 16:34). Between the beginning and the end of his undertaking all his children were cut off. In New Testament times Jericho stood some distance to the south-east of the ancient one, and near the opening of the valley of Achor. It was a rich and flourishing town, having a considerable trade, and celebrated for the palm trees which adorned the plain around. It was visited by our Lord on his last journey to Jerusalem. Here he gave sight to two blind men (Matthew 20:29-34; Mark 10:46-52), and brought salvation to the house of Zacchaeus the publican (Luke 19:2-10). The poor hamlet of er-Riha, the representative of modern Jericho, is situated some two miles farther to the east. It is in a ruinous condition, having been destroyed by the Turks in 1840. “The soil of the plain,” about the middle of which the ancient city stood, “is unsurpassed in fertility; there is abundance of water for irrigation, and many of the old aqueducts are almost perfect; yet nearly the whole plain is waste and desolate...The climate of Jericho is exceedingly hot and unhealthy. This is accounted for by the depression of the plain, which is about 1,200 feet below the level of the sea.” There were three different Jerichos, on three different sites, the Jericho of Joshua, the Jericho of Herod, and the Jericho of the Crusades. Er-Riha, the modern Jericho, dates from the time of the Crusades. Dr. Bliss has found in a hollow scooped out for some purpose or other near the foot of the biggest mound above the Sultan’s Spring specimens of Amorite or pre-Israelitish pottery precisely identical with what he had discovered on the site of ancient Lachish. He also traced in this place for a short distance a mud brick wall in situ, which he supposes to be the very wall that fell before the trumpets of Joshua. The wall is not far from the foot of the great precipice of Quarantania and its numerous caverns, and the spies of Joshua could easily have fled from the city and been speedily hidden in these fastnesses.
places.smithEn: (place of fragrance), a city of high antiquity, situated in a plain traversed by the Jordan, and exactly over against where that river was crossed by the Israelites under Joshua. (Joshua 3:16) It was five miles west of the Jordan and seven miles northwest of the Dead Sea. It had a king. Its walls were so considerable that houses were built upon them. ch. (Joshua 2:15) The spoil that was found in it betokened its affluence. Jericho is first mentioned as the city to which the two spies were sent by Joshua from Shittim. (Joshua 2:1-21) It was bestowed by him upon the tribe of Benjamin, ch. (Joshua 18:21) and from this time a long interval elapses before Jericho appears again upon the scene. Its second foundation under Hiel the Bethelite is recorded in (1 Kings 16:34) Once rebuilt, Jericho rose again slowly into consequence. In its immediate vicinity the sons of the prophets sought retirement from the world; Elisha “healed the spring of the waters;” and over against it, beyond Jordan, Elijah “went up by a whirlwind into heaven.” (2 Kings 2:1-22) In its plains Zedekiah fell into the hands of the Chaldeans. (2 Kings 25:5; Jeremiah 39:5) In the return under Zerubbabel the “children of Jericho,” 345 in number, are comprised. (Ezra 2:34; Nehemiah 7:36) Under Herod the Great it again became an important place. He fortified it and built a number of new palaces, which he named after his friends. If he did not make Jericho his habitual residence, he at last retired thither to die, and it was in the amphitheater of Jericho that the news of his death was announced to the assembled soldiers and people by Salome. Soon afterward the palace was burnt and the town plundered by one Simon, slave to Herod; but Archelaus rebuilt the former sumptuously, and founded a new town on the plain, that bore his own name; and, most important of all, diverted water from a village called Neaera to irrigate the plain which he had planted with palms. Thus Jericho was once more “a city of palms” when our Lord visited it. Here he restored sight to the blind. (Matthew 20:30; Mark 10:46; Luke 18:35) Here the descendant of Rahab did not disdain the hospitality of Zaccaeus the publican. Finally, between Jerusalem and Jericho was laid the scene of his story of the good Samaritan. The city was destroyed by Vespasian. The site of ancient (the first) Jericho is placed by Dr. Robinson in the immediate neighborhood of the fountain of Elisha; and that of the second (the city of the New Testament and of Josephus) at the opening of the Wady Kelt (Cherith), half an hour from the fountain. (The village identified with jericho lies a mile and a half from the ancient site, and is called Riha . It contains probably 200 inhabitants, indolent and licentious and about 40 houses. Dr. Olin says it is the “meanest and foulest village of Palestine;” yet the soil of the plain is of unsurpassed fertility.—ED.)

places.eastonEn: founded by God, a “desert” on the ascent from the valley of the Dead Sea towards Jerusalem. It lay beyond the wilderness of Tekoa, in the direction of Engedi (2 Chronicles 20:16, 20). It corresponds with the tract of country now called el-Hasasah.
places.smithEn: (founded by God), The wilderness of, the place in which Jehoshaphat was informed by Jahaziel the Levite that he should encounter the hordes of Ammon, Moab and the Mehunims. (2 Chronicles 20:16) The name has not been met with.
