places.name: 우스 (욥의 거주지 / 나홀 아들)
places.desc: 아람과 나홀의 아들 이름이자 의인 욥이 살던 광대한 동방 땅
places.eastonKo: "비옥한 땅"이라는 뜻. (1) 아람의 아들이자 셈의 손자(창 10:23; 대상 1:17). (2) 에돔 땅 호리 족장 중 하나(창 36:28). (3) 아브라함의 형제 나홀의 맏아들(창 22:21).
places.smithKo: '빛, 모래땅'이라는 뜻으로 나홀과 밀가의 맏아들이다(창세기 22:21).
places.eastonEn: fertile land. (1.) The son of Aram, and grandson of Shem (Genesis 10:23; 1 Chronicles 1:17). (2.) One of the Horite “dukes” in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:28). (3.) The eldest son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother (Genesis 22:21, R.V.).
places.smithEn: (light, sandy soil), the eldest son of Nahor and Milcah. (Genesis 22:21) (B.C. about 1900).

places.name: 우살
places.eastonKo: '방랑자'라는 뜻으로 욕단의 후손이며 아라비아 부족과 그 지역, 수도의 이름의 기원으로 추정된다(창세기 10:27).
places.smithKo: 욕단의 여섯째 아들로 그 정착지는 예멘의 수도 사나(원래 이름 아우잘)의 고대 이름에서 그 흔적을 찾을 수 있다(창세기 10:27).
places.eastonEn: a wanderer, a descendant of Joktan (Genesis 10:27; 1 Chronicles 1:21), the founder apparently of one of the Arab tribes; the name also probably of the province they occupied and of their chief city.
places.smithEn: (separate), the sixth son of Joktan, (Genesis 10:27; 1 Chronicles 1:21) whose settlements are clearly traced in the ancient name of San’a, the capital city of the Yemen (a district of Arabia), which was originally Awzal . From its position in the centre of the best portion of that kingdom it must always have been an important city. (San’a is situated about 150 miles from Aden and 100 miles from the coast of the Red Sea. It is one of the most imposing cities of Arabia -ED.)

places.name: 웃사 동산
places.eastonKo: '힘'이라는 뜻으로 므낫세와 아몬이 매장된 동산이며(열왕기하 21:18) 예루살렘 왕궁 근처였을 것으로 추정된다.
places.smithKo: 베냐민 지파 에훗의 후손, 므라리 계열 레위인, 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 느디님 가문, 또는 웃사(Uzzah)와 동일 인물을 가리킨다(역대상 8:7, 6:29; 에스라 2:49).
places.eastonEn: strengh, a garden in which Manasseh and Amon were buried (2 Kings 21:18, 26). It was probably near the king’s palace in Jerusalem, or may have formed part of the palace grounds. Manasseh may probably have acquired it from some one of this name.
places.smithEn: (strength). • A Benjamite of the sons of Ehud. (1 Chronicles 8:7) (B.C. 1445.) • Elsewhere called Uzza, Or Uzzah. (1 Chronicles 13:7,9,10,11) [Uzza, Or Uzzah] • The children of Uzza were a family of Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel. (Ezra 2:49; Nehemiah 7:51) (B.C. before 536.) • Properly Uzzah. As the text now stands, Uzzah is a descendant of Merari, (1 Chronicles 6:29) (14); but there appears to be a gap in the verse. Perhaps he is the same as Zina or Zizah the son of Shimei. (1 Chronicles 23:10,11) for these names evidently denote the same person, and, in Hebrew character, are not unlike Uzzah.

places.name: 웃센세에라
places.desc: 현재 Beit Ur al Tahta. within 5 km of Lower Beth-horon. 대상에 언급
places.eastonKo: 벧호론 근처로 추정되는 성읍으로 에브라임의 딸 이름을 따서 붙여졌다(역대상 7:24).
places.smithKo: 에브라임 사람 여인 세에라가 세운(또는 재건한) 성읍으로 아래·위 벧호론과 함께 언급된다(역대상 7:24).
places.eastonEn: a town probably near Beth-horon. It derived its name from the daughter of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:24).
places.smithEn: (ear (or point) of Sherah) a town founded or rebuilt by Sherah, an Ephraimite woman the daughter either of Ephraim himself or of Beriah. It is named only in (1 Chronicles 7:24) in connection with the two Beth-horons.

places.name: 골짜기 문 (힌놈 골짜기 방면)
places.modern: 힌놈 골짜기 방면 자파 게이트 남편 (예루살렘)
places.desc: 느헤미야가 밤에 나귀를 타고 나가 무너진 성벽을 시찰한 문

places.name: 아골 골짜기 (아간의 심판 돌무더기)
places.desc: 아간의 범죄로 돌에 맞은 곳, "아골 골짜기로 소망의 문을 삼아 주리라"
places.eastonKo: "괴로움"이라는 뜻으로 여리고 근처의 골짜기다. 아간의 죄가 이스라엘에 끼친 괴로움 때문에 그렇게 불렸다(수 7:24, 26). "아골 골짜기"라는 말은 괴로움을 일으키는 것을 가리키는 속담처럼 쓰이게 된 듯하다.

places.name: 아얄론 골짜기
places.desc: 골짜기. 수10:12

places.name: 아웬 골짜기
places.desc: 골짜기. 암1:5

places.name: 바가 골짜기 (눈물 골짜기)
places.desc: "눈물 골짜기로 지나갈 때에 그곳에 많은 샘이 있을 것이며" 시온 순례자의 길
places.smithKo: "울음"이라는 뜻으로 바가 골짜기는 팔레스타인의 한 골짜기다. 유배 중인 시인이 환상 중에, 시온의 여호와 성소를 향해 나아가는 순례자들이 이곳을 지나는 것을 본다(시 84:6). 이름 앞에 정관사가 쓰인 것으로 보아 실재하는 곳이었을 가능성이 매우 높다.

places.name: 브라가 골짜기
places.desc: 골짜기. 대하20:26

places.name: 결단의 골짜기
places.desc: 골짜기. 욜3:14

places.name: 엘라 골짜기 (다윗과 골리앗)
places.desc: 소년 다윗이 만군의 여호와의 이름으로 물맷돌을 던져 골리앗을 쓰러뜨린 결투장
places.eastonKo: "상수리나무"라는 뜻. (1) 다윗이 골리앗을 죽일 때 이스라엘이 진 치고 있던 골짜기다(삼상 17:2, 19). 유다의 소고와 아세가 근처에 있었다(삼상 17:1).

places.name: 에스콜 골짜기 (12정탐꾼 포도송이)
places.desc: 12정탐꾼이 두 사람이 막대기에 꿰어 멜 정도로 거대한 포도 한 송이를 베어 온 풍요로운 골짜기
places.eastonKo: "송이, 용맹함"이라는 뜻. (1) 그돌라오멜의 손에서 롯을 되찾을 때 아브라함과 함께한 젊은 아모리 족장(창 14:13, 24). (2) 정탐꾼들이 훌륭한 포도송이를 얻은 골짜기(민 13:23, 24).
places.smithKo: "포도송이"라는 뜻. 아모리 사람 마므레와 아넬의 형제이며, 롯을 끌고 간 네 왕을 추격할 때 아브라함과 동행한 이들 중 하나다(창 14:13, 24).

places.name: 기브온 골짜기
places.desc: 골짜기. 사28:21

places.name: 헤브론 골짜기
places.desc: 골짜기. 창37:14

places.name: 힌놈의 아들 골짜기 (도벳 / 게헨나)
places.desc: 자녀를 몰렉에게 불사르던 가증한 우상 산당, 요시야가 더럽히고 종말 지옥(게헨나)의 표상이 된 곳
places.eastonKo: 시온산과 이른바 "악한 모략의 언덕"을 가르는 깊고 좁은 협곡. "힌놈의 아들이라는 옛 인물"에게서 이름을 얻었다. 수 15:8에 처음 언급된다. 우상을 섬기던 유대인들이 이곳에서 자녀를 몰렉과 바알에게 산 채로 불살랐다.
places.smithKo: "애곡"이라는 뜻으로 "힌놈의 아들 골짜기"라고도 한다. 예루살렘 남쪽과 서쪽의 깊고 좁은 협곡으로 양쪽이 가파른 바위 벼랑이며, 북쪽 시온산을 "악한 모략의 언덕" 및 비스듬한 바위 고원과 갈라놓는다.

places.name: 입다엘 골짜기 (스불론 북부 경계)
places.desc: 스불론 지파와 아셀 지파의 경계를 가르는 비옥한 계곡. [이스턴/스미스 대조: 넷토파 평원과 지중해를 잇는 통로 계곡]

places.name: 여리고 골짜기
places.desc: 골짜기. 신34:3

places.name: 미스베 골짜기
places.desc: 골짜기. 수11:8

places.name: 르바임 골짜기
places.desc: 예루살렘 남서쪽 골짜기. 다윗이 블레셋을 두 번 대파한 곳(삼하5:18-22). 르바임 거인족이 살던 지역

places.name: 염곡 (소금 골짜기 / 다윗의 승전)
places.desc: 다윗과 요압이 에돔 사람 1만 8천 명을 쳐죽이고 수비대를 둔 승전 골짜기
places.eastonKo: 음식의 간을 맞추는 데 쓰였고(욥 6:6) 가축 여물에도 섞었다(사 30:24). 모든 소제에는 소금으로 간을 했다(레 2:13). 누구와 소금을 먹는다는 것은 그의 대접을 받고 그에게서 살아갈 것을 얻는다는 뜻이다.
places.smithKo: 소금은 우리에게도 없어서는 안 되지만 히브리인에게는 더욱 그러했다. 사람의 음식(욥 6:6)과 짐승의 먹이(사 30:24)에 입맛을 돋우는 양념이었고, 더운 기후가 고기에 미치는 영향을 막는 값진 방부제였으며, 그 밖에도 여러 쓰임이 있었다.

places.name: 사웨 골짜기 (왕의 골짜기)
places.desc: 아브라함이 그돌라오멜을 격파하고 돌아올 때 소돔 왕과 멜기세덱을 만난 골짜기
places.smithKo: "평지"라는 뜻으로 사웨 골짜기는 "왕의 골짜기"라 서술되며(창 14:17), 압살롬이 기둥을 세운 자리로 삼하 18:18에 다시 언급된다.

places.name: 소렉 골짜기 (들릴라의 집)
places.desc: 삼손이 들릴라를 사랑하여 머리털 비밀을 발설하고 힘을 잃게 된 포도 골짜기
places.eastonKo: "좋은 포도나무"라는 뜻으로 골짜기 곧 급류가 흐르는 골의 이름이다. 지금의 와디 수라르 곧 "비옥한 곳의 골짜기"로 유다 서편 산지의 물을 모아 막게다와 야브넬을 지나 욥바 남쪽 8마일쯤에서 바다로 흘러든다. 삼손이 사랑한 들릴라의 집이 있던 곳이다(삿 16:4).
places.smithKo: "붉다"는 뜻으로 소렉 골짜기는 들릴라가 살던 와디다(삿 16:4). 블레셋 주요 성읍 가운데 가사에 가장 가까웠을 수 있는데, 삼손이 들릴라의 집에서 붙잡힌 뒤 그곳으로 끌려갔기 때문이다.

places.name: 아르논 골짜기
places.desc: 사해 북쪽에서 유입되는 요단 동편의 주요 강. 이스라엘 영토의 남방 경계. 시혼 왕국의 남쪽 한계

places.name: 스보임 골짜기 (광야 하이에나 골짜기)
places.modern: 와디 아부 다바 (Wadi Abu Daba) (팔레스타인 서안)
places.desc: 믹마스 동쪽 광야로 내려가는 험준한 '하이에나 골짜기'
places.eastonKo: "노루" 또는 "사슴"이라는 뜻. (1) 소돔 "평지의 다섯 성읍" 중 하나로 대개 아드마와 짝지어 나온다(창 10:19; 14:2; 신 29:23; 호 11:8). 자기 왕(세메벨)이 있었으므로 제법 중요한 곳이었다. 다른 평지 성읍들과 함께 멸망했다.

places.name: 세렛 골짜기
places.desc: 골짜기. 민21:12

places.name: 와헙
places.desc: 광야 진영지. 민21:14

places.name: 예루살렘 수문 앞 광장
places.desc: 학사 에스라가 새벽부터 정오까지 율법책을 낭독하고 온 백성이 울며 회개한 부흥의 광장

places.name: 메롬 물가 (북부 가나안 결전)
places.modern: 메롬 호수 유역 / 훌라 계곡 (이스라엘 북부)
places.desc: 여호수아가 북부 가나안 연합군 철병거 군대를 기습하여 말 뒷발의 힘줄을 끊은 결전장

places.name: 홍해
places.modern: road between the Dead Sea and the Gulf of Aqaba

places.name: 서문
places.desc: 성문. 대상26:16

places.name: 시내 광야
places.desc: 홍해를 건넌 후 이스라엘이 1년간 머문 광야. 십계명과 율법을 받은 시내산이 있는 곳. 성막을 건립하고 장정을 계수한 곳

places.name: 십 광야 & 마온 광야
places.modern: 텔 지프 / 텔 마온 (Tel Zif) (팔레스타인 서안)
places.desc: 요나단과 마지막 언약을 맺은 수풀, 부유한 나발과 지혜로운 아비가일의 만남 무대
places.eastonKo: "흐르다"는 뜻. (1) 여할렐렐의 아들(대상 4:16). (2) 유다 남부의 성읍으로(수 15:24) 수파 고갯길에 있었던 것으로 보인다. (3) 유다 산지의 성읍으로(수 15:55) 헤브론 남동쪽 약 5마일의 사람이 살지 않는 폐허 텔 에즈 지프로 비정된다.
places.smithKo: "성가퀴"라는 뜻으로 유다의 두 성읍 이름이다.

places.name: 들염소 바위
places.desc: 자연 지역. 삼상24:2

places.name: 이론
places.desc: 상부 갈릴리 고원에 위치한 요새 성읍
places.eastonKo: 두발가인이 철을 다룬 첫 사람으로 언급된다(창 4:22). 애굽 사람은 출애굽 전에 시내에서 철을 다뤘다. 다윗이 성전을 위해 철을 넉넉히 예비했다(대상 22:3; 29:7). 단과 야완의 상인들이 두로 시장에 철을 들여왔다(겔 27:19).
places.smithKo: 놋과 함께 가장 먼저 알려진 금속으로 언급된다.
places.eastonEn: Tubal-Cain is the first-mentioned worker in iron (Genesis 4:22). The Egyptians wrought it at Sinai before the Exodus. David prepared it in great abundance for the temple (1 Chronicles 22:3: 29:7). The merchants of Dan and Javan brought it to the market of Tyre (Ezekiel 27:19). Various instruments are mentioned as made of iron (Deuteronomy 27:5; 19:5; Joshua 17:16, 18; 1 Samuel 17:7; 2 Samuel 12:31; 2 Kings 6:5, 6; 1 Chronicles 22:3; Isaiah 10:34). Figuratively, a yoke of iron (Deuteronomy 28:48) denotes hard service; a rod of iron (Psalm 2:9), a stern government; a pillar of iron (Jeremiah 1:18), a strong support; a furnace of iron (Deuteronomy 4:20), severe labour; a bar of iron (Job 40:18), strength; fetters of iron (Psalm 107:10), affliction; giving silver for iron (Isaiah 60:17), prosperity.
places.smithEn: is mentioned with brass as the earliest of known metals. (Genesis 4:22) The natural wealth in iron of the soil of Canaan is indicated by describing it as a land whose stones are iron.” (8:9) (Recent explorations have shown that iron ore is abundant in the northern part of Palestine.—ED.) The book of Job contains passages which indicate that iron was a metal well known. Sheet-iron was used for cooking utensils. (Ezekiel 4:3) cf. Levi 7:9 That it was plentiful in the time of David appears from (1 Chronicles 22:3) The market of Tyre was supplied with bright or polished iron by the merchants of by Dan and Javan. (Ezekiel 27:19) The Chalybes of the Pontus were celebrated as workers in iron in very ancient times. The product of their labor is supposed to be alluded to in (Jeremiah 16:12) as being of superior quality. Specimens of Assyrian ironwork overlaid with bronze were discovered by Mr. Layard, and are now in the British Museum. Iron weapons of various kinds were found at Nimroud, but fell to pieces on exposure to the air. (pious), one of the cities of Naphtali, (Joshua 19:38) hitherto totally unknown.

places.name: 사아난 (나오지 못한 성읍)
places.desc: "사아난 주민은 나오지 못하고 벧에셀이 애곡하여"
places.eastonKo: "양 떼의 곳"이라는 뜻으로 미 1:11에만 언급된다. 유다 평지의 스난과 같은 곳일 수 있다(수 15:37).
places.smithKo: 스난(Zenan) 항목을 보라.
places.eastonEn: place of flocks, mentioned only in Micah 1:11. It may be identified with Zenan, in the plain country of Judah (Joshua 15:37).
places.smithEn: [Zenan]

places.name: 사아난님 (헤벨의 장막 / 시스라 처단)
places.desc: 납달리 지파 경계 겐 사람 헤벨이 장막을 친 상수리나무, 야엘이 말뚝으로 시스라를 처단한 역사적 현장. [이스턴/스미스 대조: 다볼산 동쪽 고대 교통로 요충지]
places.eastonKo: 사아난님과 같은 곳이다(여호수아 19:33).
places.eastonEn: =Zaanaim, (Joshua 19:33).

places.name: 사일
places.desc: 성읍. 왕하8:21
places.eastonKo: '작은'이라는 뜻으로 사해 동쪽의 한 장소로 추정되며, 요람이 반역한 에돔 군대를 물리친 곳이다(열왕기하 8:21).
places.smithKo: 여호람의 에돔 원정 기사에 언급되는 곳으로 소알과 동일시하는 견해가 있다(열왕기하 8:21).
places.eastonEn: little, a place probably east of the Dead Sea, where Joram discomfited the host of Edom who had revolted from him (2 Kings 8:21).
places.smithEn: (small), a place named in (2 Kings 8:21) only, in the account of Joram’s expedition against the Edomites. It has been conjectured that Zair is identical with Zoar.

places.name: 살몬
places.eastonKo: (1) 다윗의 용사 중 하나로 아호아 사람으로 불리며 일래라고도 불린다(사무엘하 23:28). (2) 세겜 근처의 숲으로 아비멜렉과 그 부하들이 나뭇가지를 취해 세겜 요새를 불태운…
places.smithKo: 아호아 사람으로 다윗의 용사 중 하나다(사무엘하 23:28).
places.eastonEn: shady. (1.) One of David’s warriors, called the Ahohite (2 Samuel 23:28); called also Ilai (1 Chronicles 11:29). (2.) A wood near Shechem, from which Abimelech and his party brought boughs and “put them to the hold” of Shechem, “and set the hold on fire” (Judges 9:48). Probably the southern peak of Gerizim, now called Jebel Sulman. (See SALMON.)
places.smithEn: (shady), an Ahohite one of David’s guard. (2 Samuel 23:28)

places.name: 살모나
places.desc: 호르산을 떠나 에돔 땅을 우회하던 광야 여정지
places.eastonKo: "그늘지다"는 뜻으로 이스라엘이 광야에서 머문 진영 중 하나다(민 33:41, 42).
places.smithKo: "그늘지다"는 뜻으로 이스라엘의 광야 진영이며(민 33:41) 에돔 동편에 있다.
places.eastonEn: shady, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Numbers 33:41, 42).
places.smithEn: (shady), a desert station of the Israelites, (Numbers 33:41) lies on the east side of Edom.

places.name: 자노아 (평지 자노아) (Khirbet Zanu) 1
places.desc: 포로 귀환 때 주민들이 예루살렘 골짜기 문을 중수한 성읍
places.eastonKo: "습지"라는 뜻. (1) 유다 저지대 셰펠라의 성읍으로 소라 근처에 있다(수 15:34). 포로에서 돌아온 뒤 다시 거주했다(느 11:30). 예루살렘 서쪽 10마일 와디 이스마일의 자누아가 같은 자리일 것이다.
places.smithKo: 유다 지파 쉐펠라 지역의 성읍(여호수아 15:34), 또는 산지 지역의 성읍(여호수아 15:66)을 가리키며 역대상 족보에서는 여굿엘이 사노아의 아버지로 언급된다(역대상 4:18)…
places.eastonEn: marsh. (1.) A town in the low country or shephelah of Judah, near Zorah (Joshua 15:34). It was re-occupied after the return from the Captivity (Nehemiah 11:30). Zanu’ah in Wady Ismail, 10 miles west of Jerusalem, occupies probably the same site. (2.) A town in the hill country of Judah, some 10 miles to the south-west of Hebron (Joshua 15:56).
places.smithEn: (marsh). • A town of Judah in the Shefelah or plain, (Joshua 15:34; Nehemiah 3:13; 11:30) possibly identical with Zanu’a . • A town of Judah in the highland district, (Joshua 15:66) not improbably identical with Sanute, about 10 miles south of Hebron. • In the genealogical lists of the tribe of Judah in 1 Chron., Jekuthiel is said to have been the father of Zanoah. ch. (1 Chronicles 4:18) As Zanoah is the name of a town of Judah, this mention of Bithiah probably points to some colonization of the place by Egyptians or by Israelites directly from Egypt.

places.name: 자노아 (평지 자노아) (Khirbet Beit Amra) 2
places.desc: 포로 귀환 때 주민들이 예루살렘 골짜기 문을 중수한 성읍

places.name: 사본 (숙곳 북편) (Tell es Sa’idiyeh) 1
places.desc: 입다 시대 에브라임 사람들이 시비하러 건너왔던 갓 지파 성읍
places.smithKo: "북쪽"이라는 뜻으로 갓 지파의 기업을 열거하는 데 언급된 곳이다(수 13:27).
places.smithEn: (north), a place mentioned in the enumeration of the allotment of the tribe of Gad. (Joshua 13:27)

places.name: 사본 (숙곳 북편) (Jebel Aqra) 2
places.desc: 입다 시대 에브라임 사람들이 시비하러 건너왔던 갓 지파 성읍
places.smithKo: "북쪽"이라는 뜻으로 갓 지파의 기업을 열거하는 데 언급된 곳이다(수 13:27).
places.smithEn: (north), a place mentioned in the enumeration of the allotment of the tribe of Gad. (Joshua 13:27)

places.name: 사르밧 (사렙다)
places.desc: 엘리야가 머물며 가뭄 중 기름병과 가루통이 마르지 않고 과부 아들을 살린 해변 마을
places.eastonKo: "제련소" 곧 "금속을 정련하고 녹이는 작업장"이라는 뜻이다. 지금은 수라펜드라 불리는 작은 페니키아 성읍으로 해안에서 약 1마일 거리, 두로와 시돈 사이 길의 거의 중간에 있다.
places.smithKo: "제련하는 곳"이라는 뜻. 가뭄 후반부에 선지자 엘리야가 머문 곳이다(왕상 17:9, 10). 시돈에 가깝거나 시돈에 딸린 곳이었다. 오늘날의 마을 수라펜드에 해당하며 옛 성읍의 자취가 제법 남아 있다.
places.eastonEn: smelting-shop, “a workshop for the refining and smelting of metals”, a small Phoenician town, now Surafend, about a mile from the coast, almost midway on the road between Tyre and Sidon. Here Elijah sojourned with a poor widow during the “great famine,” when the “heaven was shut up three years and six months” (Luke 4:26; 1 Kings 17:10). It is called Sarepta in the New Testament (Luke 4:26).
places.smithEn: (smelting place), the residence of the prophet Elijah during the latter part of the drought. (1 Kings 17:9,10) It was near to, or dependent on, Zidon. It is represented by the modern village of Sura-fend . Of the old town considerable indications remain. One group of foundations is on a headland called Ain el-Kanatarah ; but the chief remains are south of this, and extend for a mile or more, with many fragments of columns, slabs and other architectural features. In the New Testament Zarephath appears under the Greek form of Sarepta. (Luke 4:26)

places.name: 사레다 (사르단)
places.desc: 솔로몬 성전 청동기구 주조 장소. 요단 계곡 도자기 흙 산지. 숙곳과 사레다 사이
places.eastonKo: 이스라엘이 요단강을 건널 때 물이 멈춰 쌓인 지점 근처의 성읍으로, '사르단 곁 아담 성읍'이라 불렸다(여호수아 3:16).
places.eastonEn: When the Hebrews crossed the Jordan, as soon as the feet of the priests were dipped in the water, the flow of the stream was arrested. The point of arrest was the “city of Adam beside Zaretan,” probably near  Succoth, at the mouth of the Jabbok, some 30 miles up the river from where the people were encamped. There the water “stood and rose upon an heap.” Thus the whole space of 30 miles of the river-bed was dry, that the tribes might pass over (Joshua 3:16, 17; comp. Psalm 104:3).

places.name: 스보임
places.desc: "내가 어찌 너를 스보임 같이 두겠느냐" 소돔과 함께 멸망한 성읍
places.eastonKo: '가젤들' 또는 '노루들'이라는 뜻. (1) 소돔 평지의 '다섯 성읍' 중 하나로 아드마와 함께 언급되며 자체 왕(스메벨)이 있었으나 다른 성읍들과 함께 멸망했다(창세기 10:19). (2) 베냐민 기브아 근처의 골짜기(사무엘상 13:18). (3) 포로 후 베냐민 사람들이 거주한 곳(느헤미야 11:34).
places.smithKo: 요단 평야 다섯 성읍 중 하나로 아드마와 함께 자주 언급된다(창세기 10:19, 14:2,8). 또한 믹마스 동쪽에 위치한 것으로 보이는 스보임 골짜기도 있다(사무엘상 13:18).
places.eastonEn: gazelles or roes. (1.) One of the “five cities of the plain” of Sodom, generally coupled with Admah (Genesis 10:19; 14:2; Deuteronomy 29:23; Hos. 11:8). It had a king of its own (Shemeber), and was therefore a place of some importance. It was destroyed along with the other cities of the plain. (2.) A valley or rugged glen somewhere near Gibeah in Benjamin (1 Samuel 13:18). It was probably the ravine now bearing the name Wady Shakh-ed-Dub’a, or “ravine of the hyena,” north of Jericho. (3.) A place mentioned only in Nehemiah 11:34, inhabited by the Benjamites after the Captivity.
places.smithEn: (gazelles). • One of the five cities of the “plain” or circle of Jordan. It is mentioned in (Genesis 10:19; 14:2,8; 29:23; Hosea 11:8) in each, of which passages it is either coupled with Admah or placed next it in the lists—perhaps represented by Talaa Sebaan, a name attached to extensive ruins on the high ground between the Dead Sea and Kerak . In (Genesis 14:2,8) the name is given more correctly in the Authorized Version ZEBOIIM. • The valley of Zeboim, a ravine or gorge, apparently east of Michmash, mentioned only in (1 Samuel 13:18) The road running from Michmash to the east is specified as “the road of the border that looketh to the ravine of Zeboim toward the wilderness.” The wilderness is no doubt the district of uncultivated mountain tops and sides which lies between the central district of Benjamin and the Jordan valley. In that very district there is a wild gorge bearing the name of Shuk ed-Dubba’, ravine of the hyena, “the exact equivalent of Ge hat-tsebo’im .

places.name: 스닷
places.desc: 가나안 북쪽 경계의 지점. 민수기 34장과 에스겔 47장에서 약속의 땅 경계 설정에 사용된다.
places.eastonKo: "옆, 비탈진 곳"이라는 뜻으로 하맛 근처 팔레스타인 북부의 성읍이다(민 34:8; 겔 47:15). 에메사(홈스)와 바알벡 사이의 수두드 폐허로 비정되나 확실하지는 않다.
places.smithKo: "산비탈"이라는 뜻. 모세가 약속한 이스라엘 땅 북쪽 경계의 표지 중 하나이며(민 34:8) 에스겔이 회복한 경계에도 나온다.
places.eastonEn: side; sloping place, a town in the north of Palestine, near Hamath (Numbers 34:8; Ezekiel 47:15). It has been identified with the ruins of Sudud, between Emesa (Hums) and Baalbec, but that is uncertain.
places.smithEn: (mountain side), one of the landmarks on the north border of the land of Israel, as Promised by Moses, (Numbers 34:8) and as restored by Ezekiel. (Ezekiel 47:15) A place named Sudud exists to the east of the northern extremity of the chain of AntiLibanus, about fifty miles east-northeast of Baalbec . This may be identical with Zedad.

places.name: 셀라
places.eastonKo: '경사면'이라는 뜻으로 베냐민의 한 성읍이며 사울과 요나단이 매장된 곳이다(사무엘하 21:14); 사울의 출생지로 추정된다.
places.smithKo: 베냐민 지파 영토의 성읍으로 사울의 아버지 기스의 가족 무덤이 있었다(여호수아 18:28; 사무엘하 21:14).
places.eastonEn: slope; side, a town in Benjamin, where Saul and his son Jonathan were buried (2 Samuel 21:14). It was probably Saul’s birthplace.
places.smithEn: (a rib), a city in the allotment of Benjamin, (Joshua 18:28) contained the family tomb of Kish, the father of Saul. (2 Samuel 21:14) [Perhaps the same as Zelzah]

places.name: 셀사
places.desc: 성읍. 삼상10:2
places.smithKo: 예루살렘 남서쪽 약 5마일 지점 라헬의 무덤 근처, 베냐민 지파 경계에 위치한 곳이다(사무엘상 10:2).
places.smithEn: (shadow), a place named once only, (1 Samuel 10:2) as on the boundary of Benjamin close to Rachel’s sepulchre, five miles southwest of Jerusalem.

places.name: 스마라임
places.eastonKo: (1) 베냐민의 한 성읍(여호수아 18:22). (2) 예루살렘 북쪽 에브라임 산지의 한 산으로 아비야와 여로보암의 군대가 격돌해 이스라엘 왕이 대패한 곳이다(역대하 13:4-20…
places.smithKo: 베냐민 지파 영토의 성읍(여호수아 18:22), 또는 에브라임 산지의 스마라임산(역대하 13:4)을 가리킨다.
places.eastonEn: Atown of Benjamin (Joshua 18:22); now the ruin, rather two ruins, es-Sumrah, 4 miles north of Jericho. (2.) A mount in the highlands of Ephraim, to the north of Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 13:4-20). Here the armies of Abijah and Jeroboam engaged in a bloody battle, which issued in the total defeat of the king of Israel, who never “recovered strength again,” and soon after died.
places.smithEn: (double fleece of wool), a town in the allotment of Benjamin, (Joshua 18:22) perhaps identical with Mount Zemaraim, mentioned in (2 Chronicles 13:4) only, which was “in Mount Ephraim,” that is to say, within the general district of the highlands of that great tribe. (2 Chronicles 13:4)

places.name: 스난 (하닷사)
places.desc: 미가 선지자가 심판을 예언한 유다 저지대 성읍
places.smithKo: "뾰족하다"는 뜻으로 유다의 기업에 속한 성읍이며 셰펠라 지역에 있었다(수 15:37). 아마 미 1:11의 사아난과 같은 곳일 것이다.
places.smithEn: (pointed), a town in the allotment of Judah, situated in the district of the Shefelah. (Joshua 15:37) It is probably identical with Zaanan. (Micah 1:11)

places.name: 스밧
places.eastonKo: '봉화대', '망대'라는 뜻의 가나안 성읍으로 호르마라고도 불린다(사사기 1:17).
places.smithKo: 정복 후 호르마로 개명된 가나안 성읍의 옛 이름이다(사사기 1:17).
places.eastonEn: beacon; watch-tower, a Canaanite town; called also Hormah (q.v.), Judges 1:17. It has been identified with the pass of es-Sufah, but with greater probability with S’beita.
places.smithEn: (watch-tower), the earlier name, (Judges 1:17) of a Canaanite town, which after its capture and destruction was called by the Israelites Hormah. [Hormah]

places.name: 세르
places.desc: 아르벨 절벽 부근의 납달리 방어 성읍
places.smithKo: "부싯돌"이라는 뜻으로 납달리의 기업에 속한 요새 성읍이며 수 19:35에만 나온다. 아마 게네사렛 호수 남서쪽 부근일 것이다.
places.smithEn: (flint), a fortified town in the allotment of Naphtali, (Joshua 19:35) only, probably in the neighborhood of the southwest side of the Lake of Gennesareth.

places.name: 세렛 시내 (38년 방황 종결선)
places.desc: 이스라엘이 가데스 바네아를 떠나 38년 만에 이 시내를 건넘으로써 출애굽 구세대의 죽음과 방황이 끝난 경계선
places.eastonKo: "무성함, 버드나무 덤불"이라는 뜻으로 사해 남쪽 끝 부근으로 이어지는 시내 또는 골짜기다(민 21:12; 신 2:14). "버드나무 시내"(사 15:7), "광야의 강"(암 6:14)이라 불린다. 와디 엘 아크시로 비정된다.
places.smithKo: "고리버들 시내"라는 뜻이며(신 2:13, 14) 사렛이라고도 한다(민 21:12). 사해 남동쪽 모퉁이 부근으로 흘러드는 시내 또는 골짜기로, 로빈슨 박사는 와디 엘 아흐시와 같은 곳으로 제법 그럴듯하게 제안한다.
places.eastonEn: =Zared, luxuriance; willow bush, a brook or valley communicating with the Dead Sea near its southern extremity (Numbers 21:12; Deuteronomy 2:14). It is called the “brook of the willows” (Isaiah 15:7) and the “river of the wilderness” (Amos 6:14). It has been identified with the Wady el-Aksy.
places.smithEn: (osier brook), (2:13,14) or Za’red, (Numbers 21:12) a brook or valley running into the Dead Sea near its southeast corner, which Dr. Robinson with some probability suggests as identical with the Wady el-Ahsy . It lay between Moab and Edom and is the limit of the proper term of the Israelites’ wandering. (2:14)

places.name: 스르다 (Deir Ghassaneh) 1
places.desc: 성읍. 왕상11:26
places.eastonKo: 에브라임 산지 북쪽 도시로 여로보암의 출생지이며(열왕기상 11:26) 사르단(여호수아 3:16), 스레라(사사기 7:22), 사르단(열왕기상 4:12) 등과 동일시된다.
places.smithKo: 여로보암의 고향으로 칠십인역에 따르면 에브라임 산지에 위치했다(열왕기상 11:26).
places.eastonEn: the fortress, a city on the north of Mount Ephraim; the birthplace of Jeroboam (1 Kings 11:26). It is probably the same as Zaretan (Joshua 3:16), Zererath (Judges 7:22), Zartanah (1 Kings 4:12), or the following.
places.smithEn: (the fortress) the native place of Jeroboam. (1 Kings 11:26) Zereda or Zeredah has been supposed to be identical with Zeredathah and Zarthan or Zartanah; but the last two were in the valley of the Jordan, while Zeredah was, according to the repeated statement of the LXX., on Mount Ephraim.

places.name: 스르다 (Tell es Sa’idiyeh) 2
places.desc: 성읍. 대하4:17
places.eastonKo: 에브라임 산지 북쪽 도시로 여로보암의 출생지이며(열왕기상 11:26) 사르단(여호수아 3:16), 스레라(사사기 7:22), 사르단(열왕기상 4:12) 등과 동일시된다.
places.smithKo: 여로보암의 고향으로 칠십인역에 따르면 에브라임 산지에 위치했다(열왕기상 11:26).
places.eastonEn: the fortress, a city on the north of Mount Ephraim; the birthplace of Jeroboam (1 Kings 11:26). It is probably the same as Zaretan (Joshua 3:16), Zererath (Judges 7:22), Zartanah (1 Kings 4:12), or the following.
places.smithEn: (the fortress) the native place of Jeroboam. (1 Kings 11:26) Zereda or Zeredah has been supposed to be identical with Zeredathah and Zarthan or Zartanah; but the last two were in the valley of the Jordan, while Zeredah was, according to the repeated statement of the LXX., on Mount Ephraim.

places.name: 시글락 (다윗의 망명지)
places.desc: 아기스 왕에게 하사받아 거주하던 중 아말렉에게 불탔으나 추격하여 가족과 소유를 다 되찾은 곳
places.eastonKo: 유다 남방 네겝의 성읍(수 15:31). 다윗이 부하들과 함께 십에서 가드로 피신했을 때 블레셋이 차지하고 있었다. 아기스 왕이 시글락을 다윗의 거처로 주었고, 다윗은 그곳에서 일 년 넉 달 남짓 살았다.
places.smithKo: "굽이진 곳"이라는 뜻. 다윗이 살던 곳이자 그의 사유지였다는 점에서 각별한 관심을 받는 곳이다.
places.eastonEn: a town in the Negeb, or south country of Judah (Joshua 15:31), in the possession of the Philistines when David fled to Gath from Ziph with all his followers. Achish, the king, assigned him Ziklag as his place of residence. There he dwelt for over a year and four months. From this time it pertained to the kings of Judah (1 Samuel 27:6). During his absence with his army to join the Philistine expedition against the Israelites (29:11), it was destroyed by the Amalekites (30:1, 2), whom David, however, pursued and utterly routed, returning all the captives (1 Samuel 30:26-31). Two days after his return from this expedition, David received tidings of the disastrous battle of Gilboa and of the death of Saul (2 Samuel 1:1-16). He now left Ziklag and returned to Hebron, along with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, and his band of 600 men. It has been identified with ‘Asluj, a heap of ruins south of Beersheba. Conder, however, identifies it with Khirbet Zuheilikah, ruins found on three hills half a mile apart, some seventeen miles north-west of Beersheba, on the confines of Philistia, Judah, and Amalek.
places.smithEn: (winding), a place which possesses a special interest from its having been the residence and the private property of David. It is first mentioned in the catalogue of the towns of Judah in (Joshua 15:31) and occurs, in the same connection among the places which were allotted out of the territory of Judah to Simeon. (Joshua 19:5) We next encounter it in the possession of the Philistines (1 Samuel 27:6) when it was, at David’s request, bestowed upon him by Achish king of Gath. He resided there for a year and four months. (1 Samuel 27:6,7; 30:14,26; 1 Chronicles 12:1,20) It was there he received the news of Saul’s death. (2 Samuel 1:1; 4:10) He then relinquished it for Hebron. (2 Samuel 2:1) Ziklag is finally mentioned as being reinhabited by the people of Judah after their return from captivity. (Nehemiah 11:28) The situation of the town is difficult to determine, and we only know for certain that it was in the south country.

places.name: 시므리
places.eastonKo: '찬양받을 만한'이라는 뜻. (1) 살루의 아들로 미디안 여인을 장막에 데려온 죄로 비느하스에게 죽임을 당했다(민수기 25:6-15). (2) 디르사에서 엘라를 암살하고 이스라엘 …
places.smithKo: 시므온 지파 지도자 살루의 아들로 미디안 공주 고스비와 함께 비느하스에게 죽임당했다(민수기 25:14). 또한 이스라엘 왕국의 다섯째 왕으로 왕 엘라를 죽이고 왕위를 찬탈했으나 7…
places.eastonEn: praise-worthy. (1.) A son of Salu, slain by Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, because of his wickedness in bringing a Midianitish woman into his tent (Numbers 25:6-15). (2.) Murdered Elah at Tirzah, and succeeded him on the throne of Israel (1 Kings 16:8-10). He reigned only seven days, for Omri, whom the army elected as king, laid siege to Tirzah, whereupon Zimri set fire to the palace and perished amid its ruins (11-20). Omri succeeded to the throne only after four years of fierce war with Tibni, another claimant to the throne.
places.smithEn: • The son of Salu, a Simeonite chieftain, slain by Phinehas with the Midianitish princess Cozbi. (Numbers 25:14). (B.C. 1450.) • Fifth sovereign of the separate kingdom of Israel, of which he occupied the throne for the brief period of seven days, B.C. 930 or 929. Originally in command of half the chariots in the royal army, he gained the crown by the murder of King Elah; son of Baasha. But the army made their general, Omri, king, who marched against Tirzah, where Zimri was. Zimri retreated into the innermost part of the late king’s palace, set it on fire, and perished in the ruins. (1 Kings 16:9-20) • One of the five sons of Zerah the son of Judah. (1 Chronicles 2:6) (B.C. after 1706.) • Son of Jehoadah and descendant of Saul. (1 Chronicles 8:36; 9:42) • An obscure name, mentioned (Jeremiah 25:25) in probable connection with Dedan, Tema, Buz, Arabia, the “mingled people.” Nothing further is known respecting Zimri, but the name may possibly be the same as, or derived from, Zimran, which see.

places.name: 바란 광야 & 신 광야 (Zin Desert) 1
places.modern: 네게브 남부 칭 광야 (Wilderness of Zin) (이스라엘 네게브)
places.desc: 이스라엘이 38년간 방황하며 연단을 받은 험준한 사막 지대

places.eastonEn: a low palm-tree, the south-eastern corner of the desert et-Tih, the wilderness of Paran, between the Gulf of Akabah and the head of the Wady Guraiyeh (Numbers 13:21). To be distinguished from the wilderness of Sin (q.v.).
places.smithEn: (flat), the name given to a portion of the desert tract between the Dead Sea, Ghor, and Arabah on the east, and the general plateau of the Tih which stretches westward. The country in question consists of two or three successive terraces of mountain converging to an acute single at the Dead Sea’s southern verge, toward which also they slope. Kadesh lay in it, and here also Idumea was conterminous with Judah; since Kadesh was a city in the border of Edom. [See Kadesh, Kadeshbarnea]. (Numbers 13:21; 20:1; 27:14; 33:36; 34:3; Joshua 15:1)

places.eastonEn: sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built. It was surrounded on all sides, except the north, by deep valleys, that of the Tyropoeon (q.v.) separating it from Moriah (q.v.), which it surpasses in height by 105 feet. It was the south-eastern hill of Jerusalem. When David took it from the Jebusites (Joshua 15:63; 2 Samuel 5:7) he built on it a citadel and a palace, and it became “the city of David” (1 Kings 8:1; 2 Kings 19:21, 31; 1 Chronicles 11:5). In the later books of the Old Testament this name was sometimes used (Psalm 87:2; 149:2; Isaiah 33:14; Joel 2:1) to denote Jerusalem in general, and sometimes God’s chosen Israel (Psalm 51:18; 87:5). In the New Testament (see SION) it is used sometimes to denote the Church of God (Hebrews 12:22), and sometimes the heavenly city (Revelation 14:1).

(Joshua 15:24) It does not appear again in the history, nor has any trace of has been met with. • In the highland district, named between Carmel and Juttah. (Joshua 15:55) The place is immortalized by its connection with David. The name of Zif if, found about three miles south of Hebron, attached to a rounded hill of some 100 feet in height, which is called Tell Zif . • Son of Jehaleleel. (1 Chronicles 4:16)

places.eastonEn: (Old Egypt. Sant= “stronghold,” the modern San). A city on the Tanitic branch of the Nile, called by the Greeks Tanis. It was built seven years after Hebron in Palestine (Numbers 13:22). This great and important city was the capital of the Hyksos, or Shepherd kings, who ruled Egypt for more than 500 years. It was the frontier town of Goshen. Here Pharaoh was holding his court at the time of his various interviews with Moses and Aaron. “No trace of Zoan exists; Tanis was built over it, and city after city has been built over the ruins of that” (Harper, Bible and Modern Discovery). Extensive mounds of ruins, the wreck of the ancient city, now mark its site (Isaiah 19:11, 13; 30:4; Ezekiel 30:14). “The whole constitutes one of the grandest and oldest ruins in the world.” This city was also called “the Field of Zoan” (Psalm 78:12, 43) and “the Town of Rameses” (q.v.), because the oppressor rebuilt and embellished it, probably by the forced labour of the Hebrews, and made it his northern capital.
places.smithEn: (place of departure), an ancient city of lower Egypt, called Tanis by the Greeks. It stood on the eastern bank of the Tanitic branch of the Nile. Its name indicates a place of departure from a country, and hence it has been identified with Avaris (Tanis, the modern San), the capital of the Shepherd dynasty in Egypt, built seven years after Hebron and existing before the time of Abraham. It was taken by the Shepherd kings in their invasion of Egypt, and by them rebuilt, and garrisoned, according to Manetho, with 240,000 men. This cite is mentioned in connection with the plagues in such a manner as to leave no doubt that it is the city spoken of in the narrative in Exodus as that where Pharaoh dwelt, (Psalms 78:42,43) and where Moses wrought his wonders on the field of Zoan a rich plain extending thirty miles toward the east. Tanis gave its name to the twenty-first and twenty-third dynasties and hence its mention in Isaiah. (Isaiah 19:13; 30:4) (The present “field of Zoan” is a barren waste, very thinly inhabited. “One of the principal capitals of Pharaoh is now the habitation of fishermen the resort of wild beasts, and infested with reptiles and malignant fevers.” There have been discovered a great number of monuments here which throw light upon the Bible history. Brugsch refers to two statues of colossal size of Mermesha of the thirteenth dynasty, wonderfully perfect in the execution of the individual parts and says that memorials of Rameses the Great lie scattered broadcast like the mouldering bones of generations slain long ago. The area of the sacred enclosure of the temple is 1500 feet by 1250.- ED.)

places.name: 소알 (벨라)

places.eastonKo: "작다"는 뜻으로 사해 동쪽 또는 남동쪽의 성읍이다. 롯과 그 두 딸이 소돔에서 이곳으로 피했다(창 19:22, 23). 본래 이름은 벨라였다(창 14:2, 8). 이사야(사 15:5)와 예레미야(렘 48:34)가 언급한다.
places.smithKo: "작음"이라는 뜻으로 가나안 땅에서 가장 오래된 성읍 중 하나다. 본래 이름은 벨라였다.
places.eastonEn: small, a town on the east or south-east of the Dead Sea, to which Lot and his daughters fled from Sodom (Genesis 19:22, 23). It was originally called Bela (14:2, 8). It is referred to by the prophets Isaiah (15:5) and Jeremiah (48:34). Its ruins are still seen at the opening of the ravine of Kerak, the Kir-Moab referred to in 2 Kings 3, the modern Tell esh-Shaghur.
places.smithEn: (smallness), one of the most ancient cities of the land of Canaan. Its original name was Bela. (Genesis 14:2,8) It was in intimate connection with the cities of the “plain of Jordan”—Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, See also (Genesis 13:10) but not Genesis10:19 In the general destruction of the cities of the plain Zoar was spared to afford shelter to Lot. (Genesis 19:22,23,30) It is mentioned in the account of the death of Moses as one (of the landmarks which bounded his view from Pisgah, (34:3) and it appears to have been known in the time both of Isaiah, (Isaiah 15:5) and Jeremiah. (Jeremiah 48:34) These are all the notices of Zoar contained in the Bible. It was situated in the same district with the four cities already mentioned, viz. in the “plain” or “circle” of the Jordan, and the narrative of (Genesis 19:1)... evidently implies that it was very near to Sodom. vs. (Genesis 19:15; 23:27) The definite position of Sodom is, and probably will always be, a mystery; but there can be little doubt that the plain of the Jordan was at the north side of the Dead Sea and that the cities of the plain must therefore have been situated there instead of at the southern end of the lake, as it is generally taken for granted they were. [Sodom] (But the great majority of scholars from Josephus and Eusebius to the present of the Dead Sea.)

places.name: 소바
places.desc: 다메섹 북동쪽의 아람 소국. 다윗이 격파한 하닷에셀의 왕국. 소바 용사들이 다윗의 용사 목록에 등장
places.eastonKo: 쾰레시리아 남쪽의 시리아 지방 또는 왕국으로 레바논 동쪽 경사면에서 유브라데강 쪽으로 뻗어 있었다. 사울과 다윗이 이곳 왕들과 전쟁을 벌였다(사무엘상 14:47).
places.eastonEn: =Aram-Zobah, (Psalm 60, title), a Syrian province or kingdom to the south of Coele-Syria, and extending from the eastern slopes of Lebanon north and east toward the Euphrates. Saul and David had war with the kings of Zobah (1 Samuel 14:47; 2 Samuel 8:3; 10:6).

places.name: 소빔
places.desc: 자연 지역. 민23:14
places.eastonKo: 모압 비스가산 능선의 한 장소로(민수기 23:14) 발락이 발람을 데려가 이스라엘을 저주하게 하려 했으나 발람은 오직 여호와의 말씀, 곧 축복만을 전했다.
places.smithKo: 비스가산 정상 인근으로 발람이 이스라엘 진영을 두 번째로 바라본 곳이다(민수기 23:14).
places.eastonEn: field of watchers, a place in Moab on the range of Pisgah (Numbers 23:14). To this place Balak brought Balaam, that he might from thence curse the children of Israel. Balaam could only speak the word of the Lord, and that was blessing. It is the modern Tal’at-es-Safa. (See PISGAH.)
places.smithEn: (watchers), The field of, a spot on or near the top of Pisgah, from which Balaam had his second view of the encampment of Israel. (Numbers 23:14) The position of the field of Zophim is not defined. Possibly it is the same place which later in the history is mentioned as Mizpah-moab.

places.name: 소라 & 에스다올 (삼손 탄생지)
places.desc: 마노아의 아들 나실인 삼손의 출생지, 여호와의 영이 처음 감동하기 시작한 진영
places.eastonKo: "말벌의 곳"이라는 뜻으로 유다 저지대의 성읍이며 후에 단에게 주어졌다(수 19:41; 삿 18:2). 수 15:33의 소라와 같은 곳으로 보인다. 삼손이 태어난 곳이며(삿 13:2, 25) 그 근처에 묻혔다(삿 16:31).
places.smithKo: "말벌"이라는 뜻으로 단 지파의 기업에 속한 성읍(수 19:41). 앞서 수 15:33의 유다 목록 가운데 셰펠라 지역의 성읍으로 언급된다. 마노아가 살던 곳이자 삼손이 태어난 곳이다.
places.eastonEn: place of wasps, a town in the low country of Judah, afterwards given to Dan (Joshua 19:41; Judges 18:2), probably the same as Zoreah (Joshua 15:33). This was Samson’s birthplace (Judges 13:2, 25), and near it he found a grave (16:31). It was situated on the crest of a hill overlooking the valley of Sorek, and was fortified by Rehoboam (2 Chronicles 11:10). It has been identified with Sur’ah, in the Wady Surar, 8 miles west of Jerusalem. It is noticed on monuments in the fifteenth century B.C. as attacked by the Abiri or Hebrews.
places.smithEn: (hornet), a town in the allotment of the tribe of Dan, (Joshua 19:41) It is previously mentioned ch. (Joshua 15:33) in the catalogue of Judah, among the places in the district of the Shefelah (Authorized Version “Zoreah”), It was the residence of Manoah and the native place of Samson. It is mentioned among the places fortified by Rehoboam. (2 Chronicles 11:10) It is perhaps identical with the modern village of Sur’ah .

places.name: 숩
places.desc: 지역. 삼상9:5
places.eastonKo: 사무엘의 성읍 라마가 있던 지역으로(사무엘상 9:5,6) 엘가나의 아들 숩의 이름을 딴 것으로 추정된다.
places.smithKo: 고핫 계열 레위인으로 엘가나와 사무엘의 조상이며 다른 곳에서는 소배로 불린다(사무엘상 1:1; 역대상 6:35). 또한 사울과 그 종이 살리사, 사알림, 베냐민 지역을 지난 후 도…
places.eastonEn: honeycomb, a Kohathite Levite, ancestor of Elkanah and Samuel (1 Samuel 1:1); called also Zophai (1 Chronicles 6:26).
places.smithEn: a Kohathite Levite, ancestor of Elkanah and Samuel. (1 Samuel 1:1; 1 Chronicles 6:35) In (1 Chronicles 6:26) he is called Zophai. (honeycomb), The land of, a district at which Saul and his servant arrived after passing through the possessions of Shalisha, of Shalim and of the Benjamites. (1 Samuel 9:5) only. It evidently contained the city in which they encountered Samuel, ver. 6, and that again was certainly not far from the “tomb of Rachel.” It may perhaps be identified with Soba, a well-known place about seven miles due west of Jerusalem.

places.name: 아낫 (납달리 벧아낫)
places.desc: 가나안 전쟁의 여신 아낫 신전이 있던 상부 갈릴리 요새
places.eastonKo: "응답" 곧 "기도에 대한 응답"이라는 뜻으로, 이스라엘 사사 중 하나였던 삼갈의 아버지다(삿 3:31).
places.smithKo: "응답"이라는 뜻으로 삼갈의 아버지다(삿 3:31; 5:6).

places.name: 서해 (지중해 구약 명칭)
places.desc: 해 지는 편 서쪽 바다 지중해

places.name: 두르 샤루킨 (코르사바드 / 사르곤 2세)
places.desc: 사마리아를 최종 함락시킨 앗수르 사르곤 2세가 건설한 거대 궁성 수도

places.name: 페르세폴리스
places.desc: 다리오 1세와 아하수에로 왕이 건축한 페르시아 제국의 웅장한 의전 수도
places.smithKo: 외경 마카베오하 9:2에만 언급되며 파사 본토의 수도였다. 창건자로 보이는 다리오 히스타스페스 때부터 알렉산더의 침공 때까지 파사 궁정이 때때로 머물던 곳이다. 그 정복자가 이곳을 함부로 파괴한 일은 잘 알려져 있다.
places.smithEn: mentioned only in 2 Macc. 9:2, was the capital of Persia proper, and the occasional residence of the Persian court from the time of Darius Hystaspes, who seems to have been its founder, to the invasion of Alexander. Its wanton destruction by that conqueror is well known. Its site is now called the Chehl-Minar, or Forty Pillars. Here, on a platform hewn out of the solid rock the sides of which face the four cardinal points, are the remains of two great palaces, built respectively by Darius Hytaspes and his son Xerxes, besides a number of other edifices, chiefly temples. They are of great extent and magnificence, covering an area of many acres.

places.name: 엘림마이스 (엘람 수산)
places.desc: 오순절 성령 강림 때 예루살렘에 모였던 동방 디아스포라의 고향 엘람

places.name: 맛사다 (헤롯의 요새 & 열심당 최후)
places.desc: 헤롯 대왕의 천연 절벽 궁전 요새이자 주후 73년 로마 10군단에 맞선 열심당 960명의 최후 항전지

places.name: 아드리아 바다 (지중해 중앙)
places.desc: 열나흘째 밤에 배가 이리저리 쫓겨가며 선원들이 육지에 가까워지는 줄 짐작한 바다
places.eastonKo: 행 27:27에 나오며 개정역은 "아드리아 바다"로 적는다. 바울 당시에는 그레데와 시칠리아 사이 지중해 전체를 포함했다. 오늘날의 베네치아만이며 로마인의 마레 수페룸으로, 마레 인페룸 곧 티레니아해와 구별된다.
places.smithKo: 정확히는 아드리아스이며 아드리아해다(행 27:27). 이 말은 포강 근처의 성읍 아드리아에서 온 듯하다. 바울 당시에는 그리스와 이탈리아 사이 바다 전체를 포함했고 남쪽으로 그레데에서 시칠리아까지 이르렀다.

places.name: 트레 폰타네 (바울 참수 순교터)
places.desc: 네로 황제 박해 때 사도 바울이 참수 순교하여 세 개의 샘이 솟았다는 전승의 순교지

places.name: 스불론 해변 도로 (이방의 갈릴리 길)
places.orig: Via Maris / Way of the Sea / דֶּרֶךְ הַיָּם
places.desc: 이사야 예언 성취지. 스불론·납달리 이방의 갈릴리. 예수님 공생애 사역 지리적 배경 도로

places.name: 안디바드리
places.description: 헤롯 대왕이 그의 아버지 안디바더를 기려 세운 성읍으로, 예루살렘에서 가이사랴로 가는 길에 있었다(행 23:31). 정확한 위치는 학자들 사이에 이견이 있다.
places.eastonKo: 헤롯 대왕이 자기 아버지 안티파터를 기려 세운 도시. 가이사랴와 룻다 사이, 가이사랴에서 예루살렘으로 가는 대로에서 내륙으로 2마일 떨어진 곳에 있었다. 바울이 가이사랴로 가는 길…
places.smithKo: '그 아버지를 위하여'라는 뜻으로 병사들이 바울을 밤에 호송한 도시이다(사도행전 23:31). 옛 이름은 가바르사바였으나 헤롯이 재건하며 아버지 안티파테르를 기려 안디바드리로 개명…
places.eastonEn: a city built by Herod the Great, and called by this name in honour of his father, Antipater. It lay between Caesarea and Lydda, two miles inland, on the great Roman road from Caesarea to Jerusalem. To this place Paul was brought by night (Acts 23:31) on his way to Caesarea, from which it was distant 28 miles. It is identified with the modern, Ras-el-Ain, where rise the springs of Aujeh, the largest springs in Palestine.
places.smithEn: (for his father), a town to which the soldiers conveyed St. Paul by night on their march. (Acts 23:31) Its ancient name was Capharsaba; and Herod, when he rebuilt the city, changed it to Antipatris, in honor of his father, Antipater. The village Kefr-Sabba still retains the ancient name of Antipatris.

places.name: 아람소바
places.description: (시편 60편 표제) 아마도 유프라테스강과 오론테스강 사이의 지역.
places.eastonKo: (시편 60편 표제) 아마도 유프라테스강과 오론테스강 사이의 지역.
places.eastonEn: (Psalm 60, title), probably the region between the Euphrates and the Orontes.
places.smithEn: Psal 60:1, title. [Aram, 1]
places.smithKo: 시편 60편 표제. 아람(1) 참조.

places.name: 아스드롯가르나임
places.description: 바산의 거인족 르바임의 성읍으로(창 14:5), 다메섹 남쪽 약 30마일 지점의 현재 사나메인으로 추정된다.
places.eastonKo: '두 뿔의 아스다롯', 곧 르바임의 거처(창세기 14:5). 앞의 아스다롯과 동일시될 수 있으며, '카르나임'('두 뿔', 곧 초승달)이라 불렸다.
places.smithKo: '두 뿔의 아스다롯'이라는 뜻으로 매우 오래된 곳이며 르바임 족속의 거처였다(창세기 14:5). 마카베오서에서는 갈릴리 땅의 가르나임 또는 가르니온으로 다시 언급된다.
places.eastonEn: Ashteroth of the two horns, the abode of the Rephaim (Genesis 14:5). It may be identified with Ashtaroth preceding; called “Karnaim”, i.e., the “two-horned” (the crescent moon). The Samaritan version renders the word by “Sunamein,” the present es-Sunamein, 28 miles south of Damascus.
places.smithEn: (Ashteroth of the two horns or peaks) a place of very great antiquity, the abode of the Rephaim. (Genesis 14:5) The name reappears but once, as Carnaim or Carnion, 1 Macc. 5:26,43,44; 2 Macc. 12:21,26, in “the land of Galaad.” It is probably the modern Es-Sanamein, on the Haj route, about 25 miles south of Damascus.

places.name: 바잇
places.description: 사 15:2의 히브리어는 '바지트' 곧 '신전'으로, 그모스 신전을 가리키는 것으로 보인다.
places.eastonKo: 집. 아마도 유명한 우상 신전이 있던 모압의 한 성읍(사 15:2).
places.smithKo: '집'이라는 뜻으로 모압의 거짓 신들의 '신전'을 가리키며 같은 구절의 '산당'과 대비된다(이사야 15:2).
places.eastonEn: house, probably a city of Moab, which had a celebrated idol-temple (Isaiah 15:2). It has also been regarded as denoting simply the temple of the idol of Moab as opposed to the “high place.”
places.smithEn: (the horse), referring to the “temple” of the false gods of Moab, as opposed to the “high places” in the same sentence. (Isaiah 15:2) and comp. (Isaiah 16:12)

places.name: 브엘세바
places.description: 가나안 남쪽 경계의 성읍으로 헤브론 남서쪽 25마일 지점에 있으며 성경에 33회 언급된다. 아브라함이 처음 이름 지었고(창 21:31-33), 이삭이 다시 이름 지었다(창 26:33). 유다에게 주어졌다가 후에 시므온에게 배정되었고(수 15:28, 19:2), 흔히 가나안의 남쪽 끝을 나타내는 말로 쓰였다('단에서 브엘세바까지', 삿 20:1). 지금도 큰
places.eastonEn: well of the oath, or well of seven, a well dug by Abraham, and so named because he and Abimelech here entered into a compact (Genesis 21:31). On re-opening it, Isaac gave it the same name (Genesis 26:31-33). It was a favourite place of abode of both of these patriarchs (21:33-22:1, 19; 26:33; 28:10). It is mentioned among the “cities” given to the tribe of Simeon (Joshua 19:2; 1 Chronicles 4:28). From Dan to Beersheba, a distance of about 144 miles (Judges 20:1; 1 Chronicles 21:2; 2 Samuel 24:2), became the usual way of designating the whole Promised Land, and passed into a proverb. After the return from the Captivity the phrase is narrowed into “from Beersheba unto the valley of Hinnom” (Nehemiah 11:30). The kingdom of the ten tribes extended from Beersheba to Mount Ephraim (2 Chronicles 19:4). The name is not found in the New Testament. It is still called by the Arabs Bir es-Seba, i.e., “well of the seven”, where there are to the present day two principal wells and five smaller ones. It is nearly midway between the southern end of the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean.
places.eastonKo: 맹세의 우물, 또는 일곱의 우물. 아브라함이 팠고 아비멜렉과의 계약 후 이삭이 다시 이름 붙인 곳(창 21:31; 26:31-33). '단에서 브엘세바까지'라는 말은 약속의 땅 전체를 가리키는 관용구가 되었다.
places.smithEn: (well of the oath), the name of one of the old places in Palestine which formed the southern limit of the country. There are two accounts of the origin of the name. According to the first, the well was dug by Abraham, and the name given to Judah, (Joshua 15:28) and then to Simeon, (Joshua 19:2; 1 Chronicles 4:28) In the often-quoted “from Dan even unto Beersheba,” (Judges 20:1) it represents the southern boundary of Canaan, as Dan the northern. In the time of Jerome it was still a considerable place, and still retains its ancient name—Bir es-Seba . There are at present on the spot two principal wells and five smaller ones. The two principal wells are on or close to the northern bank of the Wady es-Seba . The larger of the two, which lies to the east, is, according to Dr. Robinson, 12 1/2 feet in diameter, and at the time of his visit (April 12) was 44 1/2 feet to the surface of the water. The masonry which encloses the well extends downward 28 1/2 feet. The other well is 5 feet in diameter, and was 42 feet to the water. The curb-stones around the mouth of both wells are worn into deep grooves by the action of the ropes of so many centures. These wells are in constant use today. The five lesser wells are in a group in the bed of the wady. On some low hills north of the large wells are scattered the foundations and ruins of a town of moderate size.
places.smithKo: '맹세의 우물'이라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 남쪽 경계를 이루던 오래된 지명이다. 아브라함이 우물을 팠다는 설이 전해지며, 유다(여호수아 15:28)와 시므온(여호수아 19:2)의 경계 성읍이 되었다. '단에서부터 브엘세바까지'라는 표현은 가나안 남북 경계를 나타낸다(사사기 20:1). 오늘날에도 비르 에스세바라는 이름으로 남아 있으며 두 개의 큰 우물과 다섯 개의 작은 우물이 있다.

places.name: 베다
places.description: 삼하 8:8의 지명으로, 대상 18:8에서는 디브핫이라 불린다.
places.eastonKo: 신뢰. 소바 왕 하닷에셀에게 속한 성읍으로 다윗에게 많은 놋 전리품을 안겨주었으며(삼하 8:8) 디브핫이라고도 불린다.
places.smithKo: '신뢰'라는 뜻으로 소바 왕 하닷에셀에 속한 성읍이며 브로대와 함께 언급되고(사무엘하 8:8) 역대상 18:8에서는 디브핫이라 불린다.
places.eastonEn: confidence, a city belonging to Hadadezer, king of Zobah, which yielded much spoil of brass to David (2 Samuel 8:8). In 1 Chronicles 18:8 it is called Tibhath.
places.smithEn: (confidence), a city belonging to Hadadezer king of Zobah, mentioned with Berothai. (2 Samuel 8:8) In the parallel account, (1 Chronicles 18:8) the name is called Tibhath.

places.name: 벧아스마웹
places.description: 베냐민의 한 성읍으로 아스마웹이라고도 불린다(느 7:28, 12:29, 스 2:24).

places.name: 벳바게
places.description: 덜 익은 무화과의 집. 예루살렘에서 여리고로 가는 길목, 베다니 근처 감람산의 한 마을(마 21:1).
places.eastonKo: 덜 익은 무화과의 집. 예루살렘에서 여리고로 가는 길목, 베다니 근처 감람산의 한 마을(마 21:1).
places.eastonEn: house of the unripe fig, a village on the Mount of Olives, on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho (Matthew 21:1; Mark 11:1; Luke 19:29), and very close to Bethany. It was the limit of a Sabbath-day’s journey from Jerusalem, i.e., 2,000 cubits. It has been identified with the modern Kefr-et-Tur.
places.smithEn: (g hard) (house of figs) the name of a place on the Mount of Olives on the road between Jericho and Jerusalem. It was apparently close to Bethany. (Matthew 21:1; Mark 11:1; Luke 19:29)
places.smithKo: '무화과의 집'이라는 뜻으로 여리고에서 예루살렘으로 가는 길, 감람산 위의 한 장소이며 베다니와 가까웠던 것으로 보인다(마태복음 21:1).

places.name: 굿바
places.description: 사마리아로 이주민이 옮겨진 바빌로니아의 도시 또는 지역(왕하 17:24).
places.eastonKo: 사마리아로 이주민이 옮겨진 바빌로니아의 도시 또는 지역(왕하 17:24).
places.eastonEn: one of the Babylonian cities or districts from which Shalmaneser transplanted certain colonists to Samaria (2 Kings 17:24). Some have conjectured that the “Cutheans” were identical with the “Cossaeans” who inhabited the hill-country to the north of the river Choaspes. Cuthah is now identified with Tell Ibrahim, 15 miles north-east of Babylon.

places.name: 엘드게
places.description: 단 지파의 한 지명으로 레위인에게 주어졌다(수 19:44, 21:23).
places.eastonEn: God is its fear, a city in the tribe of Daniel It was a city of refuge and a Levitical city (Joshua 21:23). It has been identified with Beit-Likia, north-east of latrum.
places.eastonKo: '하나님은 그의 두려움'이라는 뜻으로, 단 지파 안의 성읍. 도피성이자 레위인의 성읍이었다(여호수아 21:23). 라트룬 북동쪽 베이트리키아와 동일시된다.
places.smithEn: (God its fear), one of the cities in the border of Dan, (Joshua 19:44) which with its suburbs was allotted to the Kohathite Levites. (Joshua 21:23)
places.smithKo: 단 지파 경계의 성읍 중 하나로(여호수아 19:44) 그 주변 지역과 함께 고핫 가문 레위인에게 배정되었다(여호수아 21:23).

places.name: 엘드곤
places.description: 유다 산지의 한 성읍(수 15:59).

places.name: 엘돌랏
places.description: 유다 남부의 한 성읍으로 시므온에게 주어졌으며(수 15:30, 19:4), 대상 4:29에서는 돌랏이라 불린다.
places.smithEn: (God’s kindred), one of the cities in the south of Judah, (Joshua 15:30) allotted to Simeon, (Joshua 19:4) and in possession of that tribe until the time of David. (1 Chronicles 4:29)
places.smithKo: '하나님의 친족'이라는 뜻으로 유다 남쪽의 성읍이며(여호수아 15:30) 시므온에 배정되었고(여호수아 19:4) 다윗 시대까지 그 지파의 소유로 남았다(역대상 4:29).

places.name: 길보아
places.description: 이스르엘 평야 동쪽의 산으로 길이 약 10마일이며 동남동에서 서북서로 뻗는다. 북쪽 비탈은 가파르고 남쪽은 한때 숲이었을 것이나 지금은 사람이 살며 경작한다. 사울과 요나단이 싸우다 죽은 곳이며, 사울이 여기서 엔돌의 신접한 여인을 찾아갔다(삼상 28:4, 31:6, 대상 10:1, 삼하 1:21). 지금은 제벨 푸쿠아라 불린다.
places.eastonKo: '끓는 샘'이라는 뜻으로, 지금의 제벨 푸쿠아라 불리는 산맥이며 사울이 블레셋에게 참패한 무대로 기억된다. 이곳에서 그의 세 아들도 죽었고 그 자신도 자결했다(사무엘상 28:4; …
places.smithKo: '솟아나는 샘'이라는 뜻으로 에스드라엘론 평지 동쪽, 이스르엘 성읍 위로 솟은 산맥이다. 성경에서는 오직 사울과 요나단이 블레셋에게 패해 죽은 사건과 관련해서만 언급된다(사무엘상 …
places.eastonEn: boiling spring, a mountain range, now Jebel Fukua’, memorable as the scene of Saul’s disastrous defeat by the Philistines. Here also his three sons were slain, and he himself died by his own hand (1 Samuel 28:4; 31:1-8; 2 Samuel 1:6-21; 21:12; 1 Chronicles 10:1, 8). It was a low barren range of mountains bounding the valley of Esdraelon (Jezreel) on the east, between it and the Jordan valley. When the tidings of this defeat were conveyed to David, he gave utterance to those pathetic words in the “Song of the Bow” (2 Samuel 1:19-27).
places.smithEn: (a bubbling spring) a mountain range on the eastern side of the plain of Esdraelon, rising over the city of Jezreel. Comp. (1 Samuel 28:4) with 1Sam 29:1It is mentioned in Scripture only in connection with one event in Israelitish history, the defeat and death of Saul and Jonathan by the Philistines. (1 Samuel 31:11; 2 Samuel 1:6; 21:12; 1 Chronicles 10:1,8) Of the identity of Gilboa with the ridge which stretches eastward from the ruins of Jezreel no doubt can be entertained. The village is now called Jelbou .

places.name: 여갑스엘
places.description: '하나님이 모으시는 것'이라는 뜻으로 갑스엘의 확장 표기이며 유다 최남단 최원방 성읍이다(느헤미야 11:25).
places.smithKo: '하나님이 모으시는 것'이라는 뜻으로 갑스엘의 확장 표기이며 유다 최남단 최원방 성읍이다(느헤미야 11:25).
places.smithEn: (what God gathers), a fuller form of the name of Kabzeel, the most remote city of Judah on the southern frontier. (Nehemiah 11:25)

places.name: 기브롯핫다아와
places.description: '욕심 또는 정욕의 무덤들'이라는 뜻으로, 이스라엘 백성이 광야를 유랑하며 머문 진지 중 하나. 아마도 와디 무라에 있었을 것이며, 고대 진영의 흔적이 발견된 에르웨이스 엘에베이리그와 동일시된다.
places.eastonKo: '욕심 또는 정욕의 무덤들'이라는 뜻으로, 이스라엘 백성이 광야를 유랑하며 머문 진지 중 하나. 아마도 와디 무라에 있었을 것이며, 고대 진영의 흔적이 발견된 에르웨이스 엘에베이리…
places.eastonEn: the graves of the longing or of lust, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness. It was probably in the Wady Murrah, and has been identified with the Erweis el-Ebeirig, where the remains of an ancient encampment have been found, about 30 miles north-east of Sinai, and exactly a day’s journey from ‘Ain Hudherah. “Here began the troubles of the journey. First, complaints broke out among the people, probably at the heat, the toil, and the privations of the  march; and then God at once punished them by lightning, which fell on the hinder part of the camp, and killed many persons, but ceased at the intercession of Moses (Numbers 11:1, 2). Then a disgust fell on the multitude at having nothing to eat but the manna day after day, no change, no flesh, no fish, no high-flavoured vegetables, no luscious fruits...The people loathed the ‘light food,’ and cried out to Moses, ‘Give us flesh, give us flesh, that we may eat.’” In this emergency Moses, in despair, cried unto God. An answer came. God sent “a prodigious flight of quails, on which the people satiated their gluttonous appetite for a full month. Then punishment fell on them: they loathed the food which they had desired; it bred disease in them; the divine anger aggravated the disease into a plague, and a heavy mortality was the consequence. The dead were buried without the camp; and in memory of man’s sin and of the divine wrath this name, Kibroth-hattaavah, the Graves of Lust, was given to the place of their sepulchre” (Numbers 11:34, 35; 33:16, 17; Deuteronomy 9:22; comp. Psalm 78:30, 31)., Rawlinson’s Moses, p. 175. From this encampment they journeyed in a north-eastern direction to Hazeroth.
places.smithEn: i.e. as in the margin, the graves of lust, a station of the Israelites in the wilderness, where, growing tired of manna and desiring flesh, they murmured, and God sent them quails in great abundance, but smote great numbers of them with a plague and they died. It is about three days journey from Sinai, and near the Gulf of Akabah and the Wady el Hudherah (Hazeroth.)
places.smithKo: '탐욕의 무덤'이라는 뜻으로 이스라엘 백성이 만나에 싫증나 고기를 요구하자 하나님이 메추라기를 보내셨으나 동시에 재앙으로 많은 사람이 죽어 묻힌 광야 진영이다(민수기 11장).

places.name: 로드발
places.description: '목초지 없음'이라는 뜻(사무엘하 17:27)으로, 얍복강 북쪽, 마하나임에서 멀지 않은 길르앗의 성읍(9:4,5). 아마도 드빌(여호수아 13:26)과 같은 곳일 것이다.

places.eastonEn: no pasture, (2 Samuel 17:27), a town in Gilead not far from Mahanaim, north of the Jabbok (9:4, 5). It is probably identical with Debir (Joshua 13:26).
places.smithEn: (without pasture), a place named with Mahanaim, Rogelim and other transjordanic towns, (2 Samuel 17:27) and therefore no doubt on the east side of the Jordan. It was the native place of Machir-ben-Ammiel. (2 Samuel 9:4,5)
places.smithKo: 마하나임, 로글림 등과 함께 언급되는 요단 동편의 지명으로 므비보셋을 돌본 마길의 고향이다(사무엘하 9:4,5, 17:27).

places.name: 마레사
places.description: '언덕 꼭대기'라는 뜻으로 유다 저지대의 성읍이다(수 15:44). 북왕국과 갈라진 후 르호보암이 견고케 하고 수비대를 두었다(대하 11:8). 그 근처에서 세라와 아사의 큰 전투가 있었다(대하 14:9-12). BC 110년경 요한 힐카누스가 이두매인에게서 빼앗았다. 4세기에는 폐허가 되어 유세비우스와 제롬이 엘류테로폴리스에서 두 번째 마일 지점이라 기록
places.eastonEn: possession, a city in the plain of Judah (John. 15:44). Here Asa defeated Zerah the Ethiopian (2 Chronicles 14:9, 10). It is identified with the ruin el-Mer’ash, about 1 1/2 mile south of Beit Jibrin.
places.eastonKo: '소유'라는 뜻으로, 유다 평지의 성읍(여호수아 15:44). 이곳에서 아사가 에티오피아 사람 세라를 물리쳤다(역대하 14:9,10). 베이트지브린 남쪽 약 1과 1/2마일의 폐허 엘메라시와 동일시된다.

places.eastonEn: a bond, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 10:6), at the foot of Mount Hor. (Comp. Numbers 33:37, 38). It has been identified with el-Tayibeh, a small fountain at the bottom of the pass leading to the ascent of Mount Hor.

places.smithEn: (bonds), (10:6) apparently the same as Moseroth, (Numbers 33:30) its plural form, the name of a place near Mount Hor.

places.description: (1) 르우벤의 손자로 고라·다단·아비람의 반역에 가담했으나 이름이 더 이상 나오지 않아 회개하고 물러난 것으로 추정된다(민 16:1). (2) 하이집트의 유명한 도시로 '헬리오폴리스'(태양의 도시)라 불렸으며(창 41:45; 겔 30:17), 요셉의 장인 보디베라가 이곳의 제사장이었다. 태양 숭배의 중심지로 오벨리스크와 신전이 있었으나 현재는 오벨리스크

places.eastonEn: light; the sun, (Genesis 41:45, 50), the great seat of sun-worship, called also Bethshemesh (Jeremiah 43:13) and Aven (Ezekiel 30:17), stood on the east bank of the Nile, a few miles north of Memphis, and near Cairo, in the north-east. The Vulgate and the LXX. Versions have “Heliopolis” (“city of the sun”) instead of On in Genesis and of Aven in Ezekiel. The “city of destruction” Isaiah speaks of (19:18, marg. “of Heres;” Hebrews ‘Ir-ha-heres, which some MSS. read Ir-ha-heres, i.e., “city of the sun”) may be the name given to On, the prophecy being that the time will come when that city which was known as the “city of the sun-God” shall become the “city of destruction” of the sun-God, i.e., when idolatry shall cease, and the worship of the true God be established. In ancient times this city was full of obelisks dedicated to the sun. Of these only one now remains standing. “Cleopatra’s Needle” was one of those which stood in this city in front of the Temple of Tum, i.e., “the sun.” It is now erected on the Thames Embankment, London. “It was at On that Joseph wooed and won the dark-skinned Asenath, the daughter of the high priest of its great temple.” This was a noted university town, and here Moses gained his acquaintance with “all the wisdom of the Egyptians.”
places.smithEn: (abode or city of the sun), a town of lower Egypt, called BETH-SHEMESH in (Jeremiah 43:13) On is better known under its Greek name Heliopolis. It was situated on the east side of the Pelusiac branch of the Nile, just below the point of the Delta, and about twenty miles northeast of Memphis. The chief object of worship at Heliopolis was the sun, whose temple, described by Strabo, is now only represented by the single beautiful obelisk, of red granite so feet 2 inches high above the pedestal which has stood for more than 4000 years, having been erected by Usirtesen, the second king of the twelfth dynasty. Heliopolis was anciently famous for its learning, and Eudoxus and Plato studied under its priests. The first mention of this place in the Bible is in the history of Joseph, to whom we read Pharaoh gave “to wife Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On.” (Genesis 41:45) comp. ver, Genesis41:60 and Genesis46:20 (On is to be remembered not only as the home of Joseph, but as the traditional place to which his far-off namesake took Mary and the babe Jesus in the flight to Egypt. The two famous obelisks, long called “Cleopatra’s Needles,” one of which now stands in London and the other in Central Park in New York city, once stood before this city, and were seen by the children of Israel before the exodus, having been quarried at Syene on the Nile, erected at On (Heliopolis) by Thothmes III., B.C. 1500, and inscriptions added by Rameses II. (Sesostris) two hundred years later. They were taken to Alexandria by Augustus Caesar A.D. 23, from which they were removed to their present places.—ED.) the son of Peleth and one of the chiefs of the tribe of Reuben, who took part with Korah, Dathan and Abiram in their revolt against Moses. (Numbers 16:1) (B.C. 1491.) His name does not again appear in the narrative of the conspiracy, nor is he alluded to when reference is made to the final catastrophe.

places.name: 브니엘
places.description: '하나님의 얼굴'이라는 뜻으로 얍복과 숙곳 사이의 곳이며, 야곱이 천사와 신비로운 씨름을 한 곳이다(창 32:24-32). 통상적이며 아마도 본래 형태는 '브누엘'이고 사마리아 오경도 이 형태다. 오백 년 후 기드온이 미디안을 쫓다가 브누엘에서 성읍과 망대를 발견하고 그 성읍 사람들을 죽였다(삿 8:17). 여로보암이 세겜에서 나와 브누엘을 건축했다(왕상
places.smithKo: '하나님의 얼굴'이라는 뜻으로 야곱이 하나님과 씨름한 곳에 붙인 이름이며 이후 본문에서는 브누엘로 표기가 바뀐다. 얍복강 북쪽, 숙곳 여울목 인근에 위치했다(창세기 32:30,31…
places.smithEn: (face of God) the name which Jacob gave to the place in which he had wrestled with God: “He called the name of the place ’face of El,’ for I have seen Elohim face to face.” (Genesis 32:30) In (Genesis 32:31) and the other passages in which the name occurs, its form is changed to Penuel. From the narrative it is evident that Peniel lay somewhere on the north bank of the Jabbok, and between that torrent and the fords of the Jordan at Succoth, a few miles north of the glen where the Jabbok falls into the Jordan.

places.smithEn: (plain), The valley of, described (Genesis 14:17) as “the valley of the king,” is mentioned again in (2 Samuel 18:18) as the site of a pillar set up by Absalom.

places.name: 시내
places.description: 하나님이 모세에게 율법을 주신 거룩한 산으로(출 19-20장), 아라비아 반도 시내 반도의 화강암 산군 안에 있다. 전통적으로 예벨 무사(해발 7,375피트)와 동일시되며, 4세기 이래 그 기슭에 성 카타리나 수도원이 세워져 있다. 산의 정확한 위치에 대해 예벨 세르발 등 다른 후보도 제시되지만 예벨 무사가 가장 유력한 견해이다.
places.eastonKo: '죄(달의 신)의 산'이라는 뜻으로 호렙이라고도 불리며, 출애굽 셋째 달에 이스라엘이 도착해 약 일 년간 머문 산악 지역이다. 이곳에서 십계명을 포함한 율법이 주어졌으며 라스 사사…
places.eastonEn: of Sin (the moon God), called also Horeb, the name of the mountain district which was reached by the Hebrews in the third month after the Exodus. Here they remained encamped for about a whole year. Their journey from the Red Sea to this encampment, including all the windings of the route, was about 150 miles. The last twenty-two chapters of Exodus, together with the whole of Leviticus and Numbers ch. 1-11, contain a record of all the transactions which occurred while they were here. From Rephidim (Exodus 17:8-13) the Israelites journeyed forward through the Wady Solaf and Wady esh-Sheikh into the plain of er-Rahah, “the desert of Sinai,” about 2 miles long and half a mile broad, and encamped there “before the mountain.” The part of the mountain range, a protruding lower bluff, known as the Ras Sasafeh (Sufsafeh), rises almost perpendicularly from this plain, and is in all probability the Sinai of history. Dean Stanley thus describes the scene:, “The plain itself is not broken and uneven and narrowly shut in, like almost all others in the range, but presents a long retiring sweep, within which the people could remove and stand afar off. The cliff, rising like a huge altar in front of the whole congregation, and visible against the sky in lonely grandeur from end to end of the whole plain, is the very image of the ‘mount that might be touched,’ and from which the voice of God might be heard far and wide over the plain below.” This was the scene of the giving of the law. From the Ras Sufsafeh the law was proclaimed to the people encamped below in the plain of er-Rahah. During the lengthened period of their encampment here the Israelites passed through a very memorable experience. An immense change passed over them. They are now an organized nation, bound by covenant engagement to serve the Lord their God, their ever-present divine Leader and Protector. At length, in the second month of the second year of the Exodus, they move their camp and march forward according to a prescribed order. After three days they reach the “wilderness of Paran,” the “et-Tih”, i.e., “the desert”, and here they make their first encampment. At this time a spirit of discontent broke out amongst them, and the Lord manifested his displeasure by a fire which fell on the encampment and inflicted injury on them. Moses called the place Taberah (q.v.), Numbers  11:1-3. The journey between Sinai and the southern boundary of the Promised Land (about 150 miles) at Kadesh was accomplished in about a year. (See MAP facing page 204.)

places.name: 닥딤홋시
places.description: '새로 거주한 땅'이라는 뜻으로(사무엘하 24:6) 오론테스 강변 헷 사람의 수도 가데스 인근으로 추정된다.
places.eastonKo: '새로 거주한 땅'이라는 뜻으로(사무엘하 24:6) 오론테스 강변 헷 사람의 수도 가데스 인근으로 추정된다.
places.eastonEn: the land of the newly inhabited, (2 Samuel 24:6). It is conjectured that, instead of this word, the reading should be, “the Hittites of Kadesh,” the Hittite capital, on the Orontes. It was apparently some region east of the Jordan and north of Gilead.
places.smithEn: (lowlands of Hodshi?), The land of, one of the places visited by Joab during his census of the land of Israel. It occurs between Gilead and Dan-jaan. (2 Samuel 24:6) The name has puzzled all the interpreters, (Kitto says it was probably a section of the upper valley of the Jordan, now called Ard el-Huleh, lying deep down at the western base of Hermon.—ED.)
places.smithKo: '홋시의 저지대(?)'라는 뜻으로 요압이 이스라엘 인구조사 중 방문한 장소 중 하나이며 길르앗과 단야안 사이에 언급된다(사무엘하 24:6). 정확한 위치는 해석자들을 곤혹스럽게 해왔다.

places.name: 돌랏
places.description: '풍요로운'이라는 뜻으로 유다 남쪽 시므온 지파의 한 성읍이다(역대상 4:29).
places.eastonKo: '풍요로운'이라는 뜻으로 유다 남쪽 시므온 지파의 한 성읍이다(역대상 4:29).
places.smithKo: 시므온의 성읍 중 하나로(역대상 4:29) 다른 곳에서는 엘돌랏이라 불린다.
places.eastonEn: productive, a town of Simeon, in the south of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:29).
places.smithEn: one of the towns of Simeon, (1 Chronicles 4:29) elsewhere called El-tolad.

places.name: 갈대아
places.description: 유브라데 강 양편에 자리했던 고대의 나라로 페르시아 만에 접해 있었다. 면적은 약 23,000평방마일로 추산되며, 후대에는 더 넓은 뜻으로 길이 450마일, 너비 100~130마일에 이르는 지역을 포함했다. 메소포타미아 대평원의 남쪽, 가장 비옥한 지역을 차지했고 수많은 운하로 더욱 생산성이 높았다. 후대에 '갈대아 사람의 땅'은 바벨로니아 전체와 갈대아인

places.name: 글라우다
places.description: 그레데 남쪽 지중해의 작은 섬으로 길이 7마일, 너비 3마일이다(행 27:16).
places.eastonKo: 바울이 로마로 항해하는 도중 지나친 크레타 남서쪽의 작은 섬(행 27:16).
places.smithKo: '절름발이'라는 뜻으로(사도행전 27:16) 그레데 남쪽 해안 마탈라곶 서쪽에 위치한 작은 섬이며 오늘날 고초라 불린다.
places.eastonEn: a small island off the southwest coast of Crete, passed by Paul on his voyage to Rome (Acts 27:16). It is about 7 miles long and 3 broad. It is now called Gozzo (R.V., “Cauda”).
places.smithEn: (lame), (Acts 27:16) a small island nearly due west of Cape Matala on the south coast of Crete, and nearly due south of Phoenice; now Gozzo .

places.name: 아브로나
places.description: 이스라엘 백성이 광야에서 머물렀던 진지 중 하나(민수기 33:34,35), 에시온게벨 바로 앞에 위치했다. 흠정역(A.V.)에서는 '에브로나'로 표기된다.
places.eastonKo: 이스라엘 백성이 광야에서 머물렀던 진지 중 하나(민수기 33:34,35), 에시온게벨 바로 앞에 위치했다. 흠정역(A.V.)에서는 '에브로나'로 표기된다.
places.eastonEn: one of Israel’s halting-places in the desert (Numbers 33:34,35), just before Ezion-gaber. In A.V., “Ebronah.”

places.name: 압살롬의 기념비
places.description: 압살롬의 기념비. 기드론 골짜기 곧 '왕의 골짜기'에 있었다(삼하 18:18). 지금 예루살렘 동편 감람산 기슭에 서 있는 '압살롬의 무덤'을 유대인들은 그가 세운 것으로 여긴다.

places.name: 악고
places.description: '뜨거운 모래'라는 뜻. 갈멜 산 북쪽 약 8마일에 있던 베니게의 항구 도시로, 아셀 지파에게 주어졌다(삿 1:31). 신약 시대에는 돌레마이라 불렸다(행 21:7). 지금은 아크레라 한다.
places.eastonKo: "무더운 또는 모래의," 아셀 지파에 속했으나 결코 그들에게 정복되지 않은 페니키아의 항구 도시(삿 1:31).
places.smithKo: 마카베오서와 신약의 '돌레마이'로, 오늘날 아카 또는 유럽인들이 부르는 생장다크르라 불리며 두로 남쪽 약 30마일의 시리아 해안 최대 항구 도시였다. 신약에는 사도행전 21:7에서…
places.eastonEn: sultry or sandy, a town and harbour of Phoenicia, in the tribe of Asher, but never acquired by them (Judges 1:31). It was known to the ancient Greeks and Romans by the name of Ptolemais, from Ptolemy the king of Egypt, who rebuilt it about B.C. 100. Here Paul landed on his last journey to Jerusalem (Acts 21:7). During the crusades of the Middle Ages it was called Acra; and subsequently, on account of its being occupied by the Knights Hospitallers of Jerusalem, it was called St. Jean d’Acre, or simply Acre.
places.smithEn: (the Ptolemaisof the Maccabees and New Testament), Now called Acca, or more usually by Europeans St. Jean d’Acre, the most important seaport town on the Syrian coast, about 30 miles south of Tyre. It was situated on a slightly projecting headland, at the northern extremity of that spacious bay which is formed by the bold promontory of Carmel on the opposite side. Later it was named Ptolemais, after one of the Ptolemies, probably Soter. The only notice of it in the New Testament is in (Acts 21:7) where it is called Ptolemais .

places.name: 아겔다마
places.description: '피밭'이라는 뜻. 유다가 그리스도를 판 돈으로 산 '토기장이의 밭'이다(마 27:7; 행 1:18-19). 전승에 따르면 힌놈 골짜기 남쪽 비탈, 실로암 못 근처로 본다.
places.eastonKo: 우리 주를 배반한 자에게 주었던 돈으로 산 밭에 유대인들이 자기 나라 말, 곧 아람어로 붙인 이름. 이 말은 "피밭"을 뜻한다.
places.smithKo: '피의 밭'이라는 뜻으로(개정역에는 아겔다마) 유다가 그리스도를 배반하고 받은 돈으로 산 예루살렘 근처의 밭이며 그의 처참한 죽음으로 인해 이 이름이 붙었다(사도행전 1:19). …
places.eastonEn: the name which the Jews gave in their proper tongue, i.e., in Aramaic, to the field which was purchased with the money which had been given to the betrayer of our Lord. The word means “field of blood.” It was previously called “the potter’s field” (Matthew 27:7, 8; Acts 1:19), and was appropriated as the burial-place for strangers. It lies on a narrow level terrace on the south face of the valley of Hinnom. Its modern name is Hak ed-damm.
places.smithEn: (the field of blood) (Akeldama in the Revised Version), the name given by the Jews of Jerusalem to a field near Jerusalem purchased by Judas with the money which he received for the betrayal of Christ, and so called from his violent death therein. (Acts 1:19) The “field of blood” is now shown on the steep southern face of the valley or ravine of Hinnom, “southwest of the supposed pool of Siloam.”

places.name: 아담
places.description: 수 3:16에 언급됨. "사르단 곁," 요단 서쪽 강둑에 있었다(왕상 4:12).
places.eastonKo: 수 3:16에 언급됨. "사르단 곁," 요단 서쪽 강둑에 있었다(왕상 4:12).
places.eastonEn: is referred to in Joshua 3:16. It stood “beside Zarethan,” on the west bank of Jordan (1 Kings 4:12). At this city the flow of the water was arrested and rose up “upon an heap” at the time of the Israelites’ passing over (Joshua 3:16).

places.name: 아마겟돈
places.description: '므깃도 산'이라는 뜻. 요한계시록 16:16에 상징적으로 쓰인 이름으로, 구약의 큰 싸움터였으며 지금은 에스드라엘론 평야로 알려진 곳에서 유래하였다.

places.name: 아르바
places.description: 헤브론과 기럇아르바 참조(창 35:27).
places.smithKo: 헤브론 또는 기럇아르바를 가리키며 다른 곳에서는 항상 '아르바 성읍'으로 번역된다(창세기 35:27).
places.eastonEn: four, a giant, father of Anak. From him the city of Hebron derived its name of Kirjath-arba, i.e., the city of Araba (Joshua 14:15; 15:13; 21:11; Genesis 13:18; 23:2). (See HEBRON.)
places.eastonKo: '넷'이라는 뜻으로, 거인이며 아낙의 아버지. 그에게서 헤브론이 '기럇아르바', 곧 '아르바의 성읍'이라는 이름을 얻었다(여호수아 14:15; 15:13; 21:11; 창세기 13:18; 23:2).
places.smithEn: Hebron, or Kirjath-Arba, as “the city of Arbah” is always rendered elsewhere. (Genesis 35:27)

places.name: 아스다롯
places.description: 1) 요단 동편 바산의 성읍으로 베에스드라와 동일하다(신 1:4, 수 21:27). 2) 시돈 사람들의 여신으로 불린 우상으로, 시리아와 베니게에서 널리 숭배되었다. 솔로몬이 이 숭배를 들여왔고(왕상 11:33), 헬라·로마인들은 아스타르테라 불렀다. '하늘의 여왕'이라 불리며 흔히 바알과 함께 언급된다. 요시야가 이 숭배를 척결했다.

places.name: 앗수르
places.smithKo: 앗수르(ASSYRIA) 항목 참조(에스라 4:2; 시편 83:8).
places.eastonEn: second son of Shem (Genesis 10:22; 1 Chronicles 1:17). He went from the land of Shinar and built Nineveh, etc. (Genesis 10:11,12). He probably gave his name to Assyria, which is the usual translation of the word, although the form Asshur is sometimes retained (Numbers 24:22, 24; Ezekiel 27:23, etc.). In Genesis 2:14 “Assyria” ought to be “Asshur,” which was the original capital of Assyria, a city represented by the mounds of Kalah Sherghat, on the west bank of the Tigris. This city was founded by Bel-kap-kapu about B.C. 1700. At a later date the capital was shifted to Ninua, or Nineveh, now Koyunjik, on the eastern bank of the river. (See CALAH; NINEVEH.)
places.eastonKo: 셈의 둘째 아들(창세기 10:22; 역대상 1:17). 그는 시날 땅을 떠나 니느웨 등을 세웠다(창세기 10:11,12). 그는 아마도 자기 이름을 앗수르(앗시리아)에게 주었을 것이다.
places.smithEn: (Ezra 4:2; Psalms 83:8) [Asshur, Assyria, Asshur; ASSYRIA]

places.name: 아스다롯
places.description: 아스다롯 참조.
places.smithKo: 아스다롯(ASHTAROTH) 항목 참조.
places.eastonEn: a city of Bashan, in the kingdom of Og (Deuteronomy 1:4; Joshua 12:4; 13:12; 9:10). It was in the half-tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 13:12), and as a Levitical city was given to the Gershonites (1 Chronicles 6:71). Uzzia, one of David’s valiant men (1 Chronicles 11:44), is named as of this city. It is identified with Tell Ashterah, in the Hauran, and is noticed on monuments B.C. 1700-1500. The name Beesh-terah (Joshua 21:27) is a contraction for Beth-eshterah, i.e., “the house of Ashtaroth.”
places.eastonKo: 옥의 왕국, 바산의 성읍(신명기 1:4; 여호수아 12:4; 13:12; 9:10). 므낫세 반 지파에 속했으며(여호수아 13:12) 레위인의 성읍으로 게르손 자손에게 주어졌다(역대상 6:71). 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람 웃시야(역대상 11:44)가 이 성읍 출신으로 언급된다.
places.smithEn: (1:4) [Ashtaroth]

places.name: 아소도
places.description: 아스돗의 헬라어 형태(행 8:40). 아스돗 참조.
places.eastonKo: 아스돗(참조)의 그리스화된 형태(사도행전 8:40 등).
places.smithKo: 아스돗(ASHDOD) 항목 참조.
places.eastonEn: the Grecized form (Acts 8:40, etc.) of Ashdod (q.v.).
places.smithEn: [Ashdod, Or Azotus]

places.name: 앗사
places.description: 가사와 동일한 이름(신 2:23, 왕상 4:24, 렘 25:20). 가사 참조.
places.smithKo: '강한'이라는 뜻으로 블레셋의 유명한 성읍 가사를 더 정확히 표기한 이름이다(신명기 2:23).
places.smithEn: (the strong). The more accurate rendering of the name of the well-known Philistine city Gaza. (2:23; 1 Kings 4:24; Jeremiah 25:20)

places.name: 바벨탑
places.description: 성경에 단 한 번, 미완성 상태로 언급되는 탑으로(창 11:4), 시날 평지에 역청을 모르타르 삼아 구운 벽돌로 지어졌다. 포로 시절 유대인들은 이를 벨 신전과 동일시했으며, 오늘날 학자들은 바벨론 남서쪽의 비르스 니므룟 유적을 그 터로 추정하기도 한다.
places.eastonKo: 홍수 이후 시날 땅에 세워진 탑(창 11:1-9)으로, 백성이 흩어지지 않도록 하기 위한 집결지로 의도되었다. 하나님이 그들의 언어를 혼잡하게 하셨으므로 '혼란'이라는 뜻이 되었다…
places.eastonEn: the name given to the tower which the primitive fathers of our race built in the land of Shinar after the Deluge (Genesis 11:1-9). Their object in building this tower was probably that it might be seen as a rallying-point in the extensive plain of Shinar, to which they had emigrated from the uplands of Armenia, and so prevent their being scattered abroad. But God interposed and defeated their design by condounding their language, and hence the name Babel, meaning “confusion.” In the Babylonian tablets there is an account of this event, and also of the creation and the deluge. (See CHALDEA.) The Temple of Belus, which is supposed to occupy its site, is described by the Greek historian Herodotus as a temple of great extent and magnificence, erected by the Babylonians for their God Belus. The treasures Nebuchadnezzar brought from Jerusalem were laid up in this temple (2 Chronicles 36:7). The Birs Nimrud, at ancient Borsippa, about 7 miles south-west of Hillah, the modern town which occupies a part of the site of ancient Babylon, and 6 miles from the Euphrates, is an immense mass of broken and fire-blasted fragments, of about 2,300 feet in circumference, rising suddenly to the height of 235 feet above the desert-plain, and is with probability regarded as the ruins of the tower of Babel. This is “one of the most imposing ruins in the country.” Others think it to be the ruins of the Temple of Belus.

places.name: 바벨론 왕국
places.description: '갈대아 사람들의 땅'. 티그리스강 유역을 따라 펼쳐진 광대한 지역으로 비옥함과 부유함으로 유명했으며 그 수도가 바벨론이었다.
places.eastonKo: '갈대아 사람들의 땅'. 티그리스강 유역을 따라 펼쳐진 광대한 지역으로 비옥함과 부유함으로 유명했으며 그 수도가 바벨론이었다.
places.eastonEn: called “the land of the Chaldeans” (Jeremiah 24:5; Ezek, 12:13), was an extensive province in Central Asia along the valley of the Tigris from the Persian Gulf northward for some 300 miles. It was famed for its fertility and its riches. Its capital was the city of Babylon, a great commercial centre (Ezekiel 17:4; Isaiah 43:14). Babylonia was divided into the two districts of Accad in the north, and Summer (probably the Shinar of the Old Testament) in the south. Among its chief cities may be mentioned Ur (now Mugheir or Mugayyar), on the western bank of the Euphrates; Uruk, or Erech (Genesis 10:10) (now Warka), between Ur and Babylon; Larsa (now Senkereh), the Ellasar of Genesis 14:1, a little to the east of Erech; Nipur (now Niffer), south-east of Babylon; Sepharvaim (2 Kings 17:24), “the two Sipparas” (now Abu-Habba), considerably to the north of Babylon; and Eridu, “the good city” (now Abu-Shahrein), which lay originally on the shore of the Persian Gulf, but is now, owing to the silting up of the sand, about 100 miles distant from it. Another city was Kulunu, or Calneh (Genesis 10:10). The salt-marshes at the mouths of the Euphrates and Tigris were called Marratu, “the bitter” or “salt”, the Merathaim of Jeremiah 50:21. They were the original home of the Kalda, or Chaldeans. The most famous of the early kings of Babylonia were Sargon of Accad (B.C.3800) and his son, Naram-Sin, who conquered a large part of Western Asia, establishing their power in Palestine, and even carrying their arms to the Sinaitic peninsula. A great Babylonian library was founded in the reign  of Sargon. Babylonia was subsequently again broken up into more than one state, and at one time fell under the domination of Elam. This was put an end to by Khammu-rabi (Amraphel), who drove the Elamites out of the country, and overcame Arioch, the son of an Elamite prince. From this time forward Babylonia was a united monarchy. About B.C. 1750 it was conquered by the Kassi, or Kosseans, from the mountains of Elam, and a Kassite dynasty ruled over it for 576 years and 9 months. In the time of Khammu-rabi, Syria and Palestine were subject to Babylonia and its Elamite suzerain; and after the overthrow of the Elamite supremacy, the Babylonian kings continued to exercise their influence and power in what was called “the land of the Amorites.” In the epoch of the Kassite dynasty, however, Canaan passed into the hands of Egypt. In B.C. 729, Babylonia was conquered by the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser III.; but on the death of Shalmaneser IV. it was seized by the Kalda or “Chaldean” prince Merodach-baladan (2 Kings 20:12-19), who held it till B.C. 709, when he was driven out by Sargon. Under Sennacherib, Babylonia revolted from Assyria several times, with the help of the Elamites, and after one of these revolts Babylon was destroyed by Sennacherib, B.C. 689. It was rebuilt by Esarhaddon, who made it his residence during part of the year, and it was to Babylon that Manasseh was brought a prisoner (2 Chronicles 33:11). After the death of Esarhaddon, Saul-sumyukin, the viceroy of Babylonia, revolted against his brother the Assyrian king, and the revolt was suppressed with difficulty. When Nineveh was destroyed, B.C. 606, Nabopolassar, the viceroy of Babylonia, who seems to have been of Chaldean descent, made himself independent. His son Nebuchadrezzar (Nabu-kudur-uzur), after defeating the Egyptians at Carchemish, succeeded him as king, B.C. 604, and founded the Babylonian empire. He strongly fortified Babylon, and adorned it with palaces and other buildings. His son, Evil-merodach, who succeeded him in B.C. 561, was murdered after a reign of two years. The last monarch of the Babylonian empire was Nabonidus (Nabu-nahid), B.C. 555-538, whose eldest son, Belshazzar (Bilu-sar-uzur), is mentioned in several inscriptions. Babylon was captured by Cyrus, B.C. 538, and though it revolted more than once in later years, it never succeeded in maintaining its independence.

places.smithEn: is mentioned only in the first two Gospels, (Matthew 16:13; Mark 8:27) and in accounts of the same transactions. It was at the easternmost and most important of the two recognized sources of the Jordan, the other being at Tel-el-Kadi . The spring rises from and the city was built on a limestone terrace in a valley at the base of Mount Hermon 20 miles north of the Sea of Galilee. It was enlarged by Herod Philip, and named after Caesar, with his own name added to distinguish it from Caesarea. Its present name is Banias, a village of some 50 houses, with many interesting ruins. Caesarea Philippi has no Old Testament history, though it has been not unreasonably identified with Baal-gad . It was visited by Christ shortly before his transfiguration, (Matthew 16:13-28) and was the northern limit of his journeys. (Mark 8:27)

places.eastonEn: fortress of Chemosh, a city on the west bank of the Euphrates (Jeremiah 46:2; 2 Chronicles 35:20), not, as was once supposed, the Circesium at the confluence of the Chebar and the Euphrates, but a city considerably higher up the river, and commanding the ordinary passage of the Euphrates; probably identical with Hierapolis. It was the capital of the kingdom of the northern Hittites. The Babylonian army, under Nebuchadnezzar, the son of Nabopolassar, here met and conquered the army of Pharaoh-necho, king of Egypt (B.C. 607). It is mentioned in monuments in B.C. 1600 and down to B.C. 717.
